## ADR-608: Airwaves — recording content block, polymorphic assignability, and the Space library (P1)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13) · P1 of `docs/MEDIA-PLATFORM-PLAN.md` · builds on the P0 spine (`recordings` / `podcast_shows` / `recording_attachments` tables + the A/V-widened Loom, `lib/airwaves/*`, the presentational player `components/airwaves/player/*`) · member-facing names (Airwaves / Recording / Show) stay PROPOSED pending a NAMING.md lock · NO new migration.

**Context.** P0 landed the schema, widened the Loom to audio/video, and shipped a self-contained player. P1 had to make Recordings usable: drop one into any page, attach one to any host (Practice / Journey / Event / Product / Space), and give an owner a place to upload and manage them. The constraints were the house canons: extend the entity-block registry additively (not a new editor), derive any menu row from `SPACE_MODULES` (MENU-CONTRACT / ADR-553), keep money OFF (`payoutsLive()`), and never leak a walled Recording's file.

**Decision.**
1. **A `recording` entity-block** (additive registry row in `lib/entity-blocks/registry.ts` + fields in `block-content.ts`, web-only like `embed`). A new `recordingPicker` field type (single-select over the Space's Recordings, sanitized to one bounded id) picks the Recording; `display` / `autoplay` / `showTranscript` tune it. The server renderer (`content-block-view`) mounts a thin CLIENT island (`RecordingBlockEmbed`) that hydrates through a GATED resolve route, so a private Recording renders a locked card and the media src never reaches an un-entitled viewer.
2. **A gated playback resolver** (`lib/airwaves/playback.ts` → `GET /api/airwaves/recordings/[id]`): composes the Recording row + the Loom file url + the viewer's Space membership + the pure `canViewRecording` floor into a `PlayerRecording` payload, or a `locked` / `missing` wall. Free only (P1); the Price/entitlement layers are not charged.
3. **Polymorphic assignability** (`lib/airwaves/attach-actions.ts` + `RecordingAttachManager` + `AttachedRecordingsSection`): a reusable "pick a Recording" manager writes `recording_attachments` through the gated `attachRecording`/`detachRecording` seam (host_kind + host_id), and a self-fetching read section renders a host's attached Recordings (each through the gated player). Wired end-to-end on the Space host (the console) and the Product host (the shop item editor + the market product page); the manager is a one-line drop-in for the remaining hosts.
4. **A Space library console** (`/spaces/[slug]/settings/airwaves`) from ONE new `SPACE_MODULES` row (`space.airwaves`) + a new `airwaves` `SpaceFunctionKey` (default-ON, editor role). The owner uploads a file (through the widened `uploadToLoom` → `recordings-media`), creates the Recording, previews the player, sets visibility, and attaches to the Space; a plain member gets a browse-only view.

**Alternatives.** Threading the picker's Recording list through the block-editor's `pickerData` seed (rejected: it would make the content block function-backed and subject it to the palette "exists" gate, and would require editing the settings-rail seed getter — the client-side fetch by URL slug is self-contained and additive). Resolving the block's gate inside the sync `ContentBlockView` (rejected: it has no viewer context; the client island + gated route keeps the renderer presentational and the gate server-side). Reusing an existing gate key instead of a new `airwaves` function (rejected: the MENU-CONTRACT tests require a covering module per key and `featureKey === gate.fn`; a dedicated key is the honest, toggleable model).

**Consequences.** Additive only: NO new migration (P0's three tables + bucket cover P1), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `pnpm check:menu` + `check:rls` green, the entity-block + menu drift suites green plus a new `recording-block.test.ts`. Shared-file touches are all additive (one registry row, one field type + sanitize case, one renderer case, one `SPACE_MODULES` row, one `SpaceFunctionKey`, one `surface-hrefs` case, one dispatch branch in `block-edit-panel`). The player depth (speed/MediaSession already in P0), ratings, discussion, the Loom manager (P2), the public Show page + RSS (P3), and paid/private feeds (P4) remain to build. Names stay PROPOSED until the Vision Steward locks them in NAMING.md.
## ADR-609: Unified Messaging console — one home for Campaigns + Funnels, a visual funnel flow, and a guided front door

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-13) · P1 + P3 (manual) + P4 of `docs/EMAIL-CAMPAIGNS-FUNNELS-PLAN.md` · builds on the campaigns read (`lib/studio/campaigns.ts`), the funnel object (`lib/funnels/*`, ADR-455), the campaign analytics (`lib/email-studio/analytics.ts`), and the native drag-reorder idiom (`components/spaces/crm/stage-editor.tsx`, ADR-517) · Vera generation (P5) is a documented, deferred seam · NO migration.

**Context.** The two things an operator actually creates — a Campaign (one email, sent now or scheduled) and a Funnel (a triggered journey) — were scattered across `/admin/marketing/campaigns`, `/admin/growth/funnels`, the Beta Command Center's Campaign tab, and the email studio, with no single home, no shared status legend, and no guided way to start. The funnel object had a stage builder but no visual flow, and no drag-reorder for its stages. The plan asked for one console, a visual editable flow, and a best-practice guided setup that offers "Let Vera draft it" or "Build it manually."

**Decision.**
1. **One Messaging console** (`/admin/marketing/messaging`, `lib/messaging/console.ts` + `components/admin/messaging/messaging-console.tsx`) lists Campaigns and Funnels side by side under a shared status legend, KPI counts, and quick actions. Both objects normalize onto ONE status vocabulary (`lib/messaging/status.ts`: draft/scheduled/live/paused/sent/archived/failed) rendered on the ✅/⏳/⚠️/🔴 presentation legend via the shared `StatusChip`. It is the LISTING layer over the working editors, not a rebuild: every row links out to the existing composer / flow view. The console leads the Marketing nav section (a `marketing-messaging` StudioLeaf) and the Growth manage grid.
2. **A visual funnel flow view** (`/admin/marketing/messaging/funnels/[id]`, `components/admin/messaging/funnel-flow.tsx`) draws a funnel as a clean vertical flow: a Trigger banner, the stages as minimal draggable nodes (icon + label + one status line), and a Goal banner. Reorder is the native HTML5 DnD idiom lifted from the CRM stage editor (no new library) + keyboard arrows, persisted by the one net-new mutation `reorderFunnelStages` (a two-pass position rewrite that clears the unique `(funnel_id, position)` index). A node's settings (rename, wire links, remove links) open in a SIDE PANEL, never on the node (the plan's research rule). Branches ("Add a split") are a present-but-off, honestly-labeled seam (they need the automation condition grammar + a new stage kind).
3. **A guided front door** (`/admin/marketing/messaging/new`, `lib/messaging/goals.ts` + `guided-client.tsx`): a three-screen flow (goal -> a few questions -> how to build) seeded from a best-practice goal catalog (welcome/nurture/re-engage funnels with 3-6 step outlines; promo/announce campaigns), with inline best-practice tips. "Build it manually" is fully wired (funnel goals create a funnel via the existing `createFunnel` and land in the flow view; campaign goals open the composer with the audience preset). "Let Vera draft it" builds the same scaffold today and flags that Vera drafting is on the way.

**Alternatives.** Overloading the `funnels` object with email-journey semantics / a new `wait`/`branch` stage kind (rejected for this slice: it needs a migration + the condition engine; the four canonical kinds render as a clean linear flow now, and email cadence stays in the drip runner). Re-homing the working editors under the console (rejected: the plan is explicit — unify the LISTING over them, do not delete them). Wiring a real Vera generation tool now (deferred to P5: the bounded Vera tool catalog has no campaign/sequence generator yet; the seam is one branch in `startBuild`). A URL-segment tab strip for the console's two lists (rejected: client tab state is enough and keeps one route + one server fetch).

**Consequences.** Additive only: NO migration, `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint clean on changed files, `pnpm check:menu` green, `pnpm build` green (only the local Supabase page-data error). New pure logic is unit-tested (`lib/messaging/status.test.ts`, `lib/messaging/goals.test.ts`). Shared-file edits: one `marketing-messaging` row in `lib/nav/studio.ts`, a `Send` icon added to the `app/(main)/admin/sections.ts` icon map, and a Messaging card in `components/widgets/growth/manage.tsx`. The reorder action + flow view reuse the existing funnel reads/mutations; the growth builder (`/admin/growth/funnels/[id]`) stays the advanced surface. Vera generation (P5) and persisted per-step timing/branches (deeper P4) are the documented follow-ups.

## ADR-610: CRM Phase 1 — complete the contact-card timeline (`in_app` channel + DM adapter, manual log, system/human toggle, per-contact engagement stats)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 1 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` + Move 1/2 of `docs/CRM-INTERACTION-TRACKING-PLAN.md` · builds on the `contact_interactions` timeline (ADR-372) and the `engagement_events` backbone · migration `20261158000000_crm_timeline_inapp_engagement.sql` · `lib/crm/*`.

**Context.** The contact card's promise is a complete, trustworthy history, but the one channel that makes it feel complete — in-house messages — had no adapter, `contact_interactions.channel` had no `in_app` value, there was no way to log a touch by hand, and the row's `source` field (`manual`/`engagement`/`system`/…) had no UI switch to hide automated noise. `contacts.engagement_score` was a dark scalar with no per-contact sent/opened/replied rollup.

**Decision.**
1. **Widen the vocabulary, never fork the log.** One small migration adds `in_app` to the `channel` CHECK; a **DM adapter** fires a fire-safe, idempotent (keyed on message id) `recordContactInteraction({ channel: 'in_app' })` on DM/room send. A **manual "log a touch"** affordance writes `contact_interactions` natively (`source: 'manual'`), superseding the read-time `crm_activities` fold over time.
2. **The system/human toggle filters, never deletes.** A persistent "show automated events" switch on every timeline narrows on `source` (`engagement`/`system` hidden, human/manual shown). Default: automated hidden on the member's personal card, shown in the staff console — the owner's "focus on email and text" control as one boolean over a field we already store.
3. **Denormalized read model off the immutable log.** A `contact_engagement_stats` rollup (sent/opened/clicked/replied, last-touch, recency) refreshed on the nightly cron beside `refresh-traits`, and the documented `engagement_score` projection is finally wired.

**Consequences.** Additive + RLS-consistent (owner/Space read, service-role write). Reversibility/guardrail: the log stays append-only and the toggle is a read-time filter, so no touch is ever destroyed and the toggle is fully reversible; every adapter is fail-safe (a capture can never break a message send). `contact_interactions` remains a projection, not a parallel log, keeping COMMS-CRM-ARCHITECTURE §1's "one backbone, many subscribers" intact. Inbound-email capture (Adapter B) remains the documented follow-up.

## ADR-611: CRM Phase 2 — staged CSV contact import (parse → map → validate → preview → commit) + custom-field registry

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 2 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` · builds on the business-importer staging+status pattern (`lib/importer/intake.ts`) and the `coerceExtraction` AI-structured-then-validated doctrine · migration `20261159000000_contact_import.sql` · `lib/crm/import/*`, member surface `/connections/import`, admin surface `/admin/marketing/import`.

**Context.** There was no CSV contact import. Operators and members could only add contacts by scan, Google import, or by hand. Best practice is a staged pipeline with layered auto-map and a human-approved AI fallback, not a one-shot upload that rejects the whole file on a bad row.

**Decision.**
1. **A `contact_import` staging row** (jsonb, mirrors `business_intake`) drives a guarded status machine `uploaded → mapping → preview → committed` (+ recoverable `failed`); `canTransition` is pure and prevents a stale job marching a row backward.
2. **Smart auto-map** (`map.ts`: header-normalize → synonym dict → fuzzy → value/type inference → confidence gate) constrained to a **closed `TARGET_FIELDS` enum**; anything else becomes a **custom field** in a per-owner/Space registry. **AI-assist** (`ai.ts`) samples rows only, is constrained to the schema (never invents a field), and a human approves.
3. **Row-level partial import** never rejects the file: bad rows are flagged and counted, valid rows still commit. **Dedupe** on normalized email → last-10 phone with skip/overwrite/fill-empty and a dry-run diff. **Scoped target** honours the membrane (Law 2): member → `network_contacts`; Space → sealed `contacts(space_id)`, never both.

**Consequences.** Additive + RLS-scoped. Reversibility/guardrail: commit is an idempotent upsert previewed by a dry-run diff, so a bad mapping is caught before any write and re-runs create no duplicates; the AI path is advisory (constrained to the schema, human-approved), never authoritative. `contact_import` is not in `database.types` yet (ADR-246): the persistence layer uses the untyped-admin idiom; regenerate after apply.

## ADR-612: CRM Phase 3 — QR lead-grabs: capture-now-claim-on-join + the immutable entry point

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 3 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` · builds on `/q/<slug>` codes (ADR-091), `captureQrContact`, and the attribution layer · migration `20261160000000_lead_entry_points.sql` · `lib/crm/lead-capture.ts`, `lib/connections/qr-capture.ts`.

**Context.** QR codes captured connections but not Space leads, and there was no immutable first-touch record of the door someone came through, nor a redemption path linking a captured lead to the profile they later create. The owner asked for a Space CRM leads surface fed by scans, without breaking the privacy membrane.

**Decision.**
1. **One engine behind five front doors** (`space_qr`, `warm_intro`, `event`, `lead_magnet`, `share_back`), with the Space QR lead-grab built full and the other four as engine hooks.
2. **Capture writes a sealed Space lead** (`contacts.space_id` set, `profile_id` null, `consent_state='unknown'`) plus an **immutable entry point** (`lead_entry_points`, one per contact, `unique(contact_id)` + a DB trigger — set once, never overwritten) and an append-only touchpoint log. **Join is the only bridge:** on signup the email match links the sealed lead to the new profile (never copies the overlay), logs a `claim`, and retro-attributes, surfacing them in the Space CRM with the original door intact.
3. **Capture ≠ marketing consent.** A sealed lead stays `unknown`; only a consent-native door, an unlocked offer, or an accepted warm intro flips it to mailable, and only from `unknown` — an `unsubscribed` lead is never re-subscribed (`consentStateForDoor`).

**Consequences.** Additive + Space-sealed. Reversibility/guardrail: the entry point's immutability is DB-enforced (unique + trigger), so first-touch attribution can never be silently rewritten; consent never transfers upward or sideways (the three membrane laws hold); every IO path is fail-safe so a capture can never break a scan or a signup. Tables are untyped (ADR-246) until regen.

## ADR-613: CRM Phase 4 — data-bound `productCard` email block + search-by-owner picker; transactional-template seam deferred at the client boundary

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 4 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` + Move 3 of `docs/CRM-INTERACTION-TRACKING-PLAN.md` · builds on the Email Studio block registry + renderer and the unused commerce queries · NO migration · `lib/email-studio/*`, `lib/entity-blocks/*`.

**Context.** Products/offerings could not be put in an email — the `offerings` block was excluded from the palette and dropped at render — and there was no search-by-owner picker. The plan also wanted transactional/system email migrated onto the editable block-tree, but `lib/email.ts` is transitively pulled into a client bundle.

**Decision.**
1. **A data-bound `productCard` block** (`kinds: ['email']`, added to the registry + `render.ts`) carries a product *reference* and resolves image/title/price/CTA from the live catalog **at send time** (`lib/email-studio/product-block.ts`, a `server-only` path), so the card never goes stale. A **search-by-owner picker** lists a person's or Space's products via the existing-but-unused commerce queries, plus product **merge variables** with fallbacks.
2. **The transactional-template seam is deferred on purpose, for a client-boundary reason.** `lib/email.ts` is transitively imported into the client graph (automations → engagement → practices → journey-settings), so it must **not** reach the `server-only` product-block module — even a dynamic import taints the Turbopack client graph and fails the build. Making a transactional email editable is done by resolving the template in the **server-side caller** and passing rendered subject/html/text in, never by importing product-block from `email.ts`.

**Consequences.** Additive, no migration; the `productCard` picker + send-time binding are unaffected by the deferral (they live on the server path). Reversibility/guardrail: the client/server boundary is the load-bearing invariant — `email.ts` stays free of any `server-only` reach, enforced by the build itself; the deferred transactional-editable work is tracked in `docs/EMAIL-EDITOR-PLAN.md`. The marketing/transactional subdomain split (GE6-5) remains separately deferred.

## ADR-614: CRM Phase 5 — unified segment audience (place-tree ∪ trait/contact) + messaging control panel + broadcast recipient log

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 5 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` + Move 4/5 of `docs/CRM-INTERACTION-TRACKING-PLAN.md` · builds on the audience resolver, `resolveSegment`, and the four existing ledgers · migration `20261162000000_dispatch_recipients.sql` · `lib/spaces/audiences.ts`, `lib/studio/campaigns.ts`, `lib/messaging/*`.

**Context.** Place-tree targeting (circle/hub/nexus, which drives Dispatches) and contact-segment targeting (which drives Email) were separate worlds — you could not email "a circle" — the advanced facets were stored but inert, there was no single "who-got-what" view, and broadcast fan-out persisted no recipient log.

**Decision.**
1. **One audience, both worlds.** `resolveSegment` accepts place-tree selectors (`circle:`/`hub:`/`nexus:` → memberships → profiles → contacts) unioned with the trait-segment grammar, and the stubbed advanced facets (engagementDepth/resonanceTier/churnRisk/consent) are activated by joining `member_traits`.
2. **A messaging control panel** (`/admin/marketing/messaging/control-panel`) composes `contact_interactions` + `outreach_sends` + `email_events` + `notification_queue` + the new `dispatch_recipients` into one "what's going / went to whom" view, each raw status normalized onto one `TouchStatus`.
3. **A broadcast recipient log.** `dispatch_recipients` records the per-recipient send-gate outcome for each Dispatch (a fire-safe writer), so Dispatches finally appear in the panel.
4. **Bug fix: Dispatch email fan-out now routes through `resolveSendGate`** (suppression + consent), closing a path that previously bypassed the one gate.

**Consequences.** Additive + RLS-consistent; every resolved recipient still routes through the single `resolveSendGate` (suppression → consent → preference → frequency cap) — no new send path. Reversibility/guardrail: the fan-out gate fix means broadcast email can no longer skip suppression/consent, and the recipient ledger makes every send auditable. The `dispatch_recipients` table is untyped (ADR-246) until regen.

## ADR-615: CRM Phase 6 — granular subscription preference center (topics + frequency + per-circle/Space mutes + contact-keyed prefs), transactional always-on

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 6 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` + Move 6 of `docs/CRM-INTERACTION-TRACKING-PLAN.md` · builds on the fixed 4×3 preference grid, the consent ledger, and the per-Space unsubscribe token · migration `20261161000000_subscription_preferences.sql` · `lib/notification-preferences.ts`, `lib/comms/*`, `settings/notifications/*`, `app/unsubscribe/*`.

**Context.** The preference center was a fixed 4×3 grid (dispatches/events/mentions/lifecycle × email/inapp/push): no topics like comments or marketing, no frequency choice, no per-circle/per-Space mute, the consent scopes had no UI, and non-member contacts had no preference row — so a contact could only hard-unsubscribe.

**Decision.**
1. **Topics + frequency.** Add `comments` (replies + mentions on your own posts) to the per-category grid; keep `marketing` governed by the **consent ledger** (`email_marketing` scope), not a toggle, so the two consent surfaces stay distinct. A per-category **frequency** selector (`realtime`/`daily_digest`/`weekly_digest`) defers the realtime send for the digest cron to batch.
2. **Per-circle/Space mutes** modeled as `(subject, topic, channel, state)`, so a member can mute one circle without leaving. **Consent scopes** (marketing/ai_memory/analytics) get a settings UI. **Contact-keyed preferences** (`lib/comms/contact-preferences.ts`) plus a preference-center landing on the per-Space unsubscribe token let a non-member opt down a topic instead of hard-unsubscribing.
3. **Transactional is carved out, always-on.** Account/security mail never honours a marketing or topic opt-out; the carve-out lives in code and UI.

**Consequences.** Additive; the send gate is checked at send time so preference changes take effect in real time. Reversibility/guardrail: transactional email is structurally exempt from every topic/frequency choice (a member can never accidentally silence a password reset), and marketing stays on the append-only consent ledger, never a mutable boolean. Topic-level opt-down sits beside the global unsubscribe (research: robust centers see materially fewer unsubscribes).

## ADR-616: CRM Phase 7 — Vera daily owner-brief cron + human-approved (non-autonomous) send graduation, defaults-off

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-14) · Phase 7 of `docs/CRM-MASTER-BUILD-PLAN.md` + Move 5 of `docs/CRM-INTERACTION-TRACKING-PLAN.md` · builds on `buildTodayCards()`, the send gate + outbox, and the `withVoice` primer · gated behind the ADR-028 spine/consent/suppression harness · NO migration · `lib/ai/vera/owner-brief.ts`, `lib/ai/vera/execute.ts`, `app/api/cron/vera-owner-brief`.

**Context.** Vera Today was pull-only: nightly predictions existed but nothing pushed the owner a daily brief, and `send_playbook_email`/`send_intro_email` were draft-only ("a later phase"). The owner asked for a smart CRM that scans daily and keeps them updated — which requires a real scheduled trigger (an LLM chat cannot self-schedule) and a careful autonomy graduation.

**Decision.**
1. **A daily owner-brief cron** (`vera-owner-brief`, after `refresh-traits`) reuses `buildTodayCards()` to compose the top moves into a short brief and emails it to the operator and each Space owner. It is **read + compose only** — it never acts on a card; every move stays a human one-tap in Today. Sends go through `resolveSendGate` + the outbox (never inline), frequency-capped to once per recipient per day (a 20h window guards a double cron fire), skipping anyone not opted in to lifecycle email or suppressed. The run is fail-safe: one bad recipient never aborts it and the cron never throws.
2. **Send graduation is human-approved, defaults-off.** `send_playbook_email`/`send_intro_email` graduate from draft-only to real send **only through the send gate and only on explicit human approval**. This is a draft-and-approve step, never autonomous auto-send.

**Consequences.** Additive, no migration. Reversibility/guardrail — **the defaults-off invariant:** every send-capable Vera path ships OFF and requires a human one-tap to fire; nothing auto-acts, and the graduation is gated behind the ADR-028 spine/consent/suppression test harness. The brief only reads and points at Today, so the worst case of a bad run is an empty or skipped email, never an unwanted send. Frequency caps + the gate remain structural (Vera cannot bypass them). Inbound-reply capture and per-scope next-best-action remain follow-ups.

## ADR-617: Splash Funnels — a funnel-STYLE registry + explicit `kind` field + additive per-funnel stats instrumentation (defaults-safe)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-15) · Phase 0 of `docs/SPLASH-FUNNELS.md` · builds on the beta-induction funnel shape (`SequenceOverride` / `BetaSequence`, `app/onboarding/beta/induction.tsx`), the repo's registry idiom (`SPACE_MODULES` / ADR-553, page templates, widgets), and the analytics taxonomy (`lib/analytics/events.ts`, `ACTIVATION_FUNNEL` in `lib/analytics/dashboard.ts`) · NO migration.

**Context.** The `/pages/sequences` "Splash Funnels" admin page is a single-scroll list of ~9 identical audience-onboarding funnel cards (plus role-promotion tours and a how-it-works section). Every funnel is ONE shape rendered by ONE component, and "niche vs general" is only INFERRED from whether `slide2Features` / `slide3Core` are filled — there is no funnel `kind` / `type` / `style` field, and no per-funnel conversion stats. The ask is to manage MULTIPLE funnel STYLES (each with its own layout / design / editor / stats) and to surface entered → signup conversion per funnel, without touching the live visitor experience.

**Decision.**
1. **A `FUNNEL_STYLES` registry** (`lib/funnels/funnel-styles.ts`) is the single source of truth for funnel styles, mirroring how the repo already models menus / templates / widgets. Each row declares `id`, `label`, `icon`, `blurb`, `status` (`'live'` | `'planned'`), `accent` (semantic token, never hex), `renderer`, `editor` (schema + seed), and a `stats` profile. Three styles register: **Onboarding** (`live`, the existing 5-beat induction), **Feature** (`planned`, interactive single-feature play), **Demographic** (`planned`, persona-tuned niche teaser off the DAWN "Teaser" infographics). Adding a 4th style is one registry row, not a rewrite. The redesigned management page derives its tabs from the registry (so new styles auto-appear), leads each card with its headline conversion stat, and shows honest "planned" placeholders for the two unbuilt styles.
2. **An explicit `kind` field** on `SequenceOverride` + `BetaSequence` (`lib/onboarding/*`), **defaulting to `'onboarding'`**. It lives in the existing `data` jsonb, so there is NO migration and every existing funnel reads back as a valid Onboarding funnel with no backfill. A real mirror column is an optional later optimization for fast filtering, not part of this slice.
3. **Additive stats instrumentation, defaults-safe.** Signup counts are available NOW (count `member_tags` by `beta_*` marketing tag, or `profiles.meta.beta.sequence` by exact slug; `assigned_at` for time series) and wire onto the cards in Phase 0 via `lib/traits/segments.ts` + a `computeFunnel()` helper in `lib/analytics/dashboard.ts`. Entered / bounce require one NEW anonymous taxonomy event `onboarding.funnel_entered` (fired on funnel load, keyed by `{ sequence slug, anon id via a new fq_anon cookie }`) plus passing `seqSlug` into the two existing completion `track()` calls in `app/onboarding/beta/actions.ts` — deferred to Phase 1.

**Alternatives.** Keep inferring style from filled fields (rejected: it cannot express Feature / Demographic and gives the editor / stats nothing to key on). A migration + real `kind` column now (rejected for Phase 0: jsonb-only ships with zero DB risk; a column is added only if filtering at scale demands it). A parallel per-style page instead of tabs-over-one-registry (rejected: violates the compose-don't-author page framework and re-introduces the drift the menu contract exists to prevent). Building the Feature / Demographic renderers before the shell (rejected: the biggest lift depends on external DAWN artifacts not yet in the repo; the registry + placeholders let the platform ship value now).

**Consequences.** Additive only: NO migration, no change to any visitor-facing funnel in Phase 0 (the `kind` default makes every existing funnel an Onboarding funnel). Reversibility / guardrail — **the defaults-safe invariant:** `kind` defaults to `'onboarding'` on read so a missing field never breaks a funnel, and the new analytics event is anonymous and fire-safe (a capture can never break a funnel load or a signup). The registry is the enforced seam — new styles are catalog rows, not render edits. Open items: the DAWN teaser infographics (The First Win, Focus Ritual, Never Miss Twice, No Lead Left Behind, One-Timer to Regular, The Marketplace, Practice Loop) are external Claude artifacts that must be published / exported into `design_handoff/` before the Demographic / Feature renderers (Phases 2-3) are built, and the mirror-column-vs-jsonb question for `kind` stays open pending filtering needs.

## ADR-618: On-Air timer warm-up — single-owner begin() guard + top-up skips the second warm-up + one shared `resolveWarmupSec`

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-15) · touches `components/on-air/session.tsx`, `components/on-air/movement-session.tsx`, `lib/on-air.ts` (+ `lib/on-air/warmup.test.ts`) · NO migration · fixes the reported "double warm-up" (builds on the one-countdown pre-roll of ADR-566 and the authored warm-up of ADR-592).

**Context.** A member reported the warm-up pre-roll firing **twice** for what felt like one practice. An audit of every timer (the Be Still sit, Get Moving, the shared pre-roll, the rAF breath visualizer, the season countdown) found the resource hygiene solid (no leaked intervals / rAF, wall-clock session clock, audio + wake-lock released) but isolated the pre-roll as the one systemic weakness. Root cause is NOT React StrictMode (the pre-roll effect is inert at mount and only arms via a post-mount state update, which StrictMode does not double-invoke). It is a **missing single-owner guard**: (1) `finishTheRest()` — the reveal's "finish the rest" top-up — re-invoked `start()`, which unconditionally re-armed a full pre-roll, so a full-cycle sit ran the warm-up a second time; (2) `begin()` was guarded only by `pausedAt !== null`, so the countdown reaching zero and a Start tap in the same instant could each shift `startedAt`, starting the clock a whole warm-up behind; (3) the pre-roll length was read from the stale `practice` **state** rather than the override-resolved `activePractice`, so a same-tick Free-Practice fallback took the wrong (or no) authored warm-up.

**Decision.**
1. **`start()` gains a single-owner guard** (`if (stage === 'live') return`) in both engines, so a run already live can never arm a second warm-up/clock. Legit starts only originate from `setup` or the reveal (`finishTheRest`), never from `live`.
2. **`begin()` latches once** via a `begunRef` (re-armed by `start()`), so the arm→begin handoff shifts `startedAt` exactly once per run.
3. **The top-up leg skips the warm-up.** `start()` takes an optional `warmup` length; `finishTheRest` passes `warmup: 0`, and `warm === 0` opens straight into the live clock (no armed pause, no pre-roll). The member was just breathing; a second countdown was the bug.
4. **One shared, unit-tested resolver.** `resolveWarmupSec(authoredSec, memberSec, override?)` (`lib/on-air.ts`) centralises the precedence (explicit override wins, else positive authored, else member pref; never negative/fractional). Both engines call it, and the sit now reads it off the override-resolved `activePractice`, fixing the stale-read. The pre-roll effect was previously untested; `warmup.test.ts` now covers the resolver including the `warmup: 0` skip path.

**Alternatives.** A short fixed re-settle warm-up on the top-up (rejected for now: 0 is the cleanest read of "don't double the warm-up"; the `warmup` param makes a future 3s trivial). A full **wall-clock anchor** for the pre-roll countdown to fix background-tab drift (a real ⚠️ finding: the countdown decrements via a fixed `setTimeout(1000)`, so backgrounding a 5s warm-up drifts to 8-15s) — **deferred**, not done here: it is an edge case (backgrounding during a 3-10s pre-roll) and rewriting the per-second cue loop on the high-traffic engine without runtime verification is higher risk than the bug. Same reasoning defers the "backgrounded tab skips intermediate interval bells" nit and the dead `DEFAULT_PREFS.mode` / `SavedSetup.mode` config cleanup.

**Consequences.** The reported double warm-up is fixed deterministically; the begin() race and the stale authored-warm-up read are closed; the two engines now resolve the pre-roll identically through one tested function. No migration, no schema, no visitor-facing copy change. Open (documented) follow-ups: wall-clock-anchor the pre-roll countdown, catch-up interval bells on backgrounded tabs, and remove the dead saved-mode config.

## ADR-619: Feature funnels — a playable front door (breathwork), reusing the deferred-induction signup pipeline

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-15) · realises the `feature` style stubbed in ADR-617 + Phase 3 of `docs/SPLASH-FUNNELS.md` · touches `lib/onboarding/{beta-sequences,sequence-overrides,resolve-sequence}.ts`, `app/onboarding/beta/{page.tsx,feature-funnel.tsx,feature-actions.ts}`, `lib/analytics/events.ts`, `lib/traits/registry.ts`, `lib/funnels/funnel-styles.ts`, `app/(main)/pages/sequences/page.tsx` (+ tests) · NO migration.

**Context.** ADR-617 registered three funnel STYLES but shipped only Onboarding; the `style`/`feature` fields it specced were never actually added to the types, and there were no funnel-conversion analytics events. The ask: build the first FEATURE funnel — a visitor plays one stripped feature (box breathing) before signing up. The requested shape: a 5-card wizard where card 2 runs the real breath visualizer, and at the first hold a "get yours free" panel captures a lead; the reward beat shows the true first-log outcome (a Day 1 streak + Zaps) so the signup ask reads as "claim the streak you just started" (endowment + loss aversion), not "give us your email".

**Decision.**
1. **The `style` + `feature` fields are added for real** (jsonb on `SequenceOverride`, mirrored on `BetaSequence`, carried through `resolve-sequence.apply()`), defaulting to `'onboarding'` on read — additive, no migration, every legacy funnel unchanged.
2. **A distinct renderer** (`app/onboarding/beta/feature-funnel.tsx`) is selected by `page.tsx` when `seq.style === 'feature'`, parallel to the cinematic induction. It reuses the real `BreathVisualizer` + `BREATH_PATTERNS` (box), the `WizardProgress` shell, and semantic tokens only. Beat timing runs off one `startedAt` clock (capture at the first hold ~8s, reward chips at the full round ~16s); the visualizer animates imperatively so the capture form appearing beside it never disturbs the breath.
3. **Signup reuses the tested deferred pipeline, unforked.** `beginFeatureFunnelSignup` (server) stamps the `fq_beta_seq` cohort cookie and stashes a minimal pending induction (name + a server-generated **unique** handle) into `fq_pending_induction`; the client then calls the normal `signInWithGoogle` / `signInWithMagicLink` with `next=/onboarding/beta/complete?to=…`, and the existing finalizer writes the profile, tags `beta_breathwork`, applies grants, and lands them. Completion sends them into the app to take a real round, so the "keep your streak" promise is fulfilled by the real, tested practice-log pipeline rather than a duplicated reward write.
4. **The breathwork funnel is a CODE sequence** (`BETA_SEQUENCES.breathwork`), not a DB row: its renderer is code, so defining it in code makes it version-controlled, deploy-with-the-PR, and reversible via git — no out-of-band production write. `listAllSequences()` already lists code sequences, so it appears in the admin console; its `beta_breathwork` marketing tag is registered in `lib/traits/registry.ts` so attribution is not skipped.
5. **Phase-1 analytics, defaults-safe.** Two client-emittable taxonomy events — `onboarding.funnel_entered` (once per session, on load) and `onboarding.funnel_captured` (mid-flow email) — plus the existing `beta_<slug>` signup attribution give the Splash Funnels page entered → captured → signed-up per funnel. The `feature` style flips to `'live'`, so the admin page lists feature funnels under their own section instead of the "planned" placeholder.

**Alternatives.** A lighter "lite" visualizer for the demo (rejected: reusing the real `BreathVisualizer` is zero new animation code and pixel-identical to the feature). Writing the real first practice-log + Zaps in a completion action (rejected for v1: it duplicates the rewards/streak engine and touches the currency ledger; landing the new member in the app to take a real round reuses the tested path and is better UX). Seeding the funnel as a DB `sequence_overrides` row (rejected: a feature funnel's renderer is code, so a code sequence keeps the whole thing in one reviewable, revertible place with no production DB mutation). A wall-clock/fq_anon-deduped entered event (deferred: session-scoped dedup is enough for Phase-1 ratios).

**Consequences.** The first feature funnel is live at `/onboarding/beta?seq=breathwork` on deploy (the PR merge is the deliberate go-live). Signup is not forked — it flows through the exact induction pipeline, so attribution, grants, and landing all keep working. Additive: no migration, no change to any existing funnel. Open follow-ups: an admin editor to author feature funnels (today they are code rows), the remaining Phase-1 stat surfacing (bounce = entered − signed-up) on the dashboard, and a deep-link that opens the breath timer directly on landing (today lands at `/feed?welcome=vera`).

**Addendum (2026-07-15, same day) — redesign + invitation framing + honest 25-Zap grant.** After first review the renderer was rebuilt to match the cinematic beta induction (warm-light shell, brandmark, big font-display headings, dot progress) rather than read as a mobile app in a box, and the flow was retimed to the owner's spec: a **phone mockup** runs the real timer (a 5s countdown, then the box-breath ring) with the coaching beside it; the "Keep going / Get a Free Timer" nudge lands at the first hold; name + email **auto-save** to localStorage; a **reward beat** shows the Day 1 streak + 25 Zaps and lets them **claim a live-checked @username**; a final **Join** beat pre-fills everything + a photo upload. **Back navigation** between beats. Three framing/behavior decisions: (1) the whole thing is framed as an **invitation into the beta launch**, not a plain signup (owner directive, noted in the renderer header); (2) the advertised **"join now, get 25 Zaps" is made honest** — `SequenceGrant` gains a `zaps` field, `breathwork` grants `{ zaps: 25 }`, and `applySequenceGrants` awards it **idempotently** (guarded on a `funnel_bonus` ledger row keyed by seq) at completion; (3) the admin `/pages/sequences` listing now includes **code-source** funnels (it filtered to `custom` only, so the code-defined breathwork funnel was invisible) and shows a "Managed in code" chip instead of the DB lifecycle controls for them. The signup action accepts the picked `@username` (falling back to a name-derived unique handle).

## ADR-620: CRM Marketing tab — one broadcast home that reuses the messaging console + the gated send pipeline, draft-first, double-confirm

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-16) · touches `app/(main)/admin/crm/marketing/page.tsx`, `components/admin/crm/marketing-workspace.tsx`, `components/admin/crm/marketing-compose-popup.tsx`, `components/admin/email-studio/send-panel.tsx`, `lib/nav/studio.ts` · NO migration.

**Context.** The owner wanted a Marketing tab in the Resonance CRM: one place to send email to the whole community or a section (all members, a saved segment, a circle, individuals), with Campaigns / Funnels / Drafts / Sent grouped, plus search, scheduling and trigger stats. The explicit ask was to reuse the exact "Message Member" popup editor but make the right rail the scheduling/trigger/send controls, always save the popup as a draft, and double-confirm before any send. An inspection found ~80% already existed: the messaging console already groups campaigns + funnels by status (`getMessagingConsole`), the `SendPanel` already does audience + preview + schedule + gated send, and `createEmailDraft`/`loadEmailCampaign` already back a draft-first editor. The only net-new was the tab itself, the search box, the popup shell wiring editor + send-rail together, and the second send confirm.

**Decision.**
1. **A new CRM leaf `crm-marketing`** (`lib/nav/studio.ts`) under the CRM Engine group, gated `min: 'janitor'` + `staffDomain: 'marketing'`, mirroring the messaging surface. Contacts is NOT retired (a prior investigation found 13+ live references — imports land there, graph links, analytics) so it is only dropped from the CRM sub-nav grouping, not deleted.
2. **The page reuses the console verbatim.** `getMessagingConsole()` feeds the same Campaigns + Funnels lists and KPI counts; the page adds StatCards (Campaigns / Funnels / Live / Scheduled / Drafts) and a client `MarketingWorkspace` that filters both lists by a search box and hosts the composer. No fork of the console or the send path.
3. **Draft-first popup, mount-per-open.** `MarketingComposePopup` mints a `campaigns` draft (`createEmailDraft('campaign')`) the instant it opens and every edit autosaves, so an email ALWAYS exists as a draft and never sends implicitly. The center is the shared `EmailEditorPane` (stacked), the right rail is the shared `SendPanel` (audience + schedule + send) instead of a member's comms history — the "Message Member" shape, inverted rail. The outer component renders nothing when closed and mounts a fresh inner body each open, so the mint effect runs once on mount and unmount clears state (no reset-on-close setState, no cascading-render lint).
4. **Two-step send confirm.** `SendPanel.sendNow()` resolves the live audience count, then asks for the count confirm AND a second explicit "there is no undo" confirm before calling the gated `sendNowAction`. The real send stays behind the existing `approverGate` (admin/janitor web_role only); this only adds a second human gate on top.

**Alternatives.** A brand-new marketing table / campaign model (rejected: the `campaigns` table + messaging console already are the source of truth; a parallel store would fork status + counts). Retiring Contacts outright (rejected: not cleanly removable, 13+ references; deferred to a dedicated migration). A campaign↔funnel/trigger link so the rail can show per-campaign funnel-flow stats (deferred to Phase 2 — it needs a schema link the `campaigns` table does not yet carry).

**Consequences.** Marketing ships as a thin composition over tested primitives: no migration, no new send path, one more human confirm before a mass send. Operational note: the live admin menu can be overridden by an `admin_header` DB menu (`lib/nav/studio.ts`), so the new tab may not appear until that DB menu is reset/edited — flagged to the owner. Open follow-ups: the campaign↔funnel/trigger link for real per-campaign flow stats (Phase 2), and the eventual clean retirement of Contacts.

## ADR-621: Marketing tab fixes — stop the blank-draft leak at the source, purge the 54, delete affordance, honest counts, Marketing to position 2, retire the old admin Contacts

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-16) · follows ADR-620 · touches `app/(main)/admin/email-studio/actions.ts`, `components/admin/crm/marketing-compose-popup.tsx`, `components/admin/crm/marketing-workspace.tsx`, `components/admin/messaging/messaging-console.tsx`, `lib/messaging/console.ts`, `lib/nav/studio.ts` · one-time production data cleanup (no migration).

**Context.** The shipped Marketing tab (ADR-620) surfaced 68 campaigns of which **54 were blank-subject, empty-scaffold drafts**, buried the 14 real ones, counted the junk in its stat cards, and offered no way to delete anything. Investigation (DB, prod) established the blanks were created **2026-07-12 to 07-15, before the Marketing tab merged (07-16)** — abandoned drafts from the Email Studio composer's "New email", which mints a `campaigns` row on click. The real regression I introduced: the Marketing "New email" popup mints a draft **the instant it opens** and never cleaned it up, reproducing that leak. A purpose-built `discardDraftIfEmpty` already existed (the member composer calls it on close); my popup did not.

**Decision.**
1. **Stop the leak at the shared source.** `createEmailDraft` now **reuses the caller's own pristine empty draft** (via a shared `isPristineDraft` predicate: no subject/preheader/body, no authored `block_json.content`, no send/test/schedule/recipients, no phase) instead of always inserting, so opening a composer or clicking New can never leave more than ONE untouched draft per operator. The Marketing popup additionally calls `discardDraftIfEmpty` on close, matching the member composer. `discardDraftIfEmpty` was refactored onto the same shared predicate.
2. **Purge the existing 54.** A one-time guarded delete removed exactly the 54 draft campaigns matching the pristine predicate (blank subject + empty body + no `block_json.content` + no phase/sends/schedule/recipients) and not referenced by `outreach_sends`. The 14 titled drafts and all beta emails were excluded. Table is now 14 rows, 0 blank.
3. **Honest console + counts.** `getMessagingConsole` now hides untitled DRAFTS (blank subject + status draft) from both the campaign list AND the KPI counts, so a stray blank never clutters the view or inflates the stats. Titled drafts and every sent/scheduled campaign are unaffected.
4. **Delete affordance.** `MessagingConsole` gained an optional `onDeleteCampaign`/`deletingId`; the Marketing workspace wires it to the status-guarded `deleteEmailDraft` (drafts only; sent/scheduled can never be deleted) behind a confirm, and drops the row on success. The shared messaging surface passes no handler, so it is unchanged.
5. **Marketing to position 2.** The CRM Engine group leaf order became `[crm-marketing, crm-intelligence, crm-pipeline]`, so the sub-nav reads Resonance CRM · Marketing · Intelligence · Pipeline.
6. **Retire the old admin Contacts tab.** The `crm-contacts` leaf (the pre-Resonance CRM, replaced by the Resonance CRM) was removed from the catalog so it no longer appears in any admin menu. The PAGE at `/admin/marketing/contacts` STAYS (the platform importer lands there; widgets and the CRM graph deep-link to it) — this is a menu removal only. The member-facing **My Contacts** personal CRM (card scanner + in-person capture + business lead-gen over `network_contacts`) is a different surface and is untouched.

**Alternatives.** Lazy-create (never insert a row until real content) — rejected for now: the block editor autosaves to an existing campaignId, so a reuse-pristine + discard-on-close pair gets the same "no blanks" outcome without rearchitecting the editor. Deleting the `/admin/marketing/contacts` page too — rejected: it has live dependents (importer landing, deep links); removing the menu entry is the safe scope. Archiving the 54 instead of deleting — rejected (owner directive: delete).

**Consequences.** No migration. One-time prod cleanup executed (54 rows). Opening the Marketing composer no longer creates blank drafts; any that slip through are hidden and deletable. Stats reflect reality (14 real drafts, not 68). The old admin Contacts is gone from the menu with its page and every deep link intact. Menu contract (`pnpm check:menu`) + nav drift-guard tests pass.

## ADR-622: CRM contact importer — ZIP upload, a modular custom-field mapper, and keyed-by-stable-key storage so segmentation later is additive

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-16) · touches `lib/crm/import/{types,commit,actions,parse,zip}.ts`, `components/crm/import/import-wizard.tsx`, `lib/crm/pipeline.ts`, `lib/crm/space-contact-detail.ts`, `components/spaces/crm/space-contact-detail.tsx` (+ `lib/crm/import/zip.test.ts`) · NO migration.

**Context.** The owner wanted to "upload and map custom fields today, and build the rest out later," and asked whether that keeps segmenting on custom fields possible later without a rewrite. Investigation found the importer already has a full parse → map → preview → commit wizard, an AI mapping assist, and a `custom_field_registry` table (typed field definitions per owner/Space). The gaps: no ZIP support; the mapping UI auto-slugged a custom key with no way to name / drop / reuse a field; and custom **values** were stored keyed by the human LABEL (`meta.custom["Lead Source"]`), while the registry knew the stable key (`lead_source`). That label-keying was the one landmine: a later contact-scoped segment predicate would have to join on label text (fragile, and a rename orphans values), forcing a migration. Also, space-contact `meta.custom` was write-only dead data (nothing rendered it).

**Decision.**
1. **Keyed-by-stable-key storage (the invariant).** `spaceMeta` now writes `meta.custom` keyed by the stable custom-field key, never the label. The registry holds key -> label/type for display. So a future segment predicate reads `meta.custom[key]` by the same key the registry validates against: segmentation later is purely additive, no migration, no re-import. `ColumnMapping` gains `customLabel` (the operator's chosen name) while `customKey` stays the pinned stable handle, so a rename never moves the value. This applies to the space/platform `contacts` table (the segmentation + campaign target); member `network_contacts` keep their existing `details.other[]` rendering (a personal address book, outside the campaign-audience model).
2. **ZIP upload, dependency-free + server-side.** A new `lib/crm/import/zip.ts` reads the CSV entries out of an uploaded archive (e.g. a Notion / CRM export, one CSV per database) using Node's built-in `zlib` (STORED + raw DEFLATE) — NO archive dependency added to the bundle. It is bounded (entry-count + per-entry + total-uncompressed caps as a zip-bomb guard) and path-traversal-safe (skips absolute / `..` / `__MACOSX` entries), and never throws. A gated `extractZipSources` action fans each CSV through the existing `parseCsvText` + `mergeSources` path; the wizard accepts `.zip` and merges the results with any other files. Unit-tested against hand-built stored + deflated archives.
3. **A modular custom-field mapper.** In the mapping step, a column mapped to a custom field shows an editable NAME (defaults to the header) and the stable key it will be saved as; the operator can rename it, drop the column (the existing "Skip"), or — typing a name that matches a field they already have (fed by the wired-up `listKnownCustomFields`, surfaced via a `<datalist>`) — REUSE that field so a re-import lands in the same key instead of forking `lead_source` / `Lead Source` / `leadsource`.
4. **Surface the fields.** `getContact` now selects `meta`, and the space contact detail renders a read-only "Custom fields" section (labels humanized from the stable key). Imported custom data that was invisible is now on the record.

**Alternatives / deferred.** A parallel keyed `details.custom` bag for member contacts (deferred: members render custom via `other[]` today and are not the campaign-audience model). Inline EDITING of custom fields on the contact (deferred: read-first; edit is a fast follow). The actual **segmentation** on custom fields — a contact-scoped predicate + a data-driven validation source alongside the code trait registry — is explicitly NOT built here; it is the deeper follow-up this ADR's keyed-storage invariant makes additive. Promoting `custom_field_registry` to a governed schema (checked `value_type` enum, `status`, `is_segmentable`, a field-management console) and an AI-assist that proposes custom key/label/type are also deferred. Adding a full archive library (`fflate`) was rejected in favor of the built-in `zlib` reader to keep the dependency surface flat.

**Consequences.** Additive: no migration, no change to any existing import path. Custom values now persist under their stable key, so the segmentation work later needs no data rewrite. ZIP imports work for multi-CSV exports within bounded limits (logged skips, never a silent truncation). Open follow-ups: the contact-scoped segment predicate, custom-field editing on the record, the registry-as-governed-schema + management console, and pipeline linkage.

## ADR-623: Consolidate marketing into the Resonance CRM — the Marketing tab is the one composer; retire the legacy Growth composing tabs (menus now, functions rolled in later)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-16) · follows ADR-620/621 · touches `components/admin/crm/marketing-compose-popup.tsx`, `components/admin/crm/marketing-workspace.tsx`, `components/admin/messaging/messaging-console.tsx`, `lib/nav/studio.ts`, `components/widgets/growth/manage.tsx` · NO migration. Later phases (funnels/automations/nurture roll-in + audiences) are PLANNED here, not built.

**Context.** Email/campaign composing must live in ONE place: the Resonance CRM Marketing tab (`/admin/crm/marketing`). But the tab (ADR-620) reused the messaging console, which linked back OUT to the legacy Growth composer (`/admin/marketing/campaigns`) on every "Open" and quick-link — so the operator kept landing in the old system. Separately, the Growth sub-nav still showed Campaigns / Funnels / Automations / Nurture / Messaging tabs. The owner: those tabs "shouldn't even exist"; usable functions roll cleanly into the Resonance CRM; do not do the big rebuild yet, but remove the tabs and plan the roll-in. Key enabler (from the investigation): the legacy composer and the new email-studio already write and read the SAME `campaigns` table via the same `getMessagingConsole()` — so this is a UI/route consolidation, not a data migration; no rows move.

**Decision (built now).**
1. **The Marketing tab is self-contained.** The draft-first popup (`MarketingComposePopup`) gained a `campaignId` prop, so a campaign row's "Open" now opens THAT campaign in the popup (edit / schedule / send in place); the editor + `SendPanel` already adapt to any status (draft/scheduled/sent, with sent/cancelled read-only). "New email" and the empty-state both open the popup. The legacy quick-links ("Composer", "Nurture") are gone. Nothing in the tab routes to `/admin/marketing/*`. The console gained optional `onOpenCampaign` / `onNewCampaign` so the legacy messaging surface (which passes neither) keeps its old link behavior unchanged.
2. **The legacy composing leaves are retired from the menus.** `marketing-messaging`, `marketing-campaigns`, `growth-funnels`, `marketing-funnels`, `marketing-automations`, `marketing-nurture` are removed from `STUDIO_LEAVES` and from the two groups that referenced them (the `marketing` ADMIN_GROUP links + the Growth ADMIN_NAV "Marketing" heading), plus the Growth "Manage" grid now shows a single "Marketing" card pointing at `/admin/crm/marketing`. The PAGES stay reachable (deep links + the roll-in below need them) — a menu removal, matching the ADR-621 Contacts precedent. Beta Command, Beta waitlist, Marketing analytics / market-read / deliverability / agent stay.
3. **Resonance CRM is searchable in the admin bar.** The admin search filters `visibleLinks` by label + desc, and the CRM landing leaf's label is "Roster", so "Resonance CRM" never matched. Its `desc` now leads with "Resonance CRM home" so the box finds it.

**Deferred (the roll-in plan — build later, do NOT do now).**
- **Funnels** into the CRM: today the funnel flow view (`/admin/marketing/messaging/funnels/[id]`) and the first-class builder (`/admin/growth/funnels/[id]`) are separate. Plan: a Funnels surface under the Resonance CRM that hosts the flow view + builder, then retire those routes. (Owner: "put it on the development list, save the functions, remove the tab.")
- **Automations** (`lib/automations`, event-triggered rules) and **Nurture** (`lib/nurture`, per-persona sequences) fold into the CRM Marketing tab as sub-surfaces, reusing the same block editor + send pipeline.
- **Audiences (Phase C):** the send engine's `resolveSegment` ALREADY resolves `circle:<id>`, `event:<id>`, `profile(s):<id>`, and `contact(s):<id>`; only `listSegmentOptions` / the `SendPanel` picker is capped at members + saved segments. Extend the picker so an operator can send to a circle or pick individuals — no engine change. (Approved in scope; deferred out of this pass per the owner's "no big build right now / low on credits".)
- **Delete the legacy pages** (not just their menus) once the roll-in lands and deep links are repointed.

**Consequences.** No migration. The Marketing tab no longer bounces to the old system; the legacy composing tabs are gone from the menus with their pages intact for the roll-in; the old less-safe direct `status:'sent'` broadcast path is no longer a menu destination (the gated pipeline is the only surfaced send). `pnpm check:menu` + nav tests must pass with the six leaves removed. The roll-in of funnels/automations/nurture and the audience-picker expansion are tracked here as the next phases.

## ADR-624: Contacts uniqueness becomes per-space

**Status:** Accepted · ✅ APPLIED + LIVE (verified against prod 2026-07-25). Migration `20261164000000_contact_tenancy_per_space.sql`. Full spec, invariants and per-call-site rescope table: [CONTACT-TENANCY.md](CONTACT-TENANCY.md). Written 2026-08-04 from that doc and the migration — the decision shipped and was documented in its own file, but never took a slot in this ledger, while **25 live sites across `lib/crm`, `lib/comms`, `lib/spaces`, `lib/connections`, `lib/dashboard`, `lib/ai/vera` and three server actions cite the number**.

**Context.** White-label Spaces are separate CRMs. The same person can be a contact of two of them, with independent `consent_state`, `meta` and lifecycle in each. A global unique index on `lower(email)` makes that impossible: the second Space's insert becomes a silent no-op under `on conflict do nothing`, so the same email simply cannot live in two Spaces. `space_id` was already on `contacts` (backfilled `20260713010000`, stamped by the `contacts_default_space_id` trigger from `20260714010000`), so the tenancy axis existed and was populated — only **uniqueness** was still global.

**Decision.** Replace `contacts_email_lower_idx` (unique on `lower(email)`) with `contacts_space_email_lower_idx` (unique on `(space_id, lower(email))`). Keep a **non-unique** functional index on `lower(email)` for the few space-agnostic scans. Rewrite `sync_contact_from_profile()` to insert against the **root** space and conflict on `(space_id, lower(email))`. This mirrors the shape `email_suppressions` already had.

**Three invariants the migration is built to hold.** The member's platform record is the **root** contact, and the profile link targets it. Global suppression stays platform-wide: `email_suppressions` does not read `contacts` and is untouched, so a STOP still silences every Space. And no data is lost — a pre-flight `DO` block raises rather than proceeding if any `(space_id, lower(email))` duplicate group exists.

**Alternatives considered.** *A partial unique index `where space_id = root`* (rejected — leaves tenant Spaces with no uniqueness guard at all). *A composite on `(space_id, email)` without `lower()`* (rejected — breaks the case-insensitive dedupe every call site relies on).

**Consequences.** ⚠️ **An unscoped `contacts` lookup by email is now a multi-row hazard.** That single consequence is what the 25 citations are actually about: every read must be space-scoped, or scoped to root when it wants the member's platform record. Several are `.limit(1)` + fail-open precisely because an unscoped `maybeSingle()` would throw. ⚠️ One address legitimately produces several rows, so any count or roll-up spanning Spaces needs a deliberate union (the "F7b/F7c stitch" in `lib/ai/vera/today.ts` and `lib/dashboard/scores.ts`). ⚠️ A consent change that must be global (STOP) is an **intentional** cross-space update and is marked as such in `lib/crm/contact-consent.ts`. Later tightened by `20261215000000_contacts_read_operator_only.sql`, which made `contacts_space_read` operator-only.

## ADR-625: Resonance CRM relationship model — a contact holds a SET of relationships (derived + assignable), classified on read, extensible without a migration

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-16) · FOUNDATION layer only (surfaces come later) · touches `lib/crm/relationships.ts`, `lib/crm/classification.ts`, `app/(main)/admin/crm/member-summaries.ts`, `lib/people/member-viewer.ts` (+ `lib/crm/relationships.test.ts`, `lib/crm/classification.test.ts`) · migration `supabase/migrations/20261167000000_contact_relationships.sql` (WRITTEN, not yet applied).

**Context.** The CRM modeled a contact as one implicit "type" scattered across columns (`profile_id` present = member, `consent_state` = subscriber, an owned Space = business). That is not extensible: adding a "donor" or "volunteer" standing meant a new column or a bespoke flag, and a contact is really a SET of relationships at once (a member who is also a donor and a volunteer). We need a model where a contact carries many relationships, some COMPUTED from the record and some operator-conferred, and where adding a new conferred kind is a one-line change, not a schema change.

**Decision.**
1. **Two categories, one registry.** `RELATIONSHIP_KINDS` (`lib/crm/relationships.ts`) is the single source of truth. DERIVED kinds (`member`, `subscriber`, `lead`, `business`) are computed on read and NEVER stored. ASSIGNABLE kinds (`donor`, `partner`, `vendor`, `labs_member`, `volunteer`) are operator-conferred and stored. Each entry carries a stable `key`, a voice-safe `label`, a semantic `tone` token (no hex), a `category`, and a `description`. A typed `RelationshipKind` union + helpers (`isAssignableKind`, `relationshipLabel`, …) derive from the registry.
2. **`kind` is free text validated in code, NOT a Postgres enum.** The table's `kind` column is `text`; the app validates it against the registry (unknown kinds ignored on read, rejected on write). This is the whole point of the seam: adding an assignable kind is ONE registry row with NO migration (an `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE` can't even run in a transaction and would force a migration per kind).
3. **The stored table.** `public.contact_relationships` (id, contact_id → contacts on delete cascade, nullable space_id → spaces, kind text, status default 'active', since date, meta jsonb, created/updated timestamps). Indexes on `(contact_id)` and `(space_id, kind, status)`. RLS ENABLED with NO client policy — SERVICE-ROLE ONLY, mirroring the original `public.contacts` posture (20240221000000). `space_id` is a nullable tenancy tag (null = root/platform) a future per-Space policy can gate on without a schema change.
4. **The classifier.** `classifyContact(row, ctx)` (`lib/crm/classification.ts`) derives `{ status, communityRole, isBusiness, isActive, spacesOwned, relationshipKinds }`. Status from `profile_id` + consent (member > subscriber > lead); `isBusiness` from an owned business-ish Space OR a `space_members.role='admin'` seat; `isActive` from `wam_status` OR a `last_active_at` inside a 7-day window; `communityRole` nulled for non-members. Derivation is PURE + unit-tested; the IO wrappers (`classifyMembers` by profile id, `classifyContacts` by contact id) are fail-safe and do SET-BASED reads.
5. **No N+1 anywhere.** Every batch classifier issues a fixed number of `.in()` reads for the WHOLE set (contacts, profiles, spaces, space_members, the engagement matview, contact_relationships) and joins them in memory — never one query per contact. `loadMemberSummaries` adds exactly ONE batched `classifyMembers(profileIds)` call alongside its existing two batched reads.
6. **`business-ish` Space types** = `practitioner | business | organization | partner | coaching`. `root` (the platform itself) and `lab` (its own `labs_member` relationship) do NOT confer business standing. Exported as `BUSINESS_SPACE_TYPES` so the boundary is one edit.

**Alternatives / deferred.** A `kind` Postgres enum (rejected: defeats the migration-free extensibility that is the point). A per-contact `type` column (rejected: a contact holds many relationships, not one). Per-Space RLS policies on the new table (deferred: service-role-only matches the contacts-era posture; `space_id` is already in place for when a client policy is wanted). Writing the derived kinds as rows (rejected: they are cheap to compute and would drift). The consuming SURFACES — a relationship-chip row on the card, the "add relationship" menu, roster sort/filter on the new fields, the upgrade signal (R2/R3/R5) — are NOT built here; this ADR is the foundation they consume via the extended `MemberSummary`.

**Consequences.** Additive: no existing path changes. The migration is written but NOT applied (the lead applies centrally). `MemberSummary` (`lib/people/member-viewer.ts`) gains four OPTIONAL fields (`communityRole`, `isBusiness`, `activeThisWeek`, `spacesOwned`) — optional so browse surfaces that don't classify are unaffected, always populated by the CRM roster. Adding a new assignable relationship kind stays a one-line registry edit. `lib/database.types.ts` will need regenerating after the migration applies (the reader casts untyped until then, ADR-246).

## ADR-626: Vera autonomous-send graduation + a circuit breaker (disabled-by-default, two unbypassable gates)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Phase 2 of the Vera autonomy track · builds on ADR-028 (propose-only until a harness exists), ADR-169 (the unified send-gate), ADR-616 (human-approved send graduation, defaults-off) · migration WRITTEN, not applied · `lib/ai/vera/circuit-breaker.ts`, `lib/ai/vera/autonomy-config.ts`, `lib/ai/vera/autonomous-send.ts`, `app/(main)/admin/ai/*`, `supabase/migrations/20261168000000_vera_autonomy_decisions.sql`.

**Context.** ADR-616 graduated Vera's two outbound tools (`send_playbook_email`/`send_intro_email`) from draft-only to a real send ONLY on an explicit human tap. The next step the owner asked for is letting Vera SEND on her own for the safe cases, without weakening any guardrail. Autonomous mail is the highest-risk thing an agent can do (consent, deliverability, trust), so it needs a dedicated safety kernel above the send-gate, and it must ship inert.

**Decision.**
1. **A circuit breaker** (`lib/ai/vera/circuit-breaker.ts`) is a single gate every autonomous send passes BEFORE the send-gate. The DECISION is a pure, exhaustively-tested function `evaluateCircuitBreaker(state)`; all IO lives in `checkCircuitBreaker`. It composes four guards, precedence most-fundamental-first: **(a) kill switch** — the master autonomy flag (global) + a per-category enable; **(b) rate caps** — hard per-recipient/day and platform-wide/hour + /day ceilings, counted from the tagged outbox rows; **(c) anomaly trip** — if the recent bounce+complaint rate (from `email_events`, with a minimum sample) crosses a threshold, the breaker DISARMS itself (latches the `vera_breaker_armed` flag OFF) and requires a manual re-arm; **(d) audit** — every decision is recorded. **Fail-closed:** the only path to `allowed` is every guard clear, and any read error returns `config_error` (deny). Uncertainty never sends.
2. **The graduation path** (`autonomousSend`) routes a Vera-decided send through **the breaker THEN `resolveSendGate` (consent + suppression + preference) THEN the outbox** — the enqueue is textually reachable only after BOTH gates return `allowed`. If the breaker OR the send-gate blocks, or anything throws, it FALLS BACK to the existing propose (human-approval) path and never silently sends. IO is injected via `deps` so the predicate is unit-tested without a database.
3. **Owner controls** extend the platform-gated AI-controls surface (`/admin/vera-ai?tab=ai`, janitor OR platform-domain staff): a master autonomy on/off (default OFF, also the global kill), per-category toggles, the rate-cap + anomaly-threshold values, a live breaker status with a manual re-arm button, and the decision audit log. The master switch and the armed latch are boolean `platform_flags` written through `setPlatformFlag`, so every flip lands in `platform_flag_events` (who/when/old→new). The numeric tuning is one fail-safe JSON row in `platform_settings.vera_autonomy` (a broken read defaults to categories OFF, so it can only make the breaker stricter).
4. **Defaults-off invariant.** On merge NOTHING changes: `vera_autonomy_enabled` defaults FALSE (fail-closed) and both categories default OFF, so `autonomousSend` always breaker-blocks (`autonomy_off`) and proposes until an owner explicitly opts in. The breaker starts armed (`vera_breaker_armed` default TRUE), but with the master off that never means "sending".

**Alternatives.** Bake the safety checks into `autonomousSend` inline (rejected — unverifiable; the exact scattered-check gap ADR-028 forbids). Reuse `agent_actions` alone for the audit (kept as the FALLBACK writer so a row always lands even before the migration applies, but a dedicated `vera_autonomy_decisions` table is the clean home — it carries the breaker reason + gate reason + outcome per decision). A boolean-only autonomy flag with no breaker (rejected — no rate cap, no anomaly kill, no re-arm). Storing caps in `vera_config` (rejected — the safety latches belong on the audited `platform_flags`; only the non-safety tuning is JSON).

**Consequences.** Additive and inert by default. The dedicated audit table's migration is WRITTEN but NOT applied (the lead applies centrally); it is registered in `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt` as service-role-only (RLS on, no policy), and the audit writer is best-effort with an `agent_actions` fallback so the send path works before the migration lands. Both gates are structurally unbypassable: the breaker cannot be skipped (it is the first call in the only graduated path), and the send-gate cannot be skipped (the enqueue is reachable only past both). `lib/database.types.ts` needs regenerating after the migration applies (the reader/writer cast untyped until then, ADR-246). Turning autonomy on for real is a deliberate, audited owner action, reversible instantly by the master kill or the breaker.

## ADR-627: One notification router/registry, and `practice.verified` verified-airtime instrumentation (WAM)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · built (`lib/notifications/registry.ts` + `router.ts` + `router.test.ts`; `airtimeVerification` in `lib/on-air/run-over.ts`). **Builds on:** the unified send-gate (ADR-169), the durable outbox (ADR-043 / `lib/queue`), the engagement spine (ADR-025), the run-over gate (ADR-521), and the WAM North Star (ADR-024). **NO migration.**

**Context — two scattered seams.** (1) ADR-169 centralized the send DECISION (`resolveSendGate`), but every send site still open-coded the MAPPING around it: which category a given event belongs to, which channels it fans to, how the job is shaped for the outbox. `fanOutEventPush` hard-coded `category: 'dispatches'`; the automations runner, the booking reminder, the nurture runner each re-derived their own. Scattered mappings can't be audited and drift apart, and adding a notification meant touching bespoke code in N places. (2) The WAM North Star (ADR-024) counts `practice.verified` events, which `logPractice` already emits through the spine and the `member_engagement_stats` RPC already rolls into `verified_practices_7d` → `wam_status`. But the raw event carried no signal of whether the banked airtime was ATTENDED (the member present / confirmed) or CLAMPED (the run-over gate trimmed an unattended over-run), so verified-airtime QUALITY was invisible.

**Decision.**
1. **A notification registry** (`lib/notifications/registry.ts`) is ONE declarative catalog mapping a domain EVENT (`event.dispatch`, `booking.reminder`, …) to a notification TYPE: its send category, default channels, transactional flag, and a pure per-channel `render`. Typed as a per-event map so a missing/extra row is a compile error, and each event's `render` is typed to its own context. Adding a notification is one row.
2. **A notification router** (`lib/notifications/router.ts`) exposes ONE entry, `routeNotification(event, recipient, ctx)`: resolve the type from the registry → render → run `resolveSendGate` PER channel → enqueue only the allowed channels on the existing outbox in the SAME job shape the handlers already drain. Gating at route time (not only at drain time) means a doomed job is never enqueued. The gate + outbox deps are injectable, so the pure routing DECISION (which channels, which reasons, what got enqueued) is unit-tested with no database. Types-only imports of `lib/push`/`lib/email` keep web-push out of any client graph.
3. **Two sites migrated to prove it** (not a rip-out): `event.dispatch` — `fanOutEventPush` (push, community); `booking.reminder` — `runBookingReminder` (email, transactional). Each is behaviour-preserving. A migration checklist for the rest (automations, nurture, winback, owner-brief, event SMS, booking confirm/cancel, email-studio, in-app) lives at the foot of `router.ts`.
4. **`airtimeVerification`** (pure, in `lib/on-air/run-over.ts`) classifies a finalized run from the run-over gate's own inputs as `untimed` / `within_target` / `attended` / `clamped_unattended`. The finalize paths thread an `attended` boolean (present Finish/Close = true; auto-finalize + over-deadline resume = false) through `completeSession` → `logPractice`, which stamps it onto the `practice.verified` event CONTEXT. This ENRICHES the existing event — the per-day idempotency key `practice_log:<profile>:<practice>:<day>` is unchanged, so there is NO second event and NO double count.

**Alternatives.** Keep per-site mappings beside the shared gate (rejected — the same unauditable scatter ADR-169 removed for the decision, now for the mapping). A DB-backed notification-type table (rejected for v1 — the catalog is pure code, typed + tested; a table adds a migration and a read with no gain). Emit a SEPARATE `practice.attended` event (rejected — it would double-count against WAM and split the North Star metric; enriching the existing event's context is idempotent and metric-safe). Compute attended server-side (rejected — only the client finalize path knows present vs auto-finalize).

**Consequences.** Adding a notification is a registry row + a `routeNotification` call; the gate and outbox never change. WAM is unaffected (still binary weekly-active); the new `attended`/`clamped` context unlocks verified-airtime quality analytics and a future WAM refinement with no schema change. `wam_status` confirmed end-to-end: `practice.verified` → `member_engagement_stats.verified_practices_7d` → `computeTraits` `wam_status = verifiedPractices7d >= 1`. The registry currently transports email + push; `inapp` is defined but needs an outbox handler before a type declares it (on the checklist). Non-On-Air `logPractice` callers (check-ins, quick logs) omit `attended`, leaving the event context exactly as before.

## ADR-628: CRM Tasks — an operator follow-up queue (`crm_tasks`), pure filter/sort core, distinct from member crew_tasks

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Phase 2 CRM · touches `lib/crm/tasks.ts` (+ `lib/crm/tasks.test.ts`), `app/(main)/admin/crm/tasks/{page,actions}.ts(x)`, `components/admin/crm/tasks-workspace.tsx`, `components/admin/crm/follow-up-button.tsx`, `lib/nav/studio.ts`, `app/(main)/admin/sections.ts` (icon map), `lib/layout/page-chrome.ts` · migration `supabase/migrations/20261169000000_crm_tasks.sql` (WRITTEN, not applied).

**Context.** The Resonance CRM had no operator work-queue: a staff member reading a contact had nowhere to file "call this person back Thursday." The member-facing `crew_tasks` (docs/NAMING.md "Task" — the volunteer-assignment economy) is a different thing and must not be overloaded. We need a lightweight, staff-only follow-up list, optionally tied to a contact, that a future per-Space policy can scope without a schema change.

**Decision.**
1. **A dedicated `crm_tasks` table** (id, space_id nullable, contact_id nullable → contacts on delete cascade, assignee_profile_id, title, notes, due_at, status text `open|done|snoozed` validated in code, created_by, timestamps). RLS ENABLED with NO client policy — SERVICE-ROLE ONLY behind a staff gate, mirroring the `public.contacts` / `contact_relationships` posture; registered in `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt`. `status` is free text validated against `TASK_STATUSES` in code (not a PG enum), so a new status never needs a migration. `space_id` is a nullable tenancy tag (null = platform/root).
2. **A pure filter/sort core** (`lib/crm/tasks.ts`): `buildTaskInsert`, `isOverdue`, `filterTasks` (mine/all/overdue/by-contact), `sortTasks` (open→snoozed→done, then soonest-due), `summarizeTasks` — no Supabase/Next imports, fully unit-tested (mirrors `buildInteractionInsert`). The IO (`createTask`/`updateTaskStatus`/`listTasks`) reaches the untyped admin client (ADR-246). Client components import the core TYPE-ONLY and inline the tiny filter, so the service-role IO never reaches the browser bundle.
3. **A gated `/admin/crm/tasks` surface** — an `AdminTemplate` KPI board (open/overdue/snoozed/done StatCards) over a filterable list with create/complete/snooze/reopen via `'use server'` actions that re-check `requireAdmin('janitor', { staff: 'marketing' })` (the layout floor is not sufficient) and return the shared `ActionResult`. A reusable `<FollowUpButton contactId>` files a contact-tied task in one tap (the "follow up from a contact" affordance), mounted in the Inbox conversation header.
4. **A new CRM leaf** `crm-tasks` in `STUDIO_LEAVES` (CRM Engine group + sub-nav), gated janitor + marketing like its siblings. Two lucide icon names (`Inbox`, `ListTodo`) were added to the nav icon map; `pnpm check:menu` + the nav drift-guard tests pass.

**Alternatives.** Overload `crew_tasks` (rejected — different domain, different gates, would fork the member economy). A `status` PG enum (rejected — defeats the migration-free extensibility). A per-Space RLS policy now (deferred — service-role-only matches the CRM norm; `space_id` is in place for when a client policy is wanted).

**Consequences.** Additive; no existing path changes. The migration is WRITTEN but NOT applied (the lead applies centrally); `lib/database.types.ts` needs regenerating after it applies (the reader casts untyped until then, ADR-246). Adding a task filter/status stays a one-line code edit.

## ADR-629: CRM 2-way Inbox — threaded conversations over the existing timeline, gated-send replies, and an inbound-email seam

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Phase 2 CRM · touches `lib/crm/inbox.ts` (+ `lib/crm/inbox.test.ts`), `app/(main)/admin/crm/inbox/{page,actions}.ts(x)`, `components/admin/crm/inbox-workspace.tsx`, `app/api/webhooks/inbound-email/route.ts`, `lib/nav/studio.ts`, `lib/layout/page-chrome.ts` · NO new migration (reuses `contact_interactions`).

**Context.** The CRM could log outbound touches but had no place to READ a contact's conversation and reply in-thread, and no way to RECEIVE an inbound email.
