Investigation (the send-gate + message-member path) established: replies must route through the SAME gated path Message Member uses (`resolveSendGate` → `enqueueEmail`) and must NOT bypass consent; and there is NO inbound-email receive seam today (the Resend webhook records delivery/engagement only, and the platform send path does not record an outbound timeline touch for platform email).

**Decision.**
1. **Threaded read over the ONE timeline.** `groupIntoThreads` (pure, tested) folds `contact_interactions` (channels email/sms/in_app, inbound + outbound) into per-contact conversations, newest first, with an `awaitingReply` flag when the latest message is inbound. `listInboxThreads` gathers the conversational slice + batch-loads contact identities. No new table.
2. **Gated-send replies.** `sendInboxReplyAction` resolves the contact's email + linked member profile, runs `resolveSendGate(profileId, 'email', 'marketing', { email })` — the exact gate Message Member uses — and only on `allowed` calls `enqueueEmail` onto the durable outbox (never inline), with RFC-8058 unsubscribe headers. It is FAIL-CLOSED: a pure lead with no member profile has no consent record, so we do not send. Because the platform send path does not record an outbound touch, the action then records `direction:'outbound'` on the timeline itself (mirroring the manual-touch/DM recorders) so the reply shows in the thread. Each gate-block maps to a plain, in-voice reason line.
3. **An inbound-email seam (scaffold).** `parseInboundEmailPayload` (pure, tested) + `recordInboundEmail` (match from-address → contact → record `direction:'inbound'` via the one recorder, never the table directly) behind a signature-verified route at `/api/webhooks/inbound-email` (modeled on the Resend webhook: Svix verify + freshness + 200-ack). It NEEDS PROVIDER CONFIG to go live — `RESEND_INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (until set, every request is rejected 401, so the seam is inert but wired) and `CRM_INBOX_OWNER_PROFILE_ID` (the owner for a platform inbound touch from a lead with no member profile; a member contact's own profile owns it). No provider secret is invented here.
4. **A new CRM leaf** `crm-inbox` in `STUDIO_LEAVES` (CRM Engine group + sub-nav), gated janitor + marketing. Uses `AdminTemplate` with a two-pane conversation body (the /admin shell; StreamTemplate is a member shell). Both surfaces are registered in `MANAGED_ROUTES`; the rail stays the admin default ('none').

**Alternatives.** Use category `transactional` for replies (rejected — it bypasses consent; the brief forbids that, so we match Message Member's `marketing`). Send to leads without a profile (rejected — no consent record; fail-closed). A new inbox/messages table (rejected — the `contact_interactions` timeline already is the source of truth). Insert inbound rows directly (rejected — everything goes through `recordContactInteraction`, the one front door).

**Consequences.** No migration. Outbound replies are consent-gated end to end and appear in-thread. The inbound half is a documented seam that goes live by configuring the two env vars + pointing a provider inbound webhook at the route; until then it is verified-and-inert. `pnpm check:menu` + `check:rls` + `check:seo` + the nav drift-guard tests pass.

## ADR-630: Segment Builder — operators constrained by field type, and a date control for timestamp traits

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · CRM / Member Data Platform · touches `app/(main)/admin/segments/field-ops.ts` (+ `field-ops.test.ts`) and `app/(main)/admin/segments/segment-composer.tsx` · NO new migration, NO new route (the `segments` leaf + `/admin/segments/{new,[id]/edit}` surfaces already existed).

**Context.** The Segment Builder (ADR-069 Phase 3 → P5) already shipped: a gated index, Focus-template create/edit forms, a debounced live "matches N members" preview over the real member snapshots, `validateSegmentDefinition` against the trait registry before every write (including the value-type check), gated `createSegment`/`updateSegment`/`deleteSegment` actions that refuse `is_system` rows, and `listSegmentOptions` surfacing each saved segment to the email composer as `seg:<slug>`. Two rough edges remained against the "a beginner can build this" bar: the operator dropdown offered all six comparisons for EVERY field (so "resonance_tier greater than resonant" or "web_beta at most true" were selectable nonsense that then never matched), and timestamp traits (`activation_date`, `last_active_at`, …) rendered as a free-text box, inviting an unparseable value.

**Decision.**
1. **A pure `field-ops.ts` core** (`allowedOpsForType`, `opLabel`, `clampOp`) — no React, no server deps, unit-tested. Ordered types (number, timestamp) keep the full comparison set; categorical types (boolean, enum, string) are restricted to `eq`/`neq`. Timestamps are stored as ISO strings whose lexicographic order is chronological, so `gt`/`lt` are valid and read as "after"/"before" via a type-aware label map.
2. **The composer consumes it.** The comparison `<select>` renders only `allowedOpsForType(trait.type)`; changing the field `clampOp`s the row's operator so a stale relational op can't survive a switch to a categorical field. Timestamp traits get a native `type="date"` input (an ISO date compares correctly against the stored ISO timestamp).

**Alternatives.** Constrain ops in the registry per-trait (rejected — the type already implies the family; a per-trait list is redundant data to maintain). A full datetime picker for timestamps (rejected — date granularity is what operators reason in; the ISO-prefix compare is exact enough and forgiving). Leave the validator as the only guard (rejected — it rejects bad values but the UI should never OFFER them).

**Consequences.** Additive and UI-only; the stored `SegmentDefinition` shape, the validator, the actions, and the composer→`seg:<slug>` picker path are unchanged. `npx vitest run lib/traits app/(main)/admin/segments`, `pnpm check:menu`, and `pnpm check:seo` pass.

## ADR-742: Member-facing consent-gated promotion — network_contacts → the marketing contacts DB

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Network / CRM privacy boundary · implements ADR-154 §"privacy invariant" on the ADR-099 consent ladder. Touches `app/(main)/connections/actions.ts` (new `promoteToContacts`, hardened `setVisibility`), `app/(main)/connections/[id]/detail.tsx`, `app/(main)/network/contacts/page.tsx`, new `lib/connections/promote.ts` (+ `promote.test.ts`), new `components/connections/promote-to-contacts.tsx` + `visibility-control.tsx`. **NO migration.** Reuses the existing `syncScanToCrm` bridge — its internals are unchanged. ADR number picked high/unused to avoid clashing with the concurrent Phase-3 event-loop work (event_guests / QR).

**Context.** ADR-154 democratized the personal book (`network_contacts`) to member tier and named the one crossing that concentrates leak risk: a private capture entering the shared marketing DB (`contacts`). That crossing already had a fail-safe, idempotent, consent-correct engine (`syncScanToCrm`: root-scoped upsert on `lower(email)`, `consent_state='unknown'`, links `linked_contact_id`, never downgrades an existing lead/member) but no member-facing way to invoke it deliberately — it only fired implicitly at create time when an email was present. Members also had a Private↔Network visibility toggle with no explanation of what "Network" actually exposes.

**Decision.**
1. **`promoteToContacts(contactId)`** — owner-gated (`contactsOwnerId`, member tier), re-reads the row from the trusted owner-scoped store (never trusts client fields, which is also the ownership check), and calls `syncScanToCrm` with **only** the email + display name. **Idempotent:** an already-linked capture returns `{state:'already'}` and writes nothing. **Fail-safe:** no email → a calm reason; any throw → a calm reason, promotes nothing. The marketing row stays `consent_state='unknown'` (added, never mailable until they confirm).
2. **Deliberate + consent-gated UI** — a two-step confirmation that states plainly, before any write: they join as an unconfirmed lead, they are not and cannot be emailed until they confirm/sign up, and your private notes and tags stay with you. Never silent.
3. **`promotionState` (pure, tested)** — `linked | needs_email | ready`, so the action and the UI agree on state in one auditable place.
4. **Visibility toggle hardened + explained** — `setVisibility` now coerces anything but `'network'` to `'private'` (the deferred `'shared'` tier is never accepted even if forged), and a new `VisibilityControl` renders owner-only Private↔Network with helper text kept honest to `canViewLead`'s `network_local` rule (Network = findable by same-city stewards, only the basic card; email/phone/notes/tags stay owner-private).
5. **Linked-state surfaced** — an "In contacts" indicator on the card + detail whenever `linked_contact_id` is set.

**The privacy invariants (non-negotiable, all upheld).** Promotion is deliberate + consent-gated, never silent. The marketing row is `consent_state='unknown'` (never mailable without a later confirm). Personal **notes and tags are never copied** into the marketing/shared layer — the action passes only email + display name. Owner-scoping RLS is untouched. Democratizing to member tier does **not** widen `canViewLead` (a member sees only their own book; the network_local read path stays host+, unchanged). An existing lead/member's consent or source is never downgraded (`syncScanToCrm` touch-only path).

**Alternatives.** Auto-promote on save (rejected — silent crossing, violates the invariant). Copy notes/tags so the marketing view is "complete" (rejected — that IS the bleed the boundary exists to stop). Offer the `'shared'` visibility tier now (rejected — deferred decision; only private/network here). A new bridge helper (rejected — `syncScanToCrm` already is the consent-correct, idempotent front door; we call it, we don't fork it).

**Consequences.** Additive; no schema or RLS change; `syncScanToCrm` untouched. Operator/member guidance → Notion. Validated: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx eslint` clean, `npx vitest run lib/connections lib/crm` green, `pnpm check:authz` passes (the action guards via `contactsOwnerId`; the pure helper touches no admin client).

## ADR-631: The event-invite capture loop — one attributed scan, three books, consent observed

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Network / CRM · builds ADR-154 §3 (the Phase-3 headline) on the ADR-098/099 membrane laws + consent ladder. **New migration** `supabase/migrations/20261170000000_event_guests.sql` (NOT applied — file only). Touches new `lib/qr/event-invite.ts` (+ test), new `lib/events/guests.ts` (+ test), new public surface `app/(marketing)/rsvp/[token]/{page,form,actions}.tsx`, and one branch in `app/q/[slug]/route.ts`. Pairs with ADR-742 (the deliberate `network_contacts → contacts` promotion), which handles the later consent crossing this loop's captures eventually take.

**Context.** ADR-154 named the missing half of the Network rework: RSVP was members-only (`toggleRSVP`), so a member had no way to invite a non-member to an event and *keep* them. The data architecture already existed — `event_rsvps` (members), `network_contacts` (owner-scoped personal book), `contacts` (consent-gated marketing) — plus the attributed `/q/<slug>` primitive (owner + event stamped) and the `syncScanToCrm` bridge. What was missing was the public capture surface and the fan-out that lands one captured person in all three books without bleeding personal data into marketing.

**Decision.**
1. **`event_guests` — a new, fail-closed table.** `event_id` + `inviter_profile_id` FKs, `display_name/email/phone`, `rsvp_status` (`going|maybe|declined`, nullable), `source='event_qr'`, `meta` jsonb, `created_at`; indexed on `(event_id)` and `(inviter_profile_id)`. RLS enabled with a **SELECT-only** policy (the inviter reads their own captured guests; the event host reads their event's list) and **no** insert/update/delete policy — writes are service-role-only behind the signed-token gate. Mirrors the `network_contacts` posture. The `network_contacts.source` CHECK gains `'event'` via the same drop-and-recreate the P1 migration used for `'qr_scan'`.
2. **Token-authenticated public form.** An **anonymous** scan of a member's attributed QR (owner + event both present) is routed by `/q/<slug>` to `/rsvp/<token>`, where `<token>` is a fresh HMAC-signed `event-invite:<b64(payload)>.<sig>` minted from the code's *own* `owner_profile_id + event_id` (`lib/qr/event-invite.ts`, namespaced + expiring, mirrors `lib/beta-tokens.ts`). The form and its submit action resolve the inviter + event **only** by verifying the token — a client-supplied `inviter_profile_id`/`event_id` is never trusted. The page is `robots: { index: false }`; the submit is IP rate-limited (`event_guest`, fail-closed in prod) with an **identical success response regardless** (anti-enumeration). The public page exposes only the event's own title/time and the inviter's display name — never the inviter's other contacts.
3. **A single fail-safe orchestrator** (`lib/events/guests.ts` `captureEventGuest`) does the triple-write transactionally-best-effort, each leg isolated in its own try/catch: (1) `event_guests`, (2) the inviter's `network_contacts` (`source='event'`, `visibility='private'`, deduped on `owner_id+lower(email)`, no photo so the private bucket is untouched), (3) `contacts` at `consent_state='unknown'`, `source='event'`, root-scoped, linked back via `linked_contact_id`. The guest + personal legs are the **priority** (they define `ok`); the marketing leg is **best-effort** (swallowed). A failure in one leg never corrupts the others.

**The privacy invariant (non-negotiable, ADR-154).** The captured person stays **personal**. They enter marketing only as `consent_state='unknown'` (added, never mailed) and become mailable only on a later confirm/signup (the deliberate ADR-742 promotion). An existing lead/member is never downgraded. Owner-scoping is enforced on every write; the inviter's notes/tags never leak to marketing; the `network_contacts` owner RLS is untouched.

**Alternatives.** Trust the inviter/event from the form (rejected — a public surface must never trust a client-supplied owner id; the signed token is the only authority). Reuse `syncScanToCrm` verbatim for the marketing leg (rejected only on the `source` label — it hardcodes `'scan_invite'`; the leg here mirrors its consent-correct, no-downgrade, root-scoped, link-back behavior with `source='event'`). Auto-subscribe RSVPs (rejected — violates the bleed boundary + CAN-SPAM). One leg failing rolls back the others (rejected — the guest + personal capture is the value; a marketing hiccup must not lose the person).

**Consequences.** Additive: a new fail-closed table, a stateless signed token, one public route, and one anonymous-only branch in the QR resolver; existing signed-in scan flows (one-tap RSVP, personal capture, space lead-grab) are untouched. Member/operator usage guidance → Notion. Validated: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx eslint` clean on changed files, `npx vitest run lib/events lib/connections lib/qr` green (255) + the two new suites (13), and `pnpm check:rls` / `pnpm check:seo` / `pnpm check:authz` pass.

## ADR-743: Reviews read-side finish — Product AggregateRating JSON-LD + an operator reviews console

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Commerce / SEO-AIO · completes the ADR-597/598 reviews model (the `commerce_reviews` table + `space_review_responses`). No schema change. Touches `lib/listings-shared/detail-view.ts` (+ `listing-seo.ts` + test), `app/(main)/market/[id]/page.tsx`, `lib/commerce/reviews.ts`, `app/(main)/admin/marketplace/{page,actions,reviews/page}.tsx`, and two studio-nav rows (`lib/nav/studio.ts` + one icon in `app/(main)/admin/sections.ts`).

**Context.** The reviews model (ADR-597/598) shipped end to end EXCEPT two read-side gaps: (1) the Market product detail page loaded its review aggregate but never emitted it as schema.org `AggregateRating`, so the Product rich-result / AIO citation was thin next to the Space profile (which already carries `aggregateRating` via `spaceSchema`); and (2) operators could only moderate a review inline on each product page (the per-listing Hide button) — there was no single place to SEE every review, visible or hidden.

**Decision.**
1. **Product `AggregateRating` on the listing detail JSON-LD.** `ListingDetailView` gains an `aggregateRating` field; `listingDetailFromProduct` fills it from the already-loaded `getProductReviews` aggregate (classifieds + housing pass `null` — no review model). `listingJsonLd` emits the `AggregateRating` node ONLY when `reviewCount > 0`, so a listing with no reviews carries no rating (a null/zero rating is dropped, matching `spaceSchema` — answer engines discard malformed schema).
2. **An operator reviews console** at `/admin/marketplace/reviews`, added as a `marketplace-reviews` studio leaf beside `-reports` / `-disputes` (the established platform-admin pattern; the MENU-CONTRACT `*_MODULES` catalogs govern the entity rail, not the platform `/admin` nav, so this is a studio-leaf row, not a registry row). It lists every review (visible + hidden) through the admin client behind `requireAdmin('admin', { staff: 'platform' })` — the RLS public policy only exposes visible reviews on active products, deliberately too narrow for oversight — with Hide / Restore actions (`unhideProductReview` is the new reverse of the existing `hideProductReview`).

**Alternatives.** Add `aggregateRating` to the generic `productSchema` builder (rejected — the listing detail page renders through `listingJsonLd`, not `productSchema`; the field belongs on the view). Put reviews moderation in `ADMIN_MODULES` (rejected — that catalog is the per-entity rail; platform marketplace oversight is a studio leaf, like reports/disputes). A reported-reviews-only queue (deferred — reviews have no report target_kind yet; the console shows all reviews so an operator can spot-check, and reported listings still flow through the existing reports queue).

**Consequences.** Additive; no schema, no RLS, no new capability (reuses the platform-staff gate + the existing `hideProductReview`). The Space reviews surfaces (tab, responses, `spaceSchema` rating) were already complete and are untouched. Operator moderation guidance → Notion. Validated: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx eslint` clean on changed files, `npx vitest run` green (new `listing-seo.test.ts` + the jsonld/space suites), `pnpm check:menu` and `pnpm check:rls` pass.

## ADR-744: Phase 4 — commerce loading states, dead-letter discard, and the deferred email refactors

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Email/queue + UX · no schema change. Touches `app/(main)/{orders,store,market}/loading.tsx` (new), `lib/queue/outbox.ts`, `app/(main)/admin/marketing/deliverability/{actions.ts,requeue-button.tsx}`, `components/widgets/marketing/deliverability-dead-letters.tsx`.

**Context.** A Phase 4 audit of the roadmap's email/queue items found most already shipped and flagged what was actually worth doing vs. what to defer.

**Decisions.**
1. **Route-level loading skeletons for `/orders`, `/store`, `/market`.** These three commerce surfaces blocked first paint on heavy async reads (force-dynamic, several sequential awaits) with no fallback. A segment `loading.tsx` renders instantly during the awaits (the house `Skeleton` pattern), so the post-checkout landing and the two hero-led catalogs never open on a blank screen. New files only — no page edits, so no Suspense refactor and no risk to the existing EmptyState handling.
2. **A terminal `discarded` status for the dead-letter queue.** Requeue resets `attempts=0`, so a poison payload (malformed job, deleted recipient) looped `failed → requeued → failed` forever. `discardDeadLettered()` marks such rows `'discarded'` — a free-text status (no CHECK constraint on `notification_queue.status`, so migration-free) that drops out of the DLQ view (which filters `status='failed'`) and out of the drain (which claims `'pending'` only), while keeping the row + `last_error` for the record instead of deleting it. Exposed via a marketing-gated `discardDeadLetters` action + a Discard button beside Requeue. The scoped `kind` is never logged (log-injection sink, CodeQL) — the count carries the signal.

**Deferred (with rationale), NOT done unattended.**
- **react-email migration — defer.** Not installed; email is three hand-rolled inline-HTML systems (`lib/email.ts` ~20 transactional templates, the `email-studio` block WYSIWYG, the campaign wrapper) carrying every deliverability-critical feature (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe, per-recipient unsubscribe tokens, plaintext alternatives, CAN-SPAM footer, consent/suppression gates). A documented in-code landmine: `lib/email.ts` is transitively pulled into a client bundle, so react-email's server `render()` would taint the Turbopack client graph and break `next build`. Safe path is phased (break the client-bundle taint behind a `server-only` seam first, then port low-risk templates one PR at a time keeping headers+plaintext identical, leave Email Studio alone). Deliverability-critical — not a big-bang.
- **`send.*` subdomain split — ops-only.** DNS + Resend + env (SPF/DKIM/DMARC + MX, verify the subdomain, repoint the sender env var). No repo change to make here.
- **FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — keep low priority.** A near-no-op for this app: the service-role client bypasses RLS via `BYPASSRLS` (most access), and plain ENABLE already governs anon/authenticated paths. The nuance PR-#1779 missed is that FORCE also subjects the table OWNER to RLS, which would put the large `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC surface (owned by `postgres`) under RLS and risk BREAKING functions that legitimately rely on owner-bypass. If ever adopted, do it per-table with the definer RPCs tested — never a blanket sweep.

**Consequences.** Additive UX + one queue-recovery affordance; no schema, no new capability (reuses the marketing staff gate). Validated: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on changed files, and the CodeQL log-injection alerts on the new log lines resolved by dropping the caller-supplied value from the log.

## ADR-777: Connector rewards — reward the OUTCOME of an event-invite capture, never the row

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Gamification / anti-farm · pairs with ADR-154 (the event-invite capture loop) and migration `20261172000000_connector_rewards`. Touches `lib/rewards/connector.ts`, `lib/events/guests.ts`, `app/(main)/events/actions.ts` (check-in), `app/onboarding/actions.ts` (signup), `lib/achievements.ts`.

**Context.** ADR-154 shipped the capture loop (a member's attributed event QR → a public RSVP form → the guest triple-write). It needed a reward model that pays the inviter for bringing real people, WITHOUT paying for a bare row (the anti-farm doctrine: "adding a row is never a payout").

**Decision.** Pay the inviter on ascending real outcomes: capture 2⚡, RSVP going/maybe 4⚡, verified check-in 8⚡, signup 8⚡ + 5💎. Every grant is (a) IDEMPOTENT via a deterministic `reward_grants` rule_key `connector:<outcome>:<inviter>:<guestKey>`, (b) DAILY-CAPPED per inviter (`CONNECTOR_DAILY_CAP=25`), and (c) FAIL-SAFE (a reward failure never breaks the capture/check-in/signup flow). Three call-site seams (capture in `captureEventGuest`, attend in `checkInEvent`, join in `completeOnboarding`) each fail-safe. A "real connection" (RSVP'd/attended/joined, never a bare capture) advances the Connector achievement at 10/25/100. The `guestKey` MUST be stable per (event, person): `captureEventGuest` leg 1 dedupes `event_guests` on `(event_id, email)` so a form resubmit refreshes the same row rather than minting a new id — otherwise the capture/RSVP reward re-pays and the achievement count inflates on every resubmit (fixed 2026-07-17 in the post-merge correctness sweep).

**Alternatives.** Pay on the raw capture row (rejected — farmable). Key the reward on the `event_guests` row id without deduping the insert (rejected — a bare insert makes the id non-stable, defeating idempotency). Award Gems for every outcome (rejected — economy inflation; only the join carries a 💎).

**Consequences.** Additive; the achievement tiers + the `connector_join` gem key are seeded in `20261172000000`. The Connector count reads `event_guests` rows with `rsvp_status IN ('going','maybe')` for the inviter, so the leg-1 dedupe is load-bearing for count accuracy too.

## ADR-778: The `'shared'` visibility tier for personal network contacts (supersedes ADR-742's deferral)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-17) · Privacy / CRM · migration `20261171000000_network_contacts_shared_space`. **Supersedes** the ADR-742 note that deferred this tier ("Offer the 'shared' visibility tier now — rejected, deferred"): the tier is now specified and its write path + RLS ship. Touches `lib/connections/visibility.ts`, `lib/connections/store.ts`, `lib/connections/types.ts`, `lib/spaces/operated.ts`, `app/(main)/connections/actions.ts`, `components/connections/visibility-control.tsx`.

**Context.** ADR-098 built `network_contacts` as an owner-scoped personal CRM (private → shared → network). ADR-132/154 shipped private↔network for members; `'shared'` was left deferred (ADR-742). This lands it.

**Decision.** `'shared'` means the contact's CARD (name/role/company/city/links/email/phone — never the owner's private notes/tags) is readable by the TEAM of ONE Space (`shared_space_id`) the owner OPERATES. Two distinct bars: WHO MAY SHARE — the owner must operate the target Space (own it or be an active admin space_member), verified server-side via `operatesSpace` and the pure fail-closed `resolveVisibilityChange` (an unauthorized/unscoped `shared` coerces to `private`); WHO MAY READ — the Space's team (owner or any active space_member), gated by `isSpaceTeamMember`. A permissive RLS SELECT policy OR-ed alongside the owner/network policies grants the team a READ of the shared row; writes stay owner-only; the notes/tags tables are untouched (owner-only), so the privacy invariant holds. Moving away from `'shared'` clears `shared_space_id` (a DB CHECK mirrors it).

**Read surface.** The team-facing READ SURFACE — a Space operator view listing the shared cards via `listSpaceSharedContacts` (card fields only, gated by `isSpaceTeamMember`) — ships alongside the write tier so a contact shared with a Space's team is actually visible to that team. The RLS grants a raw row read (broader than the app reader's card-only projection); a defense-in-depth follow-up is to expose only card columns via a security-barrier view.

**Consequences.** Additive column + CHECK + partial index + one RLS policy; the cross-steward `network` tier (ADR-132) and `canViewLead` are untouched. Consent never transfers, notes/tags never leak.

## ADR-779: Space-authored Practices & Journeys (tenancy wiring), the free-published-Journey cap, and the beta-notice rule

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Tenancy / entitlements / content · NO migration (columns exist). Touches `lib/journeys/publish-limits.ts` + `publish-gate.ts` (new), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/journeys/*` + `practices/*` (new), `lib/spaces/functions.ts`, `lib/admin/modules/space-modules.ts`, `lib/practices.ts`, `lib/journey-plans.ts`, `app/(main)/journeys/actions.ts`, `components/widgets/entity/entity-practices.tsx`, `lib/core/beta-notices.ts` + `docs/BETA-NOTICES.md` (new), `components/pricing/authoring-access-note.tsx` (new).

**Context.** The `space_id` tenancy plumbing on `practices` + `journey_plans` (create accepts it, `list*ForSpace` filter it, isolation tests lock it) shipped but was NEVER wired from a Space surface: every create stamped root, so a practitioner's content never appeared on their Space and there was no manager. Owner asks (2026-07-18): Crew+ can author a Practice (already true via `practice.create`); Spaces author Journeys (the e-learning program); a FREE space publishes ONE Journey (the upsell), paid to list in the library; a practitioner's own-space content skips the public-library review queue (usable by their members immediately). Plus: make the beta permission/upsell messaging a rule tied to the beta switch, with a remembered inventory to edit at launch.

**Decision.**
1. **Space-scoped authoring** — new `createSpaceJourneyAction` / `createSpacePracticeAction` (+ `setSpacePracticeLiveAction` / `submitSpacePracticeToLibraryAction`) resolve the Space from its slug and gate on MANAGING it (`getSpaceCapabilities(...).canEditProfile`), NOT the person's member tier, so a free member running a Space can build. They pass `spaceId` to the existing `createPlan`/`createPractice`, stamping the content to the Space.
2. **Own-space content skips public-library review** — a Space Journey is a private draft; a Space Practice is `status:'draft'`, `is_public:false` (usable by members: the space read ignores status/is_public). Reaching the PUBLIC library keeps the existing gate: a Journey goes `public` (paid + Vera/mod review); a Practice needs paid Crew (`practice.create`) + staff review (`submitSpacePracticeToLibraryAction` sets `pending`, never flips `is_public`).
3. **Free-published-Journey cap** — enforced CENTRALLY at the one publish chokepoint (`setJourneyVisibility` → `checkJourneyPublish`), so it covers space AND personal Journeys. "Published" = visibility past `private` (`unlisted` = live to the space/link, `public` = library). A free owner publishes `FREE_PUBLISHED_JOURNEY_LIMIT` (1); `public` is paid-only. The owner is the Space (its plan) when stamped to one, else the author (their tier). Pure rules in `publish-limits.ts`; the IO (owner + count + paid signal) in `publish-gate.ts`. NO entitlement key or migration: free-vs-paid is the lever, read from `asSpacePlan(space.plan)` / `isPaid(tier)`.
4. **Menu + managers** — two universal `SpaceFunctionKey`s (`practices`, `journeys`, default-ON, editor role) + two `SPACE_MODULES` rows (per the MENU-CONTRACT, ADR-553; `pnpm check:menu` green) route to new owner-gated managers at `/spaces/[slug]/{practices,journeys}` (mirroring `/journeys/mine`, listing ALL the space's content). The public profile block (`entity-practices`) now reads `publishedOnly` so drafts stay in the manager; its owner-empty CTAs point at the new managers.
5. **Beta-notice rule** — `lib/core/beta-notices.ts` centralizes beta-tied copy (`betaLeadLine`, `crewUpgradeSuffix`, `crewCreateUpsell`, `contentSafetyLine`) driven by `BETA_OPEN_ACCESS`, so launch flips every adopted notice at once. `AuthoringAccessNote` (on every create surface: the two Space managers, `/journeys/mine`, `/journeys/new`, `/practices/new`) states the role-based permission, the "open through September 1" beta lead, and the "nothing you build is ever lost" promise. The four create-gate strings now read `crewCreateUpsell`. `docs/BETA-NOTICES.md` is the launch checklist inventorying every beta announcement site-wide with its driver (flag / other-flag / hardcoded) and launch action.

**Alternatives.** Add a `journeys.unlimited` entitlement key (rejected — the cap is purely free-vs-paid; a key + `pricing_feature_gates` seed migration is overhead for no added flexibility). Gate the cap only in the new space action (rejected — publishing also happens from the editor's `setJourneyVisibility`, so the chokepoint is the correct single home). Create Space Practices as `approved` at birth (rejected — that would library-skip AND show a blank on the profile; `draft` keeps them out of the public profile until "make live").

**Consequences.** No migration. `createPractice`'s `status` union widened to include `'draft'` and it now writes any non-`approved` status (previously only `'pending'` was written, silently dropping others). `list{Practices,JourneyPlans}ForSpace` gained an additive `publishedOnly` option (default = today's behavior; isolation tests unchanged, 42 green). New pure tests for `publish-limits` + `beta-notices`. tsc + eslint clean; `check:menu` green. Follow-ups: per-space phase/step counts on the Journeys manager cards (currently 0), and migrating the remaining hardcoded beta strings (docs/BETA-NOTICES §4) onto the rule.

## ADR-780: Four practice-system correctness fixes (spark anti-farm, welcome-back reversal, streak race, solo-journey enrollment) + journey slots mint real practices

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Economy / journeys correctness · NO migration. Touches `lib/rewards/spark.ts`, `lib/practices.ts` (`logPractice`/`unlogPractice`), `lib/practice-streak.ts`, `lib/journey-plans.ts` (`adoptPlan`), `app/(main)/journeys/[slug]/edit/actions.ts`, `components/journey/v2/journey-editor.tsx`. Follows the practice-system audit (the ADR-779 PR).

**Context.** The audit surfaced five defects. This ADR fixes them.

**Decision.**
1. **Spark anti-farm (was a Gem drip).** `unlogPractice` deleted the `spark:{profile}:{day}` cap-claim while keeping the paid Gems (awardGems has no debit), so a `log -> unlog -> re-log` loop re-rolled the 4% Spark and banked every win, breaking the once-per-member-per-UTC-day guarantee. Fix: `unlogPractice` NO LONGER clears the Spark claim (a paid day stays consumed across un-logs); and `maybeSpark` now RELEASES the claim only when the award does not land (claim-then-pay self-heal), so an unpaid day is not stranded as a tombstone. One roll per day, paid or not, never re-rollable.
2. **Welcome-Back un-log over-debit.** The grant was inserted `amount:0` and `welcomeBack` was set true regardless of whether the award paid; when it paid 0 (disabled config), un-log read the stored 0 as a "pre-feature" row and reversed the STATIC default (10 Zaps never awarded). Fix: `logPractice` now updates the grant to the real paid amount and sets `welcomeBack` ONLY when `res.amount > 0`; when 0 is paid it DELETES the grant. So a present grant always carries its real amount and un-log reverses exactly that.
3. **Daily-streak milestone double-pay (concurrency).** `recordPracticeStreak` is a lock-free read-modify-write on `profiles.meta`, and `logPractice` is not serialized per member, so two concurrent same-day logs could both see a milestone unpaid and both pay it. Fix: each milestone payout is gated by a `reward_grants` idempotency claim (`streak.milestone:{profile}:{day}`); only the run that wins the UNIQUE insert pays + banks the freeze + posts the feed line, and a failed award releases the claim. The claim (not `meta`) is the source of truth for "already paid", so a `meta` lost-update self-heals (a later log re-detects the milestone and the claim blocks the double-pay). The residual `meta` lost-update (a rarely-lost banked freeze) is documented and non-economic; a full atomic RPC is deferred.
4. **Solo-journey progress split-brain.** `adoptPlan` wrote `journey_plan_adoptions`, but the v2 progress reader (`getMemberJourneyProgress`), the daily next-step cron (`listEnrolledMemberIds`), and the solo drip anchor (`getSoloEnrollmentStart`) all read `journey_enrollments`, which only cohort Runs wrote. ADR-252 backfilled existing adoptions once but the live adopt path never wrote it, so every new solo adoption was invisible to progress + nudges and its phase-drip never locked. Fix: `adoptPlan` now ensures a SOLO enrollment (`journey_enrollments`, `run_id` null) exists, idempotent via the solo unique index, best-effort. `journey_plan_adoptions` stays (still read by content-signals / coop-pulse / the cron / the demo engine).
5. **Journey "write your own" slot was a dead block.** A composed/seeded practice block carries a title + body + Pillar but no `practice_id`, so the player mounts no timer / Log / Zaps for it. New `mintPracticeForBlockAction` mints a real `practices` row from the slot (author-owned, stamped to the Journey's Space, a private `draft`, out of the public library) and links the block; a "Make it real" button in the editor exposes it. The slot becomes a working, timer-carrying practice the author refines in the practice editor.

**Alternatives.** A full atomic streak RPC (deferred — disproportionate to the residual non-economic lost-update; the milestone claim closes the economic hole). Unify onto one enrollment table by deleting `journey_plan_adoptions` (rejected here — too many live readers; ensure both instead). Auto-mint every composed slot (rejected — noisy; the author opts in per slot).

**Consequences.** No migration. Behavior-additive; 62 practice/journey/streak/unlog tests green, tsc + eslint clean. Residual: the streak `meta` RMW can still rarely lose a banked freeze under true concurrency (documented, non-economic).

## ADR-781: The Theme + Template Protocol — one parent, scoped children, CI-enforced (site-wide look + content)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Design system / architecture · NO migration. Introduces `components/templates/page-hero.tsx`, `scripts/check-tokens.mjs`, `scripts/check-headers.mjs`, `docs/THEME-PROTOCOL.md`; routes `IndexTemplate` + `MarketHero` through `PageHero`; migrates the drifted header pages. Builds on the existing DAWN token layer (THEME.md), the module engine (PAGE-FRAMEWORK.md), and the MENU-CONTRACT (ADR-553).

**Context.** The owner asked for a "parent/child theme" capability: make site-wide style AND content changes from one place, every visible surface covered, with no drift. Research found the codebase already had single-source "parents" for three of five layers (Style = DAWN tokens; Layout = the module engine's global `'*'` scope; Menu = the MENU-CONTRACT catalogs) but (a) the header/**structure** layer had three divergent grammars (MarketHero with hardcoded hex, IndexTemplate `heroOverlay`, plain PageHeading) with no single source, (b) the "no hardcoded hex / no hand-rolled header" rules were **doc-only, not CI-enforced**, and (c) the **copy** layer had only a shallow, opt-in, non-cascading store.

**Decision.** Formalize the model as **five layers, each: one PARENT source → scoped CHILD overrides → a CI DRIFT-GUARD** (docs/THEME-PROTOCOL.md is the operating manual). Concretely in this phase (P1):
1. **One header band.** `PageHero` is the canonical overlay-on-cover header (the Business Spaces / Circles look the owner chose), token-clean (`from-ink` scrim + `text-on-ink`). `IndexTemplate`'s overlay hero and the commerce `MarketHero` both delegate to it, so the header look is a single-file edit; MarketHero's hardcoded `rgb(20 18 16 / …)` + `text-white` are retired.
2. **Enforcement (the "no drift" core).** `check:tokens` (no hardcoded hex / `rgb()` / `text-[Npx]` in `.tsx`/`.ts` outside an allowlist of token/theme files, maps, raster OG, and color pickers, with a `// token-ok:` escape hatch) and `check:headers` (no page-level `<h1>` in `app/(main)/**/page.tsx` outside a template, `// header-ok:` escape hatch) are HARD CI gates, alongside the existing `check:menu`.
3. **Migrate the drift.** The plain-heading manager pages (`/journeys/mine`, `/spaces/[slug]/{journeys,practices}`, `/network`) get the unified hero band + the template `back` slot (hand-rolled back-links removed); the in-app hand-rolled-`<h1>` pages (`admin/events/[id]`, `spaces/[slug]/podcasts/[showSlug]`, `people/[handle]`) move onto `DetailTemplate`/`AdminTemplate`; genuinely-special surfaces (chat panes) keep a `// header-ok:` hatch.

**Alternatives.** Keep MarketHero as a separate centered hero (rejected — the owner chose to converge on the overlay grammar; two divergent heroes defeat "one edit changes everything"). Warn-only lint (rejected — the owner chose hard-gate, so new drift is blocked immediately; existing violations are fixed or allow-listed, not grandfathered). A full DetailTemplate→PageHero unification now (deferred to P3 — the entity band is richer; P1 unifies the index/commerce heroes first).

**Consequences.** No migration; additive. Editing `PageHero` restyles every hero; editing a `globals.css` token restyles every color; the two new gates fail a PR that hand-rolls around either. Follow-ups (THEME-PROTOCOL §10): P2 the copy `site→section→page` cascade + `check:canon` over `.tsx`; P3 unify `DetailTemplate`'s band onto `PageHero` + finish the `rounded-2xl → rounded-card` token migration; P4 operator-facing theme controls with a theme-contract check.

## ADR-782: Space "Manage" console overhaul — de-duplicate, re-group, nest, and mark the plan tier (+ two billing fixes)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Space console IA + billing correctness · NO migration. Touches `lib/admin/modules/space-modules.ts` (catalog), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/manage/console.tsx` (render), `components/admin/modules/module-map.tsx` (rail inline body), `lib/spaces/surface-hrefs.ts`, `lib/pricing/plans.ts`, `lib/billing/space-plan-checkout.ts`, `lib/billing/pricing-keys.ts` + their tests. Extends the MENU-CONTRACT catalog (ADR-553), does not go around it.

**Context.** The `/spaces/[slug]/manage` console showed **three cards that all opened the same `/settings/basics` page** (Identity and Branding · Info and Connect · Settings), plus several near-duplicate rows (Email / Email design / Email style; CRM / Automation / Lead capture / Capture links / Shared; QR codes / Insights). A full survey (three read-only agents: catalog IA, settings sub-pages, freemium/premium model) confirmed the duplication and found the plan story was invisible on the console. It also surfaced two genuine billing defects and two non-defects.

**Decision.**
1. **Collapse the true duplicate.** The three shell cards become ONE `space.basics` **"Profile and Settings"** card (they already deep-linked to the one section-based `/settings/basics` form). `space.branding` + `space.settings` are removed from the catalog; `UNHIDEABLE_MODULE_IDS` shrinks to `basics/layout/danger`; the rail's inline body (`module-map`) stacks the three existing section editors so the rail keeps the full config in one surface.
2. **Nest, don't orphan.** A new `parent?: string` field folds sub-modules UNDER their parent CARD on the console: Automation / Lead capture / Capture links / Shared under **CRM**; Email design / Email style under **Email**; Scans and insights under **QR codes**. Each stays a first-class catalog row (still gated, still in the rail, still deep-linkable) — only the console consolidates it. `SpaceManageConsole` splits the manifest into top-level cards + `childrenByParent`, with an orphan-child fallback so nothing is ever unreachable.
3. **Re-group.** Console groups become **Setup** (Profile and Settings + Page) · **Content** (Practices / Journeys / Airwaves, via `groupForModule` + the repurposed `place` slot) · **Audience** · **Offerings & money** · **Reach** · **Plan and billing** · **Danger**. A console-only `CONSOLE_GROUP_LABEL` override refines the headers without mutating the shared `SPACE_GROUP_META` (the rail is untouched).
4. **Mark the tier.** A new `access?: 'included' | 'freemium' | 'premium'` field renders a token-clean BADGE on every card + a one-line legend. It is presentation only (gating stays in `gates.ts` / the function registry). During the open beta every tool is usable regardless of badge; the badge previews the post-launch model.
5. **Billing fix — the multi-page website was unsellable.** `spaceCanUseFullWebsite` reads the `space_full_website` entitlement directly (default-deny, deliberately off the billing-latent seam), but the key was in NO plan's entitlement set, so buying Business never granted it. Added `space_full_website` to `BUSINESS_DEPTH_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS` (so it rides the paid depth + the `BILLING_MANAGED_KEYS` union); free stays locked.
6. **Billing fix — Nonprofit was billed per-seat.** `catalogKeysForLoadout` marked `nonprofit_seat` `perSeat: true`, so checkout billed quantity×seats, contradicting ADR-590 + the catalog test (flat $29). Set it `perSeat: false`; corrected the stale per-seat comments.

**Non-defects (investigated, documented, no code change).**
- **`reporting` entitlement key** — NOT dangling: it is granted by the paid depth and read by `crm/capabilities.ts` (`spaceHasEntitlement('reporting') → 'crm.space.analytics'`). The capability simply has no live consumer yet — a RESERVED key for a future analytics gate, not a broken one. Left in place.
- **The two Journey publish levers** — NOT conflicting: `canPublishAnotherJourney` (free capped at 1 published) and `canListJourneyInLibrary` (public library requires paid) are complementary and exactly match the stated intent ("free spaces publish one; library listing is paid"). Kept as-is.

**Alternatives.** Physically delete the CRM/Email/QR sub-modules (rejected — it would orphan their routes and rail rows and churn the drift-guards; nesting keeps them wired). A separate console module catalog (rejected — MENU-CONTRACT violation; used a label-only override + `parent` field instead). Build real tabbed destination pages for the Email/CRM combines (deferred — the console nesting delivers the "one surface" IA now; a `?view=` tab merge on the pages is a safe follow-up).

**Consequences.** No migration; additive. `SPACE_MODULES` 28 → 26 rows; the console shows one card per surface with siblings nested and an Included/Freemium/Premium badge + legend. The rail auto-derives from the same catalog (fewer rows, unchanged grammar). A Business/Nonprofit Space now actually unlocks the multi-page website; Nonprofit bills a flat $29. Full suite green (5666 tests), tsc + eslint + `check:menu` + `check:tokens` clean.

## ADR-784: Space console access badges corrected to the real caps + the free-cap lever sublabel

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Space console pricing legibility · NO migration. Touches `lib/admin/modules/space-modules.ts` (`access` + new `freeNote`), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/manage/console.tsx` (render), `lib/pricing/feature-tiers.ts` + `docs/BUSINESS-MODEL-PLAN.md` (stale copy). Phase 1 of the Manage-hub overhaul; the category rebuild is a separate ADR.

**Context.** The Included/Freemium/Premium badges shipped in ADR-782 were hand-set and drifted from the real usage caps in `lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts`. The intended model (BUSINESS-MODEL-PLAN §1-2): every tool is ON for every Space; free is a capped usage state charged a 5% take-rate; a paid plan lifts caps to unlimited and buys the take-rate down to 3%. Booking (15/mo), Memberships (10 members/1 tier), Tickets (50/1 event), and Team (1 seat) are all capped on free yet were badged plain "Included"; Practices was badged "Freemium" with no cap constant behind it. The bare badge also hid the upgrade lever (the cap or the fee), which is the whole motivation.

**Decision.**
1. **Re-badge to the code caps:** Booking / Memberships / Tickets / Team → **Freemium**; Practices → **Included**. (CRM, Email, QR, Journeys, Shop, Automation already correct.)
2. **New `freeNote` field** on `SpaceModule` — a short free-tier lever string ("250 contacts free, then unlimited" · "5% take-rate, 3% on a paid plan") mirrored from the meters + `settings.ts` take_rate. The console renders it as a muted sublabel under each top-level card, so the card states *why* it is Freemium, not just *that* it is. Presentation only; never gates.
3. **Fix stale pricing copy:** BUSINESS-MODEL-PLAN §2 said the base was "~$19 founding / $29 list" (superseded ADR-472 number) → corrected to **$49 founding / $79 list** (ADR-590/591); `feature-tiers.ts` `tierPriceLabel` rendered Non Profit as "$29/seat/mo" → **flat "$29/mo"** (ADR-590, never per-seat).

**Consequences.** No migration; presentation only (gating unchanged in `gates.ts` / the function registry). A published **Billing & Pricing comparison chart** artifact accompanies this (tiers · the 5%→3% take-rate ladder · the per-feature matrix · the upgrade/downgrade path). Deferred to the phase-2 hub rebuild: a Premium marker for the multi-page website (no console module today) and wiring tips/tickets fees to honor the 5%→3% paying-state ladder (currently flat 3% in `tips.ts`/`tickets.ts`). Tests green, tsc + eslint + guards clean.

## ADR-785: The Space Manage hub — a four-category control hub opening on Resonance (CRM + inbox)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Space console IA rebuild · NO migration. Adds `lib/admin/modules/space-hub.ts` (sections) + `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/manage/{hub-search.tsx, settings/page.tsx}`; rewrites `manage/console.tsx` (render), `manage/manage-board.tsx`, `manage/page.tsx`; adds an `adminBar` pass-through to `DashboardTemplate`. Phase 2 of the Manage-hub overhaul (phase 1 = ADR-784 badges). Extends the MENU-CONTRACT catalog (ADR-553); introduces no parallel module list.

**Context.** The `/manage` console was a flat card-board of every surface at once. The owner directed a control-hub restructure: a category menu (like Classifieds) with the space's features grouped under four browse categories, opening on a relationship-first landing, with configuration pulled into a separate header-level surface.

**Decision.**
1. **Four browse categories** (`space-hub.ts` `sectionForModule`, a PURE grouping over the ONE catalog — not a parallel list): **Resonance · Marketing · Offerings & Money · Content & Programs**, rendered as `UnderlineTabs` (the Classifieds category-menu primitive) with `?section=` URL state; Resonance is the default landing.
   - Resonance = the CRM relationship + capture surfaces (CRM, lead capture, capture links, connections). Marketing = Audience + Reach combined (email trio, QR + scans, automation/drip). Offerings & Money = the commerce surfaces + Shop. Content & Programs = Practices / Journeys / Airwaves.
2. **Resonance opens on the live CRM** — the hub embeds the existing chrome-free `CrmBody` (cockpit view: health verdict, worklist, reciprocal-match connections) above the category's feature cards, so an operator lands on real work, not a config grid.
3. **Flat categories** — each category lists its features as top-level cards (no nested sub-menus); the ADR-782 `parent` nesting is not used inside a category space.
4. **Profile & Settings is a header-level surface** (`/manage/settings`, `FocusTemplate` + `SpaceSettingsSurface`), reached from a button in the hub header — NOT a browse tab. It holds identity/brand/visibility (basics) + **Team** + **Reviews** + **Plan & usage** + **Danger zone** (owner directive).
5. **Header + shell changes:** the stat row moves into the header (tight, right of the identity) with a Mode chip + the Profile & Settings button; a **Space search bar** (`HubSearch`, a client-side finder over every tool) sits under the header rule; the on-page "Settings" admin bar is turned off (`DashboardTemplate adminBar={false}`); the **Page** module is dropped from the hub (page editing lives on the admin rail now).

**Alternatives.** A fifth "Profile & Settings" tab (rejected — the owner scoped exactly four browse categories; settings is configuration, not daily operation, so it lives in the header). Rebuild the CRM inline instead of embedding `CrmBody` (rejected — `CrmBody` is already the self-gating embeddable body used by the profile panel; reuse over rebuild). A server-backed space search (deferred — the client-side tool finder ships now; full member/content search is a follow-up).

**Consequences.** No migration. The rail still auto-derives from the same catalog (unchanged). Every service keeps an admin surface (a hub test asserts no module is orphaned: each maps to a category or the settings surface, or is the explicitly-excluded Page module). Deferred follow-ups: the net-new **Space Inbox** compose (a space-gated reply action + `InboxWorkspace` injection — the read path `listInboxThreads({spaceId})` already exists); a Premium badge for the multi-page website; wiring tips/tickets fees to the 5%→3% ladder. Full suite green (5678 tests), tsc + eslint + `check:menu`/`check:tokens`/`check:headers` clean.

## ADR-786: The Space Inbox + the ticket take-rate ladder

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Space Resonance completion + billing correctness · NO migration. Adds `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/crm/inbox/page.tsx` + `crm/inbox-actions.ts`, a `space.inbox` module, and a `sendReply` prop on `InboxWorkspace`; ladders space-hosted event tickets in `lib/billing/tickets.ts`. The follow-up to ADR-784/785 (the two items those ADRs deferred).

**Context.** The Manage hub's Resonance category opened on the CRM but had no space-scoped **Inbox** (only the platform-staff `/admin/crm/inbox` existed), and **event tickets** charged a flat platform fee instead of honoring the 5%→3% paying-state take-rate ladder that space memberships + the storefront already use.

**Decision.**
1. **Space Inbox.** The inbox data layer already accepts a `spaceId` (`listInboxThreads({ spaceId })`), and `InboxWorkspace` was coupled to the admin reply action. We (a) added an injectable `sendReply` prop to `InboxWorkspace` (default = the admin action), (b) built `sendSpaceInboxReplyAction(slug, input)` — the space-manager-gated sibling of the admin action, with a **tenancy check** (the contact must belong to this space) and the SAME gated send pipeline (`resolveSendGate → enqueueEmail → recordContactInteraction`), and (c) added `/spaces/[slug]/crm/inbox` (threads scoped to the space, the workspace bound to the space action) surfaced as an **Inbox** module in the Resonance category. So Resonance is now the CRM **and** the inbox — people + communication.
2. **Ticket take-rate ladder.** A **space-hosted** event's tickets now compute the platform fee via `spaceTakeRateCents(gross, space.plan, spaceIsPaying(space_id))` (5% free → 3% paid), the same lever as memberships + the storefront. A **personal** event (no owning space / the root space) keeps the flat fee. **Tips stay flat** — a tip is a profile→profile gratuity with no space seller, so the ladder does not apply (documented in `tips.ts` + `fees.ts`).

**Alternatives.** Add an `'inbox'` CRM view tab (rejected — it churns the `CrmView` union + the board's `?view=` validation; a sibling `/crm/inbox` route + a Resonance module is cleaner and reuses the admin workspace). Fork `InboxWorkspace` for the space (rejected — one injected `sendReply` prop serves both). Ladder tips (rejected — no space seller; flat is correct).

**Consequences.** No migration. Resonance is complete (CRM + inbox); a free space now pays the correct 5% on space-hosted tickets (was 3%, under-charging free / removing the upgrade incentive) — latent while billing is off. Full suite green (5678 tests), tsc + eslint + `check:menu`/`check:tokens`/`check:headers` clean.

## ADR-787: The Space Resonance tab shows the real Resonance CRM roster (not the CRM cockpit)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Corrects ADR-785 · NO migration. Adds `components/spaces/crm/space-member-viewer.tsx` + `loadSpaceMemberDetail`; scopes `loadMemberSummaries` with a `spaceId`.

**Context.** ADR-785 made Resonance the hub's landing but embedded the space CRM **cockpit** (`CrmBody activeView="cockpit"` — the health/worklist board). The owner's actual spec (from the original request) was the **admin Resonance CRM** view — the master-detail `MemberViewer` roster ("pick a member, see everything about them inline"), scoped to the space. The cockpit was the wrong component.

**Decision.** Render the SAME `MemberViewer` the admin Resonance CRM uses, scoped to the space:
1. `loadMemberSummaries(filter, { spaceId })` passes the space scope through to `listMembersByFilter` (which already supports it), so the roster reads this space's reachable scored members.
2. `loadSpaceMemberDetail(slug, profileId)` is the space-manager path to the rich inline detail — gated on **space-manage** AND a **TENANCY check** (the member must be in this space's roster, so a manager can never open an arbitrary platform member by id). It reuses the SAME `buildMemberDetail` builder the admin `loadMemberDetail` uses (extracted as a private helper; the admin loader is unchanged externally).
3. `SpaceMemberViewer` mounts `MemberViewer` with the space roster + the slug-bound detail loader; `manage-board` embeds it on the Resonance section instead of `CrmBody`.

**Consequences.** No migration. The space Resonance tab now reads identically to the admin Resonance CRM, scoped + gated to the space. The CRM board (`/crm`, People/Pipeline/Cockpit/Import) is unchanged and still linked. Security: the inline detail is tenancy-checked, so a space owner sees only their own space's members. Full suite green (5678), tsc + eslint + guards clean. (Mobile responsiveness across the hub + site is a separate follow-up sweep.)

## ADR-788: Profile & Settings becomes a real hub tab, reversing ADR-785 §4

**Status:** Accepted. Reverses [ADR-785](DECISIONS.md) §4 and the alternative ADR-785 explicitly rejected. Written 2026-08-04 from the shipped code — cited by `lib/admin/modules/space-hub.ts` and twice in its test, but never recorded, so ADR-785 §4 has been the only ledger entry on the subject while stating the opposite of what ships.

**Context.** ADR-785 scoped the Space Manage hub to **four** browse categories and put configuration in the header: *"Profile & Settings is a header-level surface… reached from a button in the hub header — NOT a browse tab."* Its Alternatives paragraph rejected precisely this change: *"A fifth 'Profile & Settings' tab (rejected — the owner scoped exactly four browse categories; settings is configuration, not daily operation, so it lives in the header)."*

That reasoning is sound about *daily operation* and wrong about *reach*. It buried **Plan & Billing**, **Team** and **Reviews** behind a header button — a control an operator hits when money or access is involved, which is exactly when a second hop is most expensive.

**Decision.** `Profile & Settings` becomes a real entry in `SPACE_HUB_SECTIONS`, trailing the browse tabs rather than leading them, so the ordering still says "this is configuration, not daily operation" while the reach is one tap. `SpaceHubSection` is now six keys; `asHubSection` accepts `'settings'` as a `?section=` value; the tab body renders the **same** `SpaceSettingsSurface` the standalone route uses, so there is one definition of the settings surface and no forked copy.

**Consequences.** The standalone `/manage/settings` route survives and still works — this adds a way in, it does not remove one. ⚠️ Two in-code comments still describe the ADR-785 world and are now counter-evidence to their own callers: `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/manage/settings/page.tsx` and the `SpaceSettingsSurface` note in `console.tsx` both say "header-level… NOT one of the four browse categories". Corrected in the same change that wrote this record. ⚠️ ADR-785 §4 and its Alternatives paragraph are now **stale where they are strongest** — a superseded decision that reads as current is worse than one that reads as old, which is the whole reason this entry exists.

## ADR-789: The Space Resonance tab IS the Resonance CRM (exact admin composition, scoped)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-18) · Corrects ADR-785/787 · NO migration. Adds `components/spaces/crm/{space-crm-stats,space-resonance-crm}.tsx`; the Resonance hub tab now renders the full CRM surface instead of feature cards.

**Context.** The owner's spec for the space Resonance tab was "EXACTLY the layout for the main Resonance CRM" (`/admin/crm`): the header + Import contacts, the four health stat cards, and the master-detail member viewer. ADR-787 wired the member viewer but left the hub feature-card grid on the tab; it did not replicate the stat row / header / import, so it did not read as the Resonance CRM.

**Decision.** The Resonance tab renders `SpaceResonanceCrm` — the SAME composition as the admin CRM page, scoped to the space: the "Resonance CRM" header + "Pick a member to see everything about them, inline" + `ImportContactsButton target={{ kind: 'space', spaceId }}`, then `SpaceCrmHealthStatRow` (Members / Active this week / At risk / Resonance Health, the same cards + tones, read from `getSpaceHealth(spaceId)` instead of `getPlatformHealth`), then the `MemberViewer` master-detail (via `loadMemberSummaries({ spaceId })` + the tenancy-gated `loadSpaceMemberDetail`). The hub feature-card grid + access legend no longer render on Resonance.

**Consequences.** No migration. The space Resonance tab reads pixel-for-composition identical to the admin Resonance CRM, every function the same component, scoped + gated to the space. Follow-ups still open (owner directive): move the admin CRM tab menu under its search bar; replicate the admin Marketing console on the space Marketing tab with a classifieds-style client-side pill sub-nav (Email / Email design / Email style / QR codes / Scans / Automation) and the "New email" popup composer (upgraded editor). Full suite green, tsc + eslint + guards clean.

## ADR-790: The admin search bar moves ABOVE the world sub-nav

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-19). Owner directive, recorded in [ADR-789](DECISIONS.md) Consequences as an open follow-up: *"move the admin CRM tab menu under its search bar"*. [ADR-791](DECISIONS.md)'s Status line vouches for it by name — *"ADR-790 was the admin search-above-menu swap"* — which is the only reason the number resolves at all. Written 2026-08-04 from `app/(main)/admin/layout.tsx`.

**Context.** ADR-789's Consequences left two owner follow-ups open. This is the first; ADR-791 (the Space Marketing tab as the scoped CRM Marketing page) is the second, and it shipped with its record while this one did not.

The admin chrome had absorbed the world sub-nav into a single sticky opaque band so page content scrolls cleanly underneath it — the fix for an older bug where a transparent gap above the input let content bleed through. Within that band the sub-nav row sat on top and the search bar below it.

**Decision.** Swap them: `AdminSearchBar` renders first, `AdminSubNav` second, both still inside the one sticky band pinned under the 3.5rem header at every breakpoint. Every world — the Resonance CRM most of all — now reads **"search, then the tab menu under it."**

The band itself is unchanged. This is an ordering decision inside existing chrome, not a re-layout, which is why it is a small entry: the expensive part (one opaque sticky container, no bleed-through) was ADR-789's.

**Consequences.** ⚠️ The container's own rationale comment still describes the pre-swap order — "the sub-nav text-link row on TOP and the Ask-Vera/search bar below" — eight lines above the ADR-790 comment that contradicts it, and above JSX that contradicts both. Corrected in the same change that wrote this record. The lesson generalises: a swap that touches two adjacent lines is exactly the kind of change whose *comments* go stale, because nobody re-reads the paragraph above the diff.

## ADR-791: The Space Marketing tab IS the CRM Marketing page (scoped) behind a no-reload pill sub-nav

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-19) · Completes the ADR-789 follow-up (ADR-790 was the admin search-above-menu swap) · NO migration. Adds `components/spaces/marketing/{space-marketing,space-marketing-dashboard,space-email-compose-popup,space-send-panel,marketing-pills}.tsx`; extends `lib/spaces/email-drafts.ts` (block-email send + audience + discard-if-empty); adds the `animate-panel-slide` utility.

**Context.** The owner's spec for the space Marketing tab was "EXACTLY the layout for the main Marketing tab, every function the same," plus: replace the marketing feature cards with a classifieds-style pill sub-nav that swaps **in place** (no reload, content slides over), and route **all** email editing through the admin "New email" popup composer with the upgraded on-canvas editor. The hub tab previously rendered the generic feature-card grid, and the space block-email editor (ADR from the Email-in-the-Business-CRM build) only test-sent to self.

**Decision.** The Marketing tab renders `SpaceMarketing`: a `MarketingPills` client sub-nav (the `MarketplaceFacets` rounded-pill shape, but state-swapped, not linked) over the gated marketing modules in catalog order (`sectionForModule === 'marketing'`), so only a surface the console would have shown becomes a pill. The **Email** pill is `SpaceMarketingDashboard` — the SAME composition as `/admin/crm/marketing`, scoped: an email-performance strip (`getSpaceEmailStats`), "Everything you send" (search + the draft list), and one "New email" button that opens `SpaceEmailComposePopup`. That popup is the space twin of `MarketingComposePopup`: the SAME `EmailEditorPane` (`arrangement="canvas"`, the upgraded editor) with the Space's own `saveSpaceEmailDraft` / `sendSpaceTestEmail` / `spaceEmailColors` injected, and a `SpaceSendPanel` right rail (the shared `AudiencePicker` + a double-confirmed Send). The remaining pills embed the existing self-gating surfaces (Email design → `SpaceEmailWorkspace`, Email style → `EmailStyleEditor`, QR codes / Scans → `QrBody`, Automation → `AutomationBody`), each streamed behind its own `Suspense`. Real block-email SEND reuses the one anti-spam delivery core every Space campaign uses (`sendSpaceCampaign` in `lib/spaces/email`): `sendSpaceEmailDraft` compiles `block_json` to branded HTML with a per-recipient unsubscribe placeholder, resolves the audience through the SAME `resolveAudience` the live count uses, hands it to the seam (kill-switch, per-Space daily cap, consent + suppression, RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe, `outreach_sends` ledger), then stamps the row sent. `discardSpaceEmailDraftIfEmpty` cleans up a pristine "New email" left unedited so the list never fills with blanks; `EmailEnableCard` leads the dashboard when the Space kill-switch is off.

**Consequences.** No migration, no forked send path (one delivery core, one audience resolver, so the confirmed count is the sent count). The space Marketing tab reads composition-identical to the admin CRM Marketing page, scoped + gated to the space, and its sub-surfaces are one no-reload pill away. Scheduling a block draft is not wired (send-now only for block emails; the plain-text composer keeps its scheduled-send cron); the QR/Scans pills both render `QrBody` (same surface, two anchors) so each executes server-side on load. Full guards + tsc + eslint clean.

## ADR-792: Embeddable elements — one canonical element, invoked by key, configured once (role-gated)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-19) · Migration `20261180000000_element_settings.sql` **APPLIED to prod 2026-07-19** (Frequency Community; table live, RLS enabled with no client policies = deny-all, the two partial-unique indexes present, 0 rows so all elements still fail-safe to registry defaults until an operator sets config). Adds `lib/elements/{registry,config,store}.ts`, the `/admin/elements` console, and wires the Loom picker as the first citizen. Now also: the `header` + `qr-studio` elements (ADR-793) and the config resolvers. Full spec: `docs/EMBEDDABLE-ELEMENTS.md`.

**Context.** Reusable in-product features (the Loom picker, QR Studio, the Email editor popup, the Resonance CRM board) were wired per surface, so "the same" element drifted between pages and its rules lived in code, edited instance by instance. The owner's directive: every reusable element should be its own app — one canonical implementation, mounted by key on any page with no divergence, whose rules are edited in ONE master and apply site-wide, with functions/settings gated by role.

**Decision.** Three parts. (1) One canonical implementation per element (already true for the Loom picker). (2) An element registry (`lib/elements/registry.ts`, `ELEMENTS`) mapping an `ElementKey` to its features (each a toggle/choice with a `defaultMinRole`) — the extension of the admin MENU-CONTRACT from menu items to embeddable UI. (3) One generic `element_settings` table (`element_key`, nullable `space_id` = platform master vs per-space override, `config` jsonb of `{ settings, roles }`); resolution is pure + fail-safe (`defaults <- master <- space`, `lib/elements/config.ts`), and role gating resolves BY CONTEXT (SpaceRole in a space, community_role + staff globally) via the existing `atLeastRole` ladder — no second permission system. The Loom picker reads its resolved, role-gated config (tabs / AI-Create / default-scope) at runtime; a staff `/admin/elements` console edits each element's master settings + role gates, applied site-wide. Missing table/row falls back to registry defaults, so the app is correct before the migration applies.

**Consequences.** New elements start on the framework by definition; existing ones adopt it incrementally (Loom done; QR Studio / Email editor / CRM board next, each: ensure one component, add a registry row, move rules to `element_settings`, mount via the registry). No forked components, no per-page rule edits. The migration is written but NOT applied (one shared DB); code fail-safes to defaults until it lands. tsc + eslint (0 errors) + 5678 tests + build compile/type-check all green.

## ADR-793: The page header/hero is an embeddable element — one component, layout variants, shared editing functions

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-19) · Builds on ADR-792. Extends `components/templates/page-hero.tsx` with layout variants, registers `'header'` in the elements registry, and converts the two "disliked" headers (Journeys, personal profiles) to it. Full spec: `docs/EMBEDDABLE-ELEMENTS.md` + `docs/PAGE-FRAMEWORK.md` §8.

**Context.** The owner liked the Marketplace and Business/Spaces headers (an immersive cover with the title/eyebrow overlaid on the ink scrim) but disliked the personal-profile and Journey headers (a plain cover band with the identity stranded in a plain lockup below it). The ask: a standardized header system with a few LAYOUTS per section but the SAME editing functions (height, focal point, links, overlay) site-wide — and make it one of the embeddable "apps."

**Decision.** `PageHero` is already the ONE canonical header band (Marketplace, Spaces, Circles, the directory heroes all render it). We made it the render side of a `header` element rather than forking a second header: (1) it gains a `variant` prop — `overlay` (the shipped centered look, unchanged default), `identity` (cover + scrim with the lockup anchored bottom-left and an optional leading chip: a Journey icon, a profile avatar), and `minimal` (cover only) — plus a `size` ladder (short/standard/large/tall), a `leading` slot, and a `dimmed` flag. Every existing caller keeps `overlay`/default, so nothing regresses. (2) `'header'` is registered in `lib/elements/registry.ts` with its role-gated FEATURES (layout, height, focal point, header links, darken-cover) so its editing functions are declared ONCE and gated by role via the ADR-792 config layer; a staff `/admin/elements` row tunes the master. The header is server-rendered (the `<h1>` stays server-side for SEO), so it is registered for config/role-gating but NOT in the client component map — templates import the canonical `PageHero` directly, which IS the one mount (the drift guard allows a registered-but-not-client-mounted element). (3) Journeys and personal profiles now render the `identity` variant: the cover + icon/avatar + name + one-line summary overlaid immersively, with the interactive meta (badges, links, stat chips, enroll/manage, bio, actions) kept in a light `band` below so those controls keep their normal contrast and styling.

**Consequences.** One header component with per-section layouts and one set of editing functions; the two disliked headers now match the liked ones. `ProfileCover` is superseded on the personal profile (left in place for any future reuse). Full per-surface config resolution (reading `element_settings` to toggle each header's controls) and folding the two scattered height ladders (`lib/spaces/hero-config.ts`, `lib/events/hero-height.ts`) into the element are the natural follow-ups (APPS-CONVERSION-PLAN Phase 2/4). tsc + eslint (0 errors) + 5690 tests + build compile/type-check all green; `check:elements` + the drift guard green.

## ADR-794: One header editor — shared image field, three overlay styles, context-scoped Loom

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-19) · Builds on ADR-792/793. Adds `components/ui/header-image-field.tsx`, three PageHero overlay styles, a `scopeKey` on the Loom picker, an avatar focus selector, and the Journey header logo. Migration `20261183000000_journey_plans_logo_image.sql` **APPLIED to prod**. Full spec: `docs/EMBEDDABLE-ELEMENTS.md`.

**Context.** The header element unified the RENDER (ADR-793) but each surface still had its own EDITOR: the Space rail had the refined single-image control (focal picker on top of the cover, Replace/Remove), profiles used a bespoke canvas drag+zoom cropper, and Journeys used a bare upload box. The Loom picker also opened in the side rail and listed every operated Space's images rather than the one being edited. The owner's directives: every header editor should offer the same name/tagline/profile-image/header-image controls using the refined Space pattern; the Loom picker must open full-screen and show only the current space/profile/page's library; profile images need a drag-to-crop focus selector; Journeys need cover + logo image + icon; and all headers must share one overlay treatment with three styles.

**Decision.** (1) The refined Space cover control is extracted to a shared `HeaderImageField` (focal-picker preview + Replace/Remove) that funnels every pick — empty state and Replace alike — through the ONE Loom picker. Space, Profile, and Journey editors all use it. (2) The Loom picker gains an optional `scopeKey` ('mine' or a Space id) that locks it to one authorized scope via a new `loomScope` server action (hides the scope switcher, loads only that library); it already opens centered full-screen. Editors pass `spaceId` (Spaces) or `'mine'` (person/journey). (3) `PageHero` overlay is now `overlayStyle` = `none` | `shadow` (full ink scrim, color-pickable, dark default) | `fade` (color faded up from the bottom, page-background default), resolved by `resolveHeaderElement` and declared as a role-gated registry feature; the deprecated `overlay` boolean maps forward. All header buttons use the shared `HERO_ACTION_CLASS`. (4) The profile avatar gains a drag-to-crop focus selector that BAKES the chosen crop into the saved 512² JPEG (`resizeToJpeg` offset by the focal), so it needs no schema and no per-surface render wiring. (5) Journeys carry a header logo image (new `journey_plans.logo_image` column) rendered as the header's leading chip beside the icon, alongside the cover + icon. The bespoke profile canvas cropper (`header-editor.tsx`) is deleted.

**Consequences.** One editor pattern and one Loom picker across every header; an editor's image picker shows only its own context's library. Overlay treatment is a single role-gated choice site-wide. Avatar cropping is self-contained (no avatar-focal column, no changes to the dozens of avatar surfaces). tsc + eslint (0 errors) + 5705 tests + `check:tokens/headers/elements/menu` all green; build compiles/type-checks (the only build failure is the pre-existing env-gated `/discover/cities/[citySlug]` page-data step in the sandbox).

## ADR-795: The space Resonance roster ranks by CONTACT COMPLETENESS by default (rich rows over bare imports)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Adds `lib/crm/completeness.ts` (+ tests), extends the space Resonance roster reader (`lib/spaces/resonance-roster.ts`) and the shared member mapper (`app/(main)/admin/crm/member-summaries.ts`) with a `completeness` sort signal, adds a "Most complete" sort option, and defaults the space Community Resonance roster to it. No schema change.

**Context.** After a CSV import of ~500 contacts, the space Community Resonance roster (ADR-789) sorted newest-first ("Recent"), so the bare email-only rows a spreadsheet drops in buried the contacts the owner had actually filled out (name, phone, company, notes). The reader only selected `email/display_name/consent/created_at/profile_id`, so there was no completeness signal to rank on.

**Decision.** A pure, weighted completeness scorer (`completenessScore`) reads the presence flags that make a row a real, rich person: a genuine display name (not the email local-part — `isRealName`), the imported extras that live in `contacts.meta` (phone/company/title/city/website/tags/notes/custom, the exact keys `lib/crm/import/commit.ts` writes), whether the row is stitched to a real member profile, an avatar, and any engagement signal. Identity (name / membership / phone / company) dominates the weights; the softer fields add polish. The roster reader computes the score into each row's `sortValues.completeness` (contacts from `meta`, members from name/avatar/activity), a "Most complete" `SortOption` is added to the shared `MEMBER_SORT_OPTIONS`, and the space roster passes `sort={{ key: 'completeness', direction: 'desc' }}` so it is the DEFAULT there. Ties fall back to the roster's newest-first input order (the sort is stable).

**Consequences.** In a space CRM the contacts you actually filled out (and your real members) surface at the top; the email-only imports sink. The admin Resonance CRM merely gains "Most complete" as a selectable sort (its default stays "Recent"), so nothing regresses there. The scorer is pure/framework-free and unit-tested; exact weights are not load-bearing (only the ordering they induce). tsc + eslint (0 errors) + 5738 tests all green.

## ADR-796: Space management redesign — one dashboard + four pillars, member-record spine, essential-up-front standard

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Consolidation plan of record: `docs/SPACE-MANAGEMENT-REDESIGN.md`. Basis: a 9-agent code survey of the current Space `/manage` area + two deep-research passes (competitor IA across Skool/Circle/Mighty Networks/Kajabi/Nas.io/GoHighLevel/HubSpot/Kit; and CRM/marketing/funnel feature-adoption). Phased build begins with Phase 0 (this ADR governs the whole sequence).

**Context.** The Space management area is five flat tabs over ~30 modules (`SPACE_MODULES`): Resonance and Marketing are real; Offerings & Money, Content & Programs, and Profile & Settings are shells; there is no dashboard/home. Communication is siloed at the read layer (a unified `contact_interactions` log exists but the Space surfaces read only the `'contact'` slice, so DMs/SMS/attendance/adoption never surface on the member); the automation rule builder ships broken; "funnel"/"sequence"/"journey" each name 3+ unrelated systems; and most growth tooling (funnels, attribution, referrals, flyers, A/B links) is platform-only. Research is unambiguous: complexity — not missing features — kills adoption (~50% of CRM rollouts fail, >60% from complexity; lightweight tools +34% adoption), the market has converged on a person-record spine + one inbox + a dashboard home, and the highest-value email is a broadcast plus 2–3 templates, not a blank-canvas builder.

**Decision.** Redesign the Space admin around **one home + four pillars + a demoted Settings**, on three binding principles that apply to the ENTIRE business-admin section: (1) the **member record is the spine and the profile IS the inbox** — one cross-channel timeline per person with a composer in place; (2) **essential up front, advanced off by default** — each area shows primary features immediately and hides advanced ones OFF until activated from that area's **control board** (progressive disclosure, ≤2 levels); (3) **Dashboard is the login home** — a command center with actionable metrics + inline CTAs.
