Approved calls: **(A)** fold Marketing INTO Resonance as "Reach" (no separate tab); **(B)** the sales pipeline is optional and OFF by default; **(C)** CUT the blank-canvas automation builder (broken + named bloat) for 2–3 pre-built templates; **(D)** log EVERY communication/activity against the member (email, texts, site messages/DMs, event attendance, program adoption, transactional notifications) by adding `recordContactInteraction` hooks + reading via the person-stitch (`listInteractionsForPerson`); **(E)** bring crew growth tools (flyer/A-B/QR) + per-Space attribution down to Space scope. The control-board standard reuses the locked `SPACE_MODULES` + Module Manager (MENU-CONTRACT / ADR-553 stays intact — a data + presentation change, not a parallel registry).

**Consequences.** Phased build (Phase 0 foundation → 1 Dashboard+Comms → 2 Reach → 3 Offerings & Money → 4 Content & Programs → 5 Settings demotion). Most Phase-0/1 plumbing already exists (the log spine, the stitcher, threaded inbox, the send-and-log pipeline), so the flagship "communications center" is largely composition. Cutting the automation builder removes broken code; making the pipeline optional matches real adoption. Each phase ships as its own reviewable PR under this ADR.

## ADR-797: Automation templates instantiate a real sequence + a direct pointer-rule; the SEQUENCE toggle is the switch

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Implements ADR-796 Decision C (Phase 2, Reach). Code: `lib/spaces/automation-types.ts` (`SPACE_AUTOMATION_TEMPLATES` + `SpaceAutomationTemplate`), `lib/spaces/automation.ts` (`instantiateAutomationTemplate` / `automationTemplateById`), `lib/spaces/automation-actions.ts` (wrapper), `components/spaces/automation/templates-panel.tsx`, mounted in the automation body.

**Context.** ADR-796 cut the blank-canvas Rules builder for 2-3 pre-built templates. The auto-enroll runtime already exists (`member.joined` → `fireSpaceTrigger` → `enrollContactInSequence` → drip cron); the only missing link for "new member → welcome sequence" was a `space_automation_rules` row whose `action_config.sequenceId` points at a drip sequence. Two constraints shaped the build: (1) `createSpaceRule` → `validateRule` REQUIRES an email subject + body (it validates a one-shot `email_audience` rule) and rejects a sequence-pointer rule; (2) the Rules panel was retired, so the operator has no UI to see or toggle a rule.

**Decision.** A template instantiates a **real drip sequence created OFF** (the operator reviews the steps first) plus its ordered steps; a **triggered** template (welcome, onboarding → `member.joined`) also writes an **ENABLED rule directly to the table** (bypassing `createSpaceRule`) with `action_config = { sequenceId }`, which the dispatcher reads via `ruleSequenceId`. The **sequence's `enabled` flag is the operator's single on/off switch**: `enrollContactInSequence` no-ops on a disabled sequence, so even with the rule enabled nothing enrolls until the operator turns the sequence ON in the (visible) Sequences panel. Re-engage has `triggerEvent: null` (no "inactive" event exists) → manual Start over a chosen audience. Instantiation is idempotent by sequence name (a template already added is not added twice). Template copy obeys the voice canon (no em/en dashes, no narrating the reader's feelings), enforced by a unit test.

**Consequences.** New-member welcome/onboarding auto-fire for members who are **consenting contacts** (the drip send seam gates on per-recipient consent + suppression, so an unconsented or non-contact member is enrolled-then-skipped, or not resolved at all). Reaching a brand-new **direct tier joiner** additionally needs (a) materializing a space-scoped contact from the member profile on `member.joined`, and (b) a compliance decision on whether a join implies marketing consent — deferred as a follow-up, NOT auto-granted here. This keeps the templates correctly wired to the existing runtime + consent model without a rushed consent write.

> **Follow-up SHIPPED (2026-07-21):** the owner decided a join IS opt-in, so `member.joined` now materializes a space-scoped **subscribed** contact by email via `ensureSpaceMemberContact` (`lib/crm/lead-capture.ts`), honoring opt-out permanence (a prior `unsubscribed` or a Space suppression is never re-subscribed), and fires the trigger with that `contactId`. The never-wired per-topic marketing opt-down (`isContactTopicMuted`) was also connected into the marketing send loop (`lib/spaces/email.ts`). See the consent hardening in the same change.

## ADR-798: The space comms center logs deliberate 1:1 touches, NOT broadcasts or platform DMs (scope of ADR-796 Decision D)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Owner decision. Refines ADR-796 Decision D ("log every communication/activity against the member").

**Context.** A comms-coverage audit found that space **broadcasts** (the event/Circle dispatch fan-out: `fanOutEventPush` + `fanOutEventSms` in `lib/events/dispatch.ts`) and member↔operator **in-app DMs** (`app/(main)/messages/actions.ts`, threaded by `lib/crm/inbox.ts`) do not record a per-member touch on the space timeline / CRM inbox. Both cross scopes: the dispatch fan-out is **event/Circle-scoped** (recipients are profile ids; a broadcast has no single space to attribute to without resolving event→owning-space + profile→space-contact per recipient), and the in-app DM system is **platform friend-messaging** with no `space_id` (its touches are `subjectKind:'profile'`, which the CRM inbox — keyed on `subjectKind:'contact'` — does not thread).

**Decision.** These stay **UNLOGGED, by design.** The member timeline is for the deliberate, 1:1, space-attributable communications an operator has with a member — email sends + the Resend engagement webhook, RSVP / membership-join / enrollment / check-in / booking and their cancellations, all stamped with `space_id` — kept as signal, not a firehose. High-volume broadcasts and platform-wide friend DMs are excluded so the timeline and the Home activity feed stay meaningful. Space-originated SMS today exists only as the broadcast path (`fanOutEventSms`), so it is covered by this same exclusion; a genuinely 1:1 space→member SMS channel does not exist yet and would be reconsidered on its own merits if it ships.

**Consequences.** A future audit that flags "broadcast push / SMS or in-app DM records no space touch" should treat it as **intended scope, not a bug**. If the product later wants broadcasts on the timeline, the work is a deliberate build (resolve event→space + profile→contact, or add a space_id to the dispatch/SMS payloads), not a one-line logging call.

## ADR-799: Operator seats (per-seat billing) and collaborator spaces (space↔space) are two different systems

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Owner decisions. Full plan of record: `docs/SPACE-COLLABORATION-AND-SEATS.md`.

**Context.** An operator asked for two capabilities that sound related but are architecturally distinct: (A) adding extra **operators** who manage a space's back end for an additional paid seat, and (B) hosting **collaborator spaces** — separate businesses that operate inside a venue/event (Royal Temple, a salon, a healing center: shared physical space, separate businesses). A prior attempt (ADR-465) to wire `spaces.seat_quantity` from subscription items was reverted because it rode the RETIRED per-seat pricing (every flat tier is `perSeat:false`), so it zeroed Business seats and arbitrarily +1'd nonprofit. This ADR sets the correct model for both.

**Decision.**
- **(A) Operator seats — a per-seat add-on on paid plans.** The seat counting + enforcement already exists (`lib/spaces/seats.ts`, gated on `billingLive()`); the owner's seat is free (`BASE_SEAT_ALLOWANCE = 1`), each extra operator (editor/moderator/admin) is a flat `$/seat/mo`. Build the missing billing loop: a REAL per-seat catalog item `operator_seat` (`perSeat:true`), included in `catalogKeysForLoadout` when the seat count > 0, with `reconcileSpacePlanSubscription` writing `spaces.seat_quantity` back from THAT item's quantity (the correct version of the reverted ADR-465), plus an add/remove-seat action wired to the existing `SeatCounter`. The price is an owner-set amount; ships with a placeholder until the Stripe price is synced.
- **(B) Collaborator spaces — a new `space_collaborations` relationship.** Greenfield (no space↔space link exists today; only `space_follows`). Mirror the `event_placement_requests` request→steward-approve shape. **Either side initiates, the other's owner/admin approves.** **Free to host** (the collaborator pays for their own space). A host is a `business` space (no new `SpaceType`). Phased: B1 relationship + profile listing/cross-link; B2 collaborator events on the host venue page; B3 shared venue calendar/booking (the "full shared operations" target).
- **(C) Topic mutes.** Space emails become topic-tagged (Marketing / Event update / Announcement) in the composer, gated per-topic on `isContactTopicMuted` (replacing the hardcoded `marketing`), honoring the three preference-center toggles for the contact-scoped path without the cross-scope broadcast work ADR-798 excluded.

Both A and B management surfaces live under the console's **Profile & Settings** (owner directive). Each phase ships as its own reviewable PR; the money- (A) and tenancy- (B) sensitive steps get an adversarial verify pass before merge.

> **Follow-up SHIPPED — Feature C (topic-tagged emails, 2026-07-21).** Space campaigns now carry a `topic` (`campaigns.topic`, migration `20261194000000`, `text not null default 'marketing' check in marketing/events/dispatches`). The composer (`components/spaces/email/composer-shell.tsx`) offers a topic selector labeled **Marketing / Event update / Announcement**, mapping onto the existing `CONTACT_TOPICS` keys `marketing / events / dispatches` (no new keys). The topic threads composer → `CampaignInput` → `campaigns.ts` (persist) → `sendViaSeam` / the scheduled cron (`campaigns-send-due.ts`) → `deliverSpaceCampaign` (`lib/spaces/email.ts`), where the per-recipient gate now reads `isContactTopicMuted({..., topic: sendTopic})` instead of the hardcoded `'marketing'`. `normalizeEmailTopic` defaults an absent/legacy/drip topic to `marketing`, so every un-updated caller (drips, already-scheduled rows) sends exactly as before (back-compat). Two deliberate choices, recorded so a future audit does not read them as bugs: (1) the CONSENT gate `canEmailContact(..., 'marketing', ...)` stays purpose `marketing` — every broadcast is still a bulk send that must clear the marketing double-opt-in, whatever its topic tag; (2) drip sequences and any 1:1 path default to `marketing` via the seam fallback (a per-sequence topic is a later, additive step). Deferred follow-ups: the block-email composer's topic selector (the shared `campaigns.topic` column already covers block drafts, which default to `marketing` until the selector ships) and reconciling the preference-center's member-facing label "Broadcasts" with the composer's "Announcement" (same `dispatches` key).

> **Follow-up SHIPPED — Feature B1-core (collaborator relationship, 2026-07-21).** The space<->space collaborator relationship (migration `20261195000000_space_collaborations.sql`; `lib/spaces/collaborations.ts` reads + pure resolvers; `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/collaborations-actions.ts` writes). **State vocabulary reconciled to `pending / accepted / declined / revoked`** (the CHECK constraint, the `CollaborationStatus` type, and this ADR now agree; the earlier "approved/ended" wording is retired). The row IS the relationship (approval has no external column, unlike `event_placement_requests` which sets `events.space_id`); `revoked` is a real terminal teardown that the partial unique index `uniq_space_collab_active` treats as re-requestable. Authz: request gates on the initiating side's owner/admin; accept/decline gate on the non-initiating side (`approverSideForRequest`); revoke gates on either side; a one-operator-owns-both case auto-accepts. Both sides must be `business` + `active` (free to host). RLS-enabled, no-policy (service-role only), untyped handle (ADR-246). Deferred to **B1-UI**: the management surface under Profile & Settings (needs a `collaborators` `SpaceFunctionKey` + a `SPACE_MODULES` catalog row per MENU-CONTRACT / ADR-553) and the public Collaborators profile tab (reusing `SpaceCard`), plus best-effort collaboration notifications.

## ADR-800: The events calendar is a grid + popup over EXISTING event infrastructure; the timezone contract has one seam

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Owner ask (fully-featured per-space events calendar tying into a Frequency-wide calendar). Full plan of record: `docs/EVENTS-CALENDAR.md`. Phase EC1 code: `lib/events/ics.ts` (+ test), migration `20261193000000_event_calendar_feed_time_zone.sql`, `app/spaces/[slug]/calendar.ics/route.ts`, refactors of `app/events/[slug]/event.ics` + `app/events/calendar/[token]`.

**Context.** A build audit found the events + calendar infrastructure is ~70% done and CORRECT: the event model + tenancy (`events.space_id`, `lib/events/store.ts`), the timezone engine (`lib/time/zone.ts` — `starts_at/ends_at` are wall-clock-as-UTC-parts interpreted in `events.time_zone`, resolved to a true instant via `eventInstant`), the tz-correct per-event `.ics`, the 3-touch reminder cron, enum recurrence with materialized child rows (ADR-007), and Event JSON-LD all exist. The real gaps are UI (no month grid, no click-to-preview popup), a built-but-**unmounted** `CalendarSubscribe` component, and a **real bug**: the subscribable member feed (`app/events/calendar/[token]`) stamped `starts_at` raw as UTC, so every subscribed event landed 7-8h off. The per-event `.ics` route had already been fixed for exactly this; the feed drifted because each route carried its OWN copy of the ICS helpers.

**Decision.** Build the calendar as a **grid + popup over the existing infrastructure**, not a rewrite, phased EC1-EC4 (`docs/EVENTS-CALENDAR.md` §3). Binding calls: **(1)** the timezone contract has **exactly one seam** — `lib/events/ics.ts` `icsEventInstants` — and every feed route builds DTSTART/DTEND from it, never from `new Date(row.starts_at)`; the shared `lib/events/ics.ts` replaces the three drifting per-route copies so the fix can never diverge again. **(2)** A **public per-space feed** (`space_public_calendar_feed` RPC + `/spaces/[slug]/calendar.ics`) exposes only what the public event page does (published, public/unlisted, non-cancelled) and only for a **network-visible, active** space; it is **slug-keyed** (public events, human-shareable URL) whereas the member feed stays **token-keyed** (private RSVPs + venues). **(3)** "Events shared with another space appear on both" is a **co-host join (event↔space)** landing in EC3, converging with collaborator spaces **B2** (ADR-799) rather than a second parallel mechanism. **(4)** Calendar surfaces **compose the page framework** (`IndexTemplate` for the grid; the rail falls through to `'global'`, no `page-chrome` edit).

**Consequences.** EC1 ships the correctness foundation (shared ICS lib + the feed tz fix + the public per-space feed) with the grid/popup/mounting to follow in EC2, the master calendar + shared events in EC3, and RRULE export + subscriber reminders in EC4. A future audit that flags "the feed and the per-event .ics compute times differently" should be impossible now (one seam). The co-host convergence means the events-calendar and collaborator-spaces roadmaps share the EC3/B2 join table rather than duplicating a space↔event link.

## ADR-801: A live On Air sit is attributed to the day it STARTED, not the day it finalizes

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-21). Fixes a streak-loss bug found in production. Code: `lib/practices/log-day.ts` (`attributedLogDay` + test), `lib/practices.ts` (`logPractice` accepts `startedAt`), `lib/practice-streak.ts` (`recordPracticeStreak` accepts the actual logged day), `app/(main)/on-air/actions.ts` (passes `startedAt`).

**Context.** The daily practice streak is DERIVED from `practice_logs.logged_for` (the member's LOCAL calendar day). `logPractice` keyed `logged_for` to the member's day AT FINALIZE TIME. A live On Air sit left running past midnight (a member started a sit and forgot to stop it) finalizes on a LATER calendar day than it began, so the practice was attributed to the finalize day, leaving the day the member actually practiced empty. That opens a one-day phantom gap in the streak; with no freeze banked, the gap collapses the whole run. A real member (14-day run) lost it exactly this way: a sit started 07-20 and finalized 07-21 logged for 07-21, so 07-20 was empty and the streak reset to 1. The run-over clamp (`lib/on-air/run-over.ts`) already trims the unattended AIRTIME to the target, but it never touched the DAY the sit was attributed to.

**Decision.** Attribute a finalized sit to the day it STARTED (the member's local day of `started_at`), which is both correct (they practiced on the day they began) and the convention timer apps use. Clamp the attribution to at most one day before the finalize day (`attributedLogDay`), so it can only ever move a log from "today" to "yesterday" (the real overnight case), never deeper. `recordPracticeStreak` takes the ACTUAL logged day so its race-guard adds that day (not the finalize day) while still deriving the streak as of the real "today" (so an overnight log correctly leaves today at-risk rather than phantom-counting it). Non-timer callers (quick logs, check-ins) pass no `started_at` and are unchanged (same-instant → finalize day).

**Trust model (anti-backdating).** The client's `input.startedAt` is spoofable, so it is NOT trusted for the day — a crafted `completeSession` claiming a yesterday start could otherwise revive a dead streak without a real practice or a freeze spend. Instead the attribution start comes from the SERVER-authoritative active timer session (`practice_timer_sessions`, ADR-521), whose `updated_at` is server-stamped on every owner-gated write and cannot be forged. `completeSession` reads that row before deleting it and only backdates when its `updated_at` is on a PRIOR local day (a genuine forgotten-overnight run); a session fabricated today has `updated_at = today` and never earns the backdate. Combined with the one-day clamp, backdating is both trust-gated and bounded. The affected member's streak was restored by re-attributing the mis-dated log to 07-20 and re-deriving (14).

**Consequences.** A sit that crosses midnight now counts for the day it began, so leaving a timer running overnight no longer silently breaks a streak, and the change cannot be used to manufacture streaks (server-gated + one-day bound). The daily cap, once-per-practice-per-day uniqueness, and the airtime clamp are untouched — only the `logged_for` DAY moves. Known low-severity follow-up: the today-only un-log path (`unlogPractice` / `recomputePracticeStreakAfterUnlog`) still keys on the finalize day, so the reveal's Undo silently no-ops for an overnight sit logged to yesterday (no data corruption — the mismatched lookup early-returns); a full fix would have un-log resolve the attributed day the same way.

## ADR-802: The events calendar EC3 — a master public feed + event↔space shares (per-event grain), with the leak gate on the event's OWN row in every reader

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Implements EC3 of ADR-800 / `docs/EVENTS-CALENDAR.md`. Code: migrations `20261196000000_public_calendar_feed.sql` (master feed RPC) + `20261197000000_event_space_shares.sql` (share table + the `space_public_calendar_feed` UNION recreation); `lib/events/event-share.ts`, `app/(main)/events/share-actions.ts`, `lib/events/store.ts` (UNION + `listPublicCalendarEvents` + the pure `passesCalendarGate` / `masterCalendarIncludes` / `mergeSpaceCalendarRows`); routes `app/events/calendar.ics` + page `app/(main)/events/calendar`; UI `event-share-field` / `event-share-approvals` (+ controls); tests `lib/events/event-share.test.ts` + additions to `store.test.ts`.

**Context.** EC1/EC2 gave every space a correct per-space calendar + subscribable `.ics`. EC3 owes two things: a **master** discovery calendar over all public events, and **shared / co-hosted events** (an event on more than one space's calendar), which is also collaborator-spaces item **B2** (ADR-799). The tenancy risk is a leak: a share is a grant of visibility across a tenancy boundary, so the mechanism must never let a share surface an event the event's own visibility would hide.

**Decision — two grains, one never becomes the other.** Shared events use a **per-event** join, `event_space_shares` (event ↔ target space), NOT the **space-pair** `space_collaborations` (ADR-799). They are deliberately distinct: a collaboration says "these two businesses work together" (a durable space↔space relationship); a share says "THIS event also belongs on THAT space's calendar" (one event, one target, its own approval + lifecycle). `space_collaborations` only ever **auto-approves** a share (if an accepted collaboration already links the event's home space and the target, the round-trip is skipped) — it is a convenience input to the share decision, **never the share store**. Reusing it as the store would conflate "we collaborate" with "this specific event is co-hosted", and revoking a collaboration would silently pull unrelated events off calendars. Two entry points (host **invites** a space → its stewards approve; a space steward asks to **feature** an event → the host approves), symmetric to the collaboration request/approve, with the pure `approverSideForShare` deciding which side is the approver.

**Decision — the leak gate is on the event's OWN row in EVERY reader (necessary, not sufficient).** An accepted share is a NECESSARY condition to surface an event elsewhere, never a SUFFICIENT one. Each of the three readers re-applies the event's own visibility gate — published + public/unlisted + non-cancelled + upcoming — on the event's own row: `space_public_calendar_feed`'s new UNION branch (in SQL), and the store's `listSpaceCalendarEvents` / `spaceHasPublicUpcomingEvents` (via the pure `passesCalendarGate`). So flipping a shared event to private/circle_only/draft, or cancelling it, drops it from every co-host calendar at once — the share row is irrelevant to the redaction. `event_space_shares` is RLS-enabled with **no policies** (service-role only, in `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt`); every write goes through app-layer authz (host side = `event.editSettings`, space side = the space steward set) with **atomic status-guarded transitions** and unique-violation-as-success.

**Decision — the master feed is PUBLIC-only and self-gated.** `public_calendar_feed()` is the per-space feed minus the space filter and with a stricter visibility gate: **public only, `unlisted` EXCLUDED** (unlisted is link-reachable, not discovery; it still surfaces in its own space's feed). It takes no argument, so there is no credential and no route gate to lean on — the redaction contract lives ENTIRELY in the `SECURITY DEFINER` function (published + public + non-cancelled + upcoming, and only network-visible active spaces; platform events with `space_id IS NULL` included via a LEFT JOIN). The grid page and the `.ics` share ONE read (`listPublicCalendarEvents` → the same RPC) so they cannot drift, mirroring the ADR-800 "one seam" principle.

**Consequences.** An event can now appear on several calendars with one home; the master calendar gives discovery a single surface. The per-event vs space-pair grain is explicit, so a future change to collaborations cannot accidentally move events, and a future audit that asks "can a share leak a private event?" has one answer to check per reader (the gate on the event's own row) plus two anon-callable RPCs that self-gate. EC4 (RRULE export, subscriber reminders, master-calendar filters) remains.

## ADR-803: The pricing admin gaps get real console editors; the catalog sync reads operator amounts, and the operator seat gets an activation switch

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Implements the "Known gaps" of `docs/PRICING-OPERATIONS.md`. Code: `lib/pricing/founding.ts` (`sanitizeFoundingConfig`), `lib/pricing/settings.ts` (the `catalog_operator_seat_active` flag), `lib/billing/pricing-products.ts` (`isCatalogItemInertPlaceholder` + the catalog sync reading operator amounts), `app/(main)/admin/pricing/{actions,load,pricing-console}.tsx`, migration `20261198000000_pricing_admin_gaps.sql`; tests `lib/pricing/founding-config.test.ts` + `lib/billing/pricing-products-placeholder.test.ts`.

**Context.** Five pricing knobs were settable only by editing `pricing_settings` / `platform_flags` by hand: the `founding` config (member one-time + cap, business monthly + take bps + city cap), the operator-seat price + activation, the 8% member take-rate (`take_rate.member_bps`), and the three beta controls (`beta_ends_at`, `beta_invite_only`, `beta_host_prompts`). Each is config that ships OFF/inert (ADR-362); moving them onto `/admin/pricing` must not change that.

**Decision — editors only, everything still ships OFF.** Each gap gets a janitor-gated console editor (a founding-rates section, an operator-seat row + activation toggle, a Member % take-rate field, and a beta-controls section), never a live flip: nothing charges until the master switch is on (billingLive()). Value edits write `pricing_settings` with `updated_by` (matching the other price saves); boolean flips write `platform_flags` via `setPlatformFlag`, so they are audited in `platform_flag_events`. `saveFoundingConfig` runs the pure `sanitizeFoundingConfig` (narrow every field fail-safe to the default, clamp the take-rate to at most 100%) so a garbage or partial input can never store an impossible value.

**Decision — the operator seat's `placeholder` is resolved from a flag, and the catalog sync reads OPERATOR amounts.** The seat stays a code-level `placeholder` skipped by `syncPricingCatalogToStripe` (the invariant that a routine sync never mints a seat price the owner did not approve). The new `catalog_operator_seat_active` flag is the ONLY thing that drops the placeholder: the pure `isCatalogItemInertPlaceholder(item, seatActive)` keeps every other placeholder inert regardless. In the same change the catalog sync now resolves each item's amount from `loadCatalogConfig()` (the operator overrides, fail-safe to the code catalog) instead of the raw code constants — honoring the console's own "run this after you change a catalog price" contract, and making the operator-set seat price the amount that gets minted. For an un-overridden DB this is identical output, so it is a strict, low-risk correction.

**Decision — `beta_ends_at` stays display-only.** The countdown date is saved as a `platform_settings` text value and feeds ONLY the countdown banner. It is deliberately NOT wired into any access gate: it grants and removes nothing. The two beta booleans keep their existing live gates (the invite gate in the signup path, the host prompts on the feed); the console only sets their flag values.

**Consequences.** The five knobs are now operator-editable with the same fail-safe-to-defaults reads as before, and every boolean flip is audited. The seat is genuinely inert until both its price is set and its switch is on. Because the catalog sync now reads overrides, an operator who edits a catalog price and re-syncs finally gets the edited price in Stripe (previously it re-synced the code constant). No new table, so `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt` is unchanged.

## ADR-804: The live Founding Business checkout is a Space-scoped Focus surface that reuses the space_plan money path and grants the founder record on the success confirm

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Implements the live founding Business checkout the marketing surface (ADR-599) always deferred ("there is no live business-checkout route yet"). Code: `lib/founding/business-checkout.ts` (+ `business-checkout.test.ts`), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/settings/billing/founding/` (page + `founding-checkout.tsx` client + `actions.ts` + `success/page.tsx`), one `MANAGED_ROUTES` catalog line in `lib/layout/page-chrome.ts`, and an entry-point link in the space `billing-body.tsx`.

**Context.** A Space could reserve a founding Business spot on the public marketing page (a free, no-card `contacts` waitlist lead), but there was no way to actually BUY the founding Business membership. The founding Business rate ($49/mo, $490/yr with two months free, a 3% take-rate bought down from the 5-8% ladder, capped at 25 businesses per city) is reconciled in `lib/pricing/founding.ts` and read via `getFoundingConfig`. The durable, grandfathered record + the `grantFoundingStatus()` hook already exist (`lib/founding/status.ts`). What was missing was the LIVE, owner-facing checkout that charges the locked rate and writes the founder record, without violating the ADR-362 no-charge invariant.

**Decision — a Space-scoped Focus surface under billing settings.** The checkout lives at `/spaces/[slug]/settings/billing/founding` (a `FocusTemplate` conversion surface), authorized by the same `resolveSpaceManageAccess` gate as the sibling billing page (notFound on a miss, no existence leak). The rail falls through to `'global'` like every other space settings sub-page, so page-chrome needs only a one-line `MANAGED_ROUTES` catalog entry, not a rail-logic change.

**Decision — reuse the `space_plan` money path; never a parallel Stripe flow.** `createFoundingBusinessCheckout` creates a `mode:'subscription'` session at the SYNCED Business price for the chosen period (`priceKey('business', period)` — the same price the standard plan checkout charges, which IS the founding price), stamped `metadata { kind:'space_plan', plan:'business', founding:'business', cohort_city }`. Because `kind:'space_plan'`, the EXISTING `reconcileSpacePlanSubscription` webhook sets the Space to Business with no webhook edit; the extra `founding.*` keys are read ONLY by the success confirm. There is no trial (a Founding Business locks in at checkout).

**Decision — grant the founder record on the webhook-independent success confirm.** `confirmFoundingBusinessCheckout` (mirroring `confirmFounderCheckout`) retrieves the paid session, verifies it belongs to THIS Space, and calls `grantFoundingStatus({ spaceId, kind:'business', cohortCity })`, which writes/activates the `founding_members` row at the locked rate + 3% take-rate WITHOUT charging (idempotent). The grant hook is REUSED, not reinvented; no new table or migration (the table + its `meta`/`cohort_city` columns already exist, RLS-deny-all registered).

**Decision — three gates, one pure state machine.** `foundingBusinessCheckoutState({ billingLive, spaceIsPaying, spotsRemaining })` returns `already_active` (a paying Space never double-subscribes — new `spaceIsPaying` reader over `spaces.plan` + `stripe_subscription_id`, precedence-first) > `not_open` (billing OFF, the ADR-362 invariant: the surface renders as a preview but no Stripe call is possible) > `sold_out` (the per-city cap is full, via `foundingBusinessSpotsRemaining` + `foundingBusinessTakenInCity`) > `open`. The same gate runs in the page render and inside the checkout seam before any Stripe call, so a live render still cannot charge until billing is on. The pure state machine + the annual "two months free" math (`foundingBusinessAnnualCents` / `foundingBusinessAnnualSavingsCents`, derived from `annual_discount.months_free`, never hardcoded) are unit-tested.

**Decision — the city is collected, not stored.** Spaces have no city column, so the checkout collects the operating city (prefilled from any existing founding record via `spaceCohortCity`), which scopes the per-city cap and stamps `cohort_city` on the grant, mirroring the marketing reservation form.

**Consequences.** A Space can now buy the founding Business membership live, grandfathered for life, entirely through the reused space-plan subscription + founding-grant machinery — no second Stripe path, no webhook change, no schema change. The surface is inert until `billing_live` (a disabled "Available soon" preview). Known follow-ups: (1) the per-city cap is checked at checkout START only (an abandoned session never reserves a spot; a simultaneous race could momentarily exceed the small cap, matching the marketing flow's soft-cap posture); (2) a dedicated `founding` webhook branch could grant the record server-side in addition to the success confirm, but the idempotent confirm already covers the redirect path; (3) the entry-point link added to `billing-body.tsx` is the one shared-file touch.

## ADR-805: Collaborator B3 shared venue coordination is an advisory request→approve HOLD, deliberately outside the booking conflict engine

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Delivers the B3 shared-venue half of collaborator spaces (ADR-799 §B) after the shared-calendar slice. Code: migration `20261202000000_space_venue_holds.sql`, `lib/spaces/venue-holds.ts` (reads + gate `spacesHaveAcceptedCollaboration`), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/venue-actions.ts` (request/accept/decline/cancel), and the collaborators-page surfaces (`venue-holds-section.tsx` + `venue-holds-panel.tsx`), alongside the shared-calendar section.

**Context.** Co-located collaborator businesses (a healing center hosting practitioners, a salon's chairs) need to coordinate use of a shared venue. The full booking engine (`booking.ts`: availability windows, exact-instant + buffer conflict, confirmed/pending/deposit states) is for a member booking a Space's service — a heavyweight, money-adjacent, conflict-enforced path. Wiring cross-space coordination INTO it would risk a hold blocking or double-booking a real customer booking.

**Decision — a coordination HOLD, not a booking.** `space_venue_holds` is a request→approve handshake (mirroring `space_collaborations` / `event_space_shares`): the requester space asks, the venue space's owner/admin approves, the row IS the hold (states pending/accepted/declined/cancelled). It NEVER touches `space_bookings` or the conflict engine, so overlapping holds are allowed and a hold can never block or double-book a customer booking. It is advisory: the humans coordinate around it. This keeps the sensitive booking path completely untouched.

**Decision — gated on an ACCEPTED collaboration; the venue side approves.** A hold can only be created when an accepted `space_collaboration` links the two spaces (`spacesHaveAcceptedCollaboration`), so the venue is only requestable by a real, mutually-agreed collaborator. Create gates on the requester space's owner/admin; respond (accept/decline) on the venue space's owner/admin (a requester cannot self-approve); cancel on either side. All status transitions are atomic (status-guarded `WHERE`). The table is RLS-enabled-no-policy (service-role only, in `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt`); reads only return holds a space is party to.

**Consequences.** Collaborators coordinate venue use from the collaborators settings surface with zero risk to the booking/conflict path (nothing charges, nothing books). Losing a collaboration does not auto-cancel existing holds (a point-in-time agreement) but blocks new ones. Known follow-ups: (1) surface accepted holds on the shared collaborator calendar; (2) a real "convert an approved hold into a booking" bridge if a venue later wants the conflict-enforced version.

## ADR-806: Opt-in space-follower event reminders are a sibling cron with a dedicated default-off preference and its own idempotency ledger

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Adds an opt-in engagement email: a member who FOLLOWS a Space is reminded of that Space's upcoming PUBLIC events they have not RSVP'd to. Code: migration `20261204000000_space_follower_reminders.sql`, `lib/events/follower-reminders.ts` (+ `follower-reminders.test.ts`), `lib/notification-preferences.ts` (`space_event_reminders` column + `wantsSpaceEventReminders`), `lib/email.ts` (`sendSpaceFollowerEventReminderEmail`), `app/api/cron/space-follower-event-reminders/route.ts`, the `/settings/notifications` toggle (`form.tsx`), and one `vercel.json` cron line.

**Context.** The event-reminder cron (`app/api/cron/event-reminders`) reminds people who RSVP'd (the 7d/24h/2h cadence, idempotent per-attendee via `event_rsvps.reminder_*_sent_at`). Following a Space (`space_follows`) expressed interest but drove zero event email. The gap: nudge a follower about a Space's upcoming events. This is OUTBOUND engagement email, so the bar is safety, not cleverness: strictly opt-in, never double-send, suppression-respecting, public-only.

**Decision — a sibling cron reusing the helpers, never a rewrite of the RSVP path.** The RSVP reminder cron is left byte-for-byte untouched (no regression risk to the transactional path). `lib/events/follower-reminders.ts` reuses the same tz-correct send window (the identical 6.5d..7.5d band + 30-min slack, filtered by `eventInstant`/`resolveZone`), the same `enqueueEmail` outbox, the same events-category unsubscribe headers, and the same `isSuppressed` guard. A new Vercel cron at `*/15 * * * *` calls it.

**Decision — a NEW preference, default OFF, is the opt-in.** `notification_preferences.space_event_reminders boolean default false`. Read via `wantsSpaceEventReminders()` (fail-closed to false). Until a member flips the `/settings/notifications` toggle, they receive ZERO of these emails. On top of the opt-in the cron ALSO requires the member's event email channel (`email_events`) to be on, the same switch the RSVP cron respects, so a global event-email opt-out is honored as a master kill-switch.

**Decision — a dedicated idempotency ledger, insert-before-send.** `space_follower_event_reminders_sent` with `unique(event_id, profile_id, lead)`. The cron claims the slot with an insert BEFORE sending and only sends if the insert won (a concurrent run's duplicate insert conflicts), so the same (member, event, window) is emailed at most once even across re-runs. A separate ledger (not the RSVP stamp columns) is correct because these recipients have NO RSVP row by definition.

**Decision — public-only and RSVP-excluding, both provable on a pure core.** `followerReminderEventEligible` accepts only `visibility='public'` + `status='published'` + not cancelled + has a Space (unlisted/private/circle_only/draft never qualify), and only ACTIVE spaces surface reminders. `selectFollowerReminderRecipients` is a pure, exhaustively unit-tested filter over `{ optedIn, eventsEmailOn, hasRsvp, suppressed, hasDeliverableEmail, alreadySent }` — RSVP'd members are excluded by design (the RSVP path covers them; this path is the opt-in complement), and the event host is dropped from the follower set (never remind the host of their own event). New table is RLS-enabled-no-policy (service-role only, registered in `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt`).

**Consequences.** Following a Space now optionally drives a gentle, public-only event nudge with the same deliverability guarantees as every other event email, and default-off means the blast radius is zero until a member opts in. The four safety invariants each have a single enforcement point: default-off (`wantsSpaceEventReminders` + the column default), idempotent (the unique ledger + insert-before-send), suppression (`isSuppressed` + `sendRawEmail`), public-only (`followerReminderEventEligible`). Known follow-ups: (1) no in-app/push leg (email only, matching the opt-in copy); (2) the whenLabel vocabulary is intentionally softer than the RSVP path ("soon" vs "in about 2 hours") since the reader has no RSVP.
## ADR-807: The calendar FEEDS collapse a recurring series to ONE RRULE VEVENT + EXDATE, computed to the materialization horizon so a cancelled occurrence never resurrects (Events EC4)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Extends the per-event RRULE export (EC4) to the subscribable FEEDS. Code: migration `20261203000000_calendar_feed_recurrence.sql`; `lib/events/ics.ts` (`computeFeedExdates`, `planCalendarFeed`, `EXDATE` in `buildVevent`); `lib/event-recurrence.ts` (`expandOccurrenceInstants`); the SPACE + MASTER `.ics` routes (`app/spaces/[slug]/calendar.ics`, `app/events/calendar.ics`). Tests in `lib/events/ics.test.ts` + `lib/event-recurrence.test.ts`.

**Context.** A recurring event materializes as an ANCHOR row (`recurrence_type != 'none'`, `parent_event_id IS NULL`) plus real CHILD occurrence rows (`parent_event_id = anchor.id`) that the daily cron rolls forward to `HORIZON_DAYS`. The SPACE + MASTER feeds emitted the anchor AND every child as SEPARATE VEVENTs — correct but verbose, and drifting from the per-event export, which already ships ONE VEVENT + `RRULE` (rruleForRecurrence, EC4). Folding the same RRULE into the feeds needs the feed RPCs to carry the recurrence shape, and needs `EXDATE` so a cancelled/deleted occurrence does not RESURRECT when the client expands the RRULE.

**Decision — add columns to the feed RPCs; never touch a gate.** `20261203000000` recreates `space_public_calendar_feed(uuid)` (with its EC3 accepted-share UNION branch) and `public_calendar_feed()` adding ONLY `recurrence_type text` / `recurrence_until timestamptz` / `parent_event_id uuid` to the RETURNS TABLE + SELECT list(s). Every WHERE clause, JOIN, the network+active owning-space gate, the accepted-share home-space gate, and the public-only master gate are VERBATIM from `20261197000000` / `20261196000000`. These are anon-callable SECURITY DEFINER leak-contract surfaces, so the migration is column-additive only; the new columns are non-sensitive shape metadata already on the public event page. The MEMBER feed (`event_calendar_feed`) is deliberately UNTOUCHED — it is per-RSVP'd-occurrence and must keep one VEVENT per occurrence.

**Decision — group in a pure seam; orphan children survive.** `planCalendarFeed` (pure, unit-tested) turns the flat rows into VEVENT plans: a recurring anchor present in the feed emits one `RRULE` (+ `EXDATE`) and its in-feed children are folded in; a non-recurring event, or an ORPHAN child whose anchor is NOT in the feed (the anchor went private / cancelled / out of window), stays its OWN VEVENT so a child is never dropped for its parent's absence. DTSTART/DTEND still route through the one timezone seam (`icsEventInstants`).

**Decision — EXDATE in absolute space, bounded to the materialization horizon (resurrection guard).** `computeFeedExdates` (pure, unit-tested) expands the series from the anchor's TRUE instant in ABSOLUTE (UTC) time — the space a client expands DTSTART+RRULE in, so an `EXDATE` matches the exact instant the client would generate — and subtracts the occurrences PRESENT in the feed (anchor + non-cancelled children, matched by UTC day). The expansion bound is the MATERIALIZATION HORIZON (`now + HORIZON_DAYS`), NOT the last present date: the feed carries only non-cancelled rows, so a cancelled TAIL occurrence is absent from the present set, and bounding to the last present date would leave it un-EXDATE'd and it would resurrect. Occurrences BEYOND the horizon are simply not materialized yet, so they are NOT EXDATE'd and the RRULE keeps generating the ongoing series (a later poll, after the cron materializes them, finds them present or EXDATEs a fresh cancellation). `recurrence_until` resolves through the zone to the same instant the RRULE `UNTIL` carries.

**Consequences.** The subscribable feeds are far smaller and read as real series in every calendar app; a cancelled/deleted occurrence is subtracted and cannot come back. The collapse only fires when the anchor itself is upcoming (in-feed); an established series whose anchor is already in the past keeps per-occurrence VEVENTs (its children have no in-feed anchor to fold into) — correct, just verbose for that case. The grid pages read the same store functions and ignore the additive columns (unchanged behavior). Inherent limitation (shared with the per-event export): the enum cadence uses a UTC DTSTART, so a DST boundary can shift a generated occurrence ~1h from its materialized wall-clock; EXDATE day-key matching absorbs that jitter.

## ADR-808: A space owner runs its events (event capability delegates to space ownership), and the space admin surfaces get their missing CRUD + confirms (deep-pass EC5)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). A completeness/safety pass over the spaces + commerce admin controls. Code: `lib/core/load-capabilities.ts` (`getEventCapabilities` space delegation), `app/(main)/events/actions.ts` (`cancelEvent`), the space Calendar console + `space-events-manager.tsx`, `lib/spaces/venue-holds.ts` (`cancelOpenHoldsBetween`), the collaborator/venue/share controls, `app/(main)/events/share-actions.ts` (`requestFeatureEventBySlug`) + `feature-event-field.tsx`, `components/marketplace/product-cover.tsx` + the Shop catalog grid, and `app/(main)/admin/pricing/*` (confirms + founding read-modify-write).

**Decision — "if you run the scope, you run its events" now covers SPACES, not just circles.** `getEventCapabilities` set `viewerManagesScope` only for `scope_type==='circle'`. A space event is `scope_type='public'` + `space_id`, so space ownership was never consulted and `event.editSettings` went to the host or staff alone — locking a space owner/admin/editor out of every space event they did not personally host. It now also resolves the owning Space via `getSpaceCapabilities(...).canEditProfile` (the same authority that gates space config), mirroring `getPractice/JourneyCapabilities`. Adversarially verified: the grant boundary is exactly editor+/owner/staff (a plain member/follower/anon never qualifies), and every null path is fail-safe to false.

**Decision — `cancelEvent` gates on the capability, then writes with the admin client.** The member action guarded the UPDATE with `.eq('host_id', me)`, silently flipping zero rows for a non-host manager. It now checks `getEventCapabilities().has('event.editSettings')` and updates by `id` with `.eq('is_cancelled', false)` for idempotency — using the RLS-bypassing admin client AFTER the gate, because the `events` UPDATE RLS policy is host/guide-only and would otherwise re-introduce the same silent no-op at the RLS layer. Refund fan-out stays idempotent on the live→cancelled transition; hosts still pass via `hostId`.

**Decision — the space Calendar console gains the CRUD list; ending a collaboration cascades.** The console was view-only; `SpaceEventsManager` lists every space event (past + upcoming, all statuses via `listEventsForSpace`) with Edit/Duplicate/Cancel/Delete behind confirms. `revokeCollaboration` calls `cancelOpenHoldsBetween` (fail-safe, both directions) so an accepted venue hold never outlives the collaboration that authorized it. Destructive collaborator/venue/share controls now confirm, and declined collaborations/holds surface (with one-click re-invite) instead of silently vanishing.

**Decision — the feature-an-event handshake is completed, not left half-wired.** `requestFeatureEvent` + its host-side approve/decline UI shipped without an entry control (dead code). `requestFeatureEventBySlug` (resolves a visible, published event by link/slug, then delegates to the self-guarding `requestFeatureEvent`) + the `FeatureEventField` control on the space manage console activate the existing `awaitingHostApproval` branch.

**Decision — one product cover, and confirms on the live money flips.** `ProductCover` is extracted so the public browse card and the Shop admin catalog share one header-image treatment; the catalog renders as a product-card grid. `billing_live`, Stripe sync, and operator-seat activation (blocked at a $0 price) each confirm. `saveFoundingConfig` is read-modify-write (merge changed fields over the current stored config) so the member row and business row can no longer clobber each other from a stale client snapshot.

**Consequences.** Space operators can fully manage their events, collaborators, holds, shares, and shop from the space surfaces, with confirms on every destructive/live action and no orphaned holds. Follow-ups (a storefront banner image, per-seat price display, seat-downgrade protection) shipped in ADR-809.

## ADR-809: The ADR-808 follow-ups: a storefront banner (JSON, no migration), seat-price display, and a seat-downgrade floor

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-22). Finishes the three items ADR-808 deferred. Code: `lib/spaces/storefront.ts` (+ `storefront.test.ts`), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/settings/shop/storefront-banner-field.tsx` + `storefront-tab.tsx` + `shop-actions.ts`, the public `(profile)/shop/page.tsx`, and the seat surfaces `billing-body.tsx` / `go-business.tsx` / `seat-editor.tsx`.

**Decision — the storefront banner rides in the existing `preferences.storefront` JSON node, so NO migration.** ADR-808 assumed a schema change; there isn't one. `StorefrontConfig` gains `bannerUrl: string | null` + `bannerFocus: string`, both sanitized in the pure reader/writer (`cleanBannerUrl` keeps only an `http(s)` string; `cleanBannerFocus` keeps only an `"x% y%"` shape, else centers). The editor is a client island (`StorefrontBannerField`) wrapping the shared `HeaderImageField` (upload-through-Loom + drag-to-focus) that mirrors its URL + focal point into hidden inputs so the plain server-action `<form>` submits them; the public Shop tab renders the banner at its saved focal crop. An empty submitted URL clears it.

**Decision — the seat pickers show what the count costs, resolved from the configured catalog.** `billing-body` loads `loadCatalogConfig()` and passes the operator seat's `monthlyFoundingCents` (the charged amount, operator-set, not the hardcoded default) into both `GoBusinessCta` and `SeatEditor`, which render "N seats x $X = $Y/mo, prorated." The price was already available server-side; only the display was missing.

**Decision — the seat editor floors at the seats already in use.** `billing-body` computes `minSeats = max(0, used - BASE_SEAT_ALLOWANCE)` (the licensed total is base + seatQuantity, and must cover the active member-operators), and `SeatEditor` floors its minus button there and shows a warning to remove operators in Members first. This stops an owner silently licensing fewer seats than the operators consuming them. The pure seat math (`seatLimitReached`/`licensedSeats`) is unchanged; this is the missing UI guard over it.

**Consequences.** The storefront gets a real banner with zero schema cost, seat quantities are never priceless, and a downgrade can't strand operators over the license. The banner is a single image (no gallery) and reuses the same image host allowlist as every other uploaded image; the seat-price display uses the month founding amount (annual seats are not sold through these pickers).

## ADR-810: Collaboration is a Business-plan capability, gated server-side on the host; the upgrade funnel is a taste-then-gate model (Crew for the first Space, Business to host + run multiple)

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-23). Owner direction. Ties the shipped collaboration machinery (ADR-799 §B / ADR-802) to the pricing funnel and fixes a gap: collaboration was free + universal (the actions gated only on `status='active'`, and the capability check lived only in the UI, not the write path). Full map: `docs/COLLABORATION-AND-UPGRADE-FUNNEL.md`. Code: `lib/pricing/gates.ts` (`space_collaborators`), `lib/spaces/function-access.ts` (`spaceCanHostCollaborators`), `app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/collaborations-actions.ts` + `app/(main)/events/share-actions.ts` (server enforcement), the collaborators settings page + `collaborators-body.tsx` (locked preview), `lib/pricing/space-limits.ts` (+ test) enforced in `lib/spaces/provision.ts`, `lib/core/capabilities.ts` + `app/(main)/events/new/page.tsx` (event creation opened). Everything ships behind `billing_live` OFF.

**Context.** The owner asked to (1) let collaborator spaces be added/removed from another space **or event** with the other side confirming, (2) restrict collaboration to spaces (never personal accounts), and (3) establish who can collaborate on what plus the upgrade-funnel points, best-practice, so members taste the value but must upgrade to do much. An audit found the relationships already built (space↔space `space_collaborations`, event↔space `event_space_shares`, venue holds `space_venue_holds`), spaces-only by construction, and confirmation already required. The missing piece was the **funnel gate**: hosting collaborators was free + universal, event creation was Crew-or-steward-only (contradicting "a member can create an event"), and there was no space-count cap.

**Decision — the collaboration wall is on the HOST side, on the Business plan, enforced in the actions.** A new `space_collaborators` feature gate (plan axis, `business` floor; Non Profit clears it via the shared full-depth set) is read by `spaceCanHostCollaborators` and checked **inside the write actions** (which are the authority, since the tables are service-role-only): `requestCollaboration` + accept gate the **host** space; `requestEventShare` gates the event's **home** space; `requestFeatureEvent` gates the **featuring** space. The collaborator (guest) side needs only an active space (it pays for its own, ADR-799). A free host is not hidden from the feature — the settings surface renders a **locked preview** with a *Go Business* prompt (the tease pattern, ADR-466), so the value is visible and the upgrade is one clear trigger. A member's personal event lives on the platform space (not a business venue), so it is gated until it runs under a Business space, which is exactly the "you need a business space to have collaborators" intent.

**Decision — the funnel boundaries (owner calls).** (1) **Event creation opens to any signed-in member** (`event.create` split out of the Crew+ creation gate; the deeper circle/journey/practice authoring stays Crew+). (2) **Space creation is capped by tier:** free → 0 (go Crew), Crew/Supporter → 1, owning a paid Business/Non Profit space → unlimited. The pure `canCreateSpace` rule is enforced in `createSpace`. (3) **Money exchange is never the wall** (holds ADR-552): every plan can transact; depth, scale, seats, and collaboration are what upgrade.

**Decision — OFF preserves today's behavior exactly.** Every new gate runs through `billingLive()` / `featureAllowed`, which short-circuits to granted while `billing_live` is OFF, and every reader is fail-safe to granted on error. So today: collaboration stays free + universal, any member creates events, space creation is uncapped. The walls bite only once an operator flips go-live. No migration (the gate is code + the existing `spaces.plan`; the relationships already have their tables).

**Alternatives.** (a) Keep collaboration free/universal — rejected: it is a depth/scale capability and the owner wants it as the Business upsell. (b) Hide the feature from free hosts — rejected: a locked preview converts better and matches the resonate-not-extract posture. (c) Gate the collaborator (guest) too — rejected: the guest already pays for their own space; double-gating would block legitimate small guests and contradicts "free to host" (ADR-799). (d) Require Crew for event creation (status quo) — rejected: the owner wants event creation as the free taste.

**Consequences.** The collaboration funnel is now real and enforced where it cannot be bypassed, while beta behavior is unchanged until billing goes live. A follow-up worth noting: platform/root events run by staff would be gated by the host-plan check once billing is live (the root space is not "business"); staff co-hosting of genuine platform events is a rare case to revisit at go-live if needed. The `space_collaborations` action module still lacks IO/action-level tests (only the pure resolvers are covered); the pure funnel rules (`canCreateSpace`, the `space_collaborators` gate) are unit-tested here.

## ADR-811: Frequency is a Community Collective — in-collective-vs-standalone pricing, six named tiers, and a network-sourced-only take-rate

**Status:** Accepted (2026-07-23). Owner-locked strategic direction after four industry-research streams and a full codebase scan. Source of truth: `docs/COMMUNITY-COLLECTIVE-STRATEGY.md`. Full implementation plan: `docs/COMMUNITY-COLLECTIVE-BUILD-PLAN.md`. **Supersedes the flat single-Business pricing of ADR-552 / ADR-590** (existing spaces grandfathered). Everything ships behind `billing_live` OFF until a single go-live flip.

**Context.** Frequency was positioned as one more wellness-business SaaS in a crowded, resented category (Mindbody, Circle, Kajabi), and ADR-552/590 had deliberately collapsed the model to one usage-metered Business plan with "no tier names." Research showed (a) the market is two silos that never touch (cold booking tools vs warm community tools) with no one serving the solo-to-collective continuum; (b) solo healers are cash-poor and hate take-rate on their own bookings, add-on creep, and lock-in; (c) the aligned monetization is a take-rate on network-*sourced* business, not on core work (Gumroad ~10% self / ~30% network; Substack owns discovery to justify 10% with no feature gates); (d) a monthly floor with no revenue is the top churn driver, so subscriptions should be cheap and success should carry the revenue. The owner directed a reposition to "Frequency is a Community Collective" with a two-world price: affordable inside the collective, standard SaaS outside it.

**Decision.**
- **Positioning:** Frequency is **the Community Collective**, a collaboration-first network that exists to support every community effort and help everyone in it succeed. This claims the unserved intersection + the solo-to-collective continuum.
- **Two-world pricing on the existing `spaces.network_connected` dial** (today dormant): **connected → highly affordable** (Member $0 · Crew $9 · Business $29 · Collective $79/beta $49 · Non Profit $39); **disconnected → standard SaaS** (Independent white-label ~$249). Belonging is the cheap default; leaving is a deliberate, priced choice (loss-framed).
- **Take-rate is network-sourced ONLY.** A member's own bookings are always **0%**; the platform takes a small, tier-declining slice (~10/8/5/3/0%) of the business the network *brings* them (referrals/discovery/marketplace). Seats and AI are **flat add-ons, never a %**. Launch the rate low and earn the right to raise it.
- **Four brand promises** (the anti-incumbent wedge): we never take a cut of your bookings · one honest price · leave anytime · see exactly what the network earned you.
- **Mission & buildings:** collaboration/shared-success is the marketing message, always as invitation never guilt; physical spaces are funded by a **separate community-owned vehicle** (co-op / community shares), not platform margin, with a capped, price-locked Founding Steward patronage tier.
- **Naming (amends NAMING.md):** "Collective" is canonical as **both** the brand ("Community Collective") **and** the $79 tier (a collective within the Collective). **Quest usage is untouched** (the game's "collective standing" / `collective-goal` stays). The stray marketing "The Collective" paid-content label is renamed in the marketing phase. Independent joins as the white-label/disconnected tier. The ADR-552 "two designators, no tier names" lock is retired.

**Alternatives.** (1) Keep the flat single-Business model (ADR-590) — rejected: an $9→$79 cliff and a subscription-floor churn trap, and it leaves the collaboration thesis unmonetized. (2) Take-rate on all commerce (Momence/Mindbody style) — rejected: the most-resented cost in this cash-poor vertical. (3) Feature-locked tiers — rejected: taxes the growth a community mission wants to maximize (never gate contacts/members).

**Consequences.** A large, phased rebuild (`docs/COMMUNITY-COLLECTIVE-BUILD-PLAN.md`, Phases 0-9) touching docs, the pricing/entitlements engine, a net-new differential-take-rate subsystem (order-level network attribution, the one genuinely hard build), the `network_connected` wiring, in-product surfaces, a member-facing "network earned you $X" readout, the public rebrand, SEO/AIO, infographics, the lead funnel, and help. ~80% is reconfiguration of shipped systems; ~20% net-new. Every phase ships behind `billing_live` OFF and is independently reviewable; grandfathered `business`/`nonprofit` spaces keep resolving. Go-live is the final deliberate flip. The take-rate's correctness (never bill a self-booking a network rate) is the top risk, mitigated by defaulting to self/0% on ambiguity + adversarial tests + the public receipt.

**Go-live addendum (2026-07-24).** The final flip, wired and turned on:

- **Founding ladder.** Business gets a **$19 founding anchor** under its $29 list (was flat $29), so the founding/list rungs read as a clean progression **$19 → $29 → $49 → $79** (Business founding/list, Collective founding/list; gaps +$10/+$20/+$30). Yearly is two months free (`$190` founding). Set in the code catalog (`business_base`), `lib/pricing/founding.ts`, and the reprice migration.
- **Collective + Independent sell through the CATALOG namespace, not `SPACE_PLAN_KEYS`.** `SPACE_PLAN_KEYS` stays `business`/`nonprofit` (it couples to `priceKey`/`PERIODS_BY_KEY`/the single-price `createSpacePlanCheckout`). The two new tiers ride the **multi-item loadout checkout** (`createSpaceLoadoutCheckout`) via new catalog bases `collective_base` ($79/$49 beta) and `independent_base` ($249 flat). `SpacePlan` already carried `collective`/`independent`, so the webhook reconciler + entitlements resolve them unchanged. New DB item keys `collective`/`independent` (`itemKeyForCatalogKey` + a CHECK-constraint migration) let their subscription-item rows persist the founding lock.
- **Gating unchanged.** Two new per-plan flags `plan_collective_enabled`/`plan_independent_enabled` (default OFF) join the existing switches. The go-live migration upserts `billing_live` + `tier_crew_enabled` + all four `plan_*_enabled` ON — **inert until `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is set in the server env** (the `billingLive()` env half) AND the operator runs the catalog sync at `/admin/pricing` (mints the new prices). Those two are the only owner-manual go-live steps.
- **Personal-event tickets** are now source-aware (0% on the host's own sale, member network rate on a network-sourced sale), so the "keep 100% of your own bookings" promise holds off-Space too (closes the ADR-811 audit's open #4).
- **Surfaces:** the Space billing plan-ladder offers a one-click Choose on each sellable higher rung for a free Space; the marketing pricing page prices Collective/Independent from the real catalog (no longer preview); the admin pricing console exposes all four plan switches.
- **Beta pricing auto-reverts on 2026-09-01 (`lib/pricing/beta.ts`).** The $19 Business / $49 Collective anchors are the *charged* price only until the cutover; after it, the loadout checkout resolves the `_list` price key instead of the founding key (both are minted active by the catalog sync, so it's a pure key switch — no re-sync). Beta subscribers are **grandfathered for life** (their locked founding price id re-bills before the window is ever consulted). Every price *surface* mirrors the same instant via `effectiveCatalogAmounts` (collapsing founding→list once beta ends, so the struck anchor + "Beta price, ends September 1" caption + the ladder's beta note all auto-clear). Machine-facing copy (SEO meta, FAQ schema, llms.txt) states the evergreen *list* prices; the beta lives only on the live, auto-reverting pricing surfaces. Owner-editable via the one `BETA_PRICING_ENDS_AT` constant.

## ADR-812 — Conversations: the unified ticketed-comms bedrock (2026-07-24)

**Status.** Accepted; foundation shipping (additive, behind flags). Full spec: `docs/COMMS-SYSTEM.md`.

**Context.** In-house communication was split across two half-systems: the CRM inbox (`lib/crm/inbox.ts`, a per-contact thread over `contact_interactions` with a dark inbound-email webhook) and the support ticket system (`support_tickets`/`support_ticket_messages`, ADR-159, with `assigned_to`, status, internal notes, and `listAssignableAgents()` but welded to a bug-report table). Neither alone gives a "leader emails the group below them, as themselves, and replies bounce back as tracked tickets" flow. All email is Resend via `enqueueEmail`; bulk sends from `noreply@send.frequencylocal.com`; campaign Reply-To already points at `hello@frequencylocal.com` (ADR-629).

**Decision.**
- **One conversation fabric.** A channel-agnostic `comms_conversations` + `comms_messages` spine is the single system of record for support, CRM, leader-to-member, and inbound replies. `contact_interactions` stays as a **write-through timeline mirror** (one write path, projected through `recordContactInteraction`), so the CRM card + person-stitch keep working unchanged. Support tickets fold in as `kind='support'` (linked now via `support_ticket_id`; renamed into `comms_conversations` with compatibility views in a later phase — additive first, no big-bang).
- **Agents = profiles** (unique id = `profiles.id`; no new identity table). `assigned_to` is the current agent; `comms_assignments` is an append-only "trade" audit (who → whom, when, why).
- **Reply-mode is a per-send choice** on `campaigns.reply_mode` (`broadcast` | `conversation`): broadcast = `noreply@`, no reply path, unsubscribe headers; conversation = a per-conversation Reply-To that routes the reply back to the exact thread.
- **The reply address is HMAC-derived from the conversation `ref`** (`lib/comms/reply-address.ts`, mirroring `lib/unsubscribe-tokens.ts`): `reply+<ref>-<hmac>@reply.frequencylocal.com` — unforgeable + non-enumerable, no stored token. Routing is by the plus-token (primary); `Message-ID`/`In-Reply-To`/`References` headers thread email clients (cosmetic, secondary).
- **Leader-as-themselves via the "via" pattern** (DKIM-aligned): `From: "<Leader> via Frequency" <people@people.frequencylocal.com>`, per-recipient conversation Reply-To. A leader's send fans out into **N individual tracked conversations** (not one blast), each attached to their sender trail (`owner_profile_id`).
- **Deliverability isolation by subdomain:** bulk `send.`, conversational `people.`, inbound `reply.`, fallback `hello@`. One-click unsubscribe on bulk only, never on 1:1.
- **AI seams designed now, built later:** a `conversations.ai` jsonb (draft/triage/summary/sentiment) + a `<VeraDraftButton>` composer slot; Vera replies are just `author_kind='vera'` messages. Every AI output lands in a human-editable field; every send/assign still runs the existing gated action.

**Alternatives.** (1) Bridge two tables forever — rejected: forces every reader to UNION two shapes; the goal is one inbox. (2) Rename `support_tickets`→`comms_conversations` up front — deferred, not rejected: correct end state but higher-risk as the first step; done as a later phase with compat views. (3) A dedicated agents table — rejected: duplicates identity; `profiles` already carries assignment + eligibility.

**Consequences.** New env: `CONVERSATION_TOKEN_SECRET`, `CONVERSATION_REPLY_DOMAIN`, `EMAIL_CONVERSATION_FROM`, `RESEND_INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `CRM_INBOX_OWNER_PROFILE_ID`. New DNS: MX on `reply.` → Resend inbound; verified `people.` sending identity; DMARC relaxed-alignment at the apex. Phased build (`docs/COMMS-SYSTEM.md`): (0) codec + schema [this], (1) send-path reply-mode branch + outbound-from-conversation, (2) inbound bridge + dedupe upgrade, (3) the unified inbox UX (reusing the shipped mobile Sheet/drill-down primitives), (4) leader→group flow, (5) AI seams. Each phase is additive and independently reviewable; nothing changes for existing sends until the reply-mode toggle is exposed and flipped.

## ADR-813 — Conversation batch + digest: quiet-time coalescing (2026-07-25)

**Status.** Accepted; shipped dormant (config-gated OFF by default). Full spec: `docs/COMMS-SYSTEM.md` (Phase 6). Extends ADR-812.

**Context.** With the ticketed 1:1 path live (ADR-812), two noise problems surface at volume: an operator typing several quick replies into one thread sends several separate emails, and a burst of member replies pings the operator once per reply. The ask: "only send a summary after an elapsed time" — batch my outbound sends into one email, and digest inbound replies to me.

**Decision.**
- **Two independent quiet-time windows, both `0` (off) by default:** `CONVERSATION_BATCH_WINDOW_MINUTES` (outbound) and `CONVERSATION_DIGEST_WINDOW_MINUTES` (inbound). One cron `/api/cron/conversation-batches` (every 5 min) runs both passes.
- **Outbound batch = queue-then-flush.** When the window is set, the three reply actions (admin / leader / space) append the message as `delivery_status='queued'` with `metadata.batch_from` and skip the immediate `enqueueEmail`; the message still shows in the workspace instantly. A debounce on the *newest* queued message in the thread means a settled burst flushes as **one** coalesced email under the original sender identity, then the rows flip to `sent`. When the window is `0` the action takes its **exact existing immediate-send branch** (byte-for-byte unchanged).
- **Inbound digest = watermark scan.** A per-conversation `last_digested_at` (new column) plus a 24h recency floor: the cron groups conversations with a fresh inbound reply (settled past the window, out-dating the watermark) by recipient (assignee, else owner) and emails **one** summary, advancing the watermark to the reply it summarized (so a later reply still out-dates it). The in-app `conversation_reply` notification is untouched — the digest only adds the batched email nudge.
- **Drain, don't strand.** The window governs the debounce, not whether we drain: the batch flush still sends already-queued mail when the window is later set back to `0`, so disabling can never strand a queued reply. At-least-once (enqueue → mark-sent), matching the outbox contract.

**Alternatives.** (1) A fixed delay from the *first* message rather than debounce on the newest — rejected: a debounce matches "after it goes quiet" and coalesces a genuine burst; a fixed delay splits a long burst across two emails. (2) Digest off `now` as the watermark — rejected: a reply arriving between the read and the write would be marked digested and lost; the per-conversation `last_inbound_at` watermark is race-safe. (3) A dedicated queue table — rejected: `delivery_status` already exists on `comms_messages`; queuing in place keeps the workspace view and the send ledger as one.

**Consequences.** New env (both optional, default off): `CONVERSATION_BATCH_WINDOW_MINUTES`, `CONVERSATION_DIGEST_WINDOW_MINUTES`. New schema: `comms_conversations.last_digested_at` + partial indexes for both scans (migration `20261211000000_conversations_digest_marker.sql`). New cron in `vercel.json`. Zero live impact until a window is set; the pure coalescer + window parsers are unit-tested (`lib/comms/outbound-batch.test.ts`).

## ADR-814 — Email bridge: two-way from your own inbox (2026-07-25)

**Status.** Accepted; shipped behind `CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE` (default off), and inert until inbound receiving is live. Full spec: `docs/COMMS-SYSTEM.md` (Phase 7). Extends ADR-812.

**Context.** ADR-812 makes 1:1 mail reply-able and threads member replies into the CRM inbox, but an operator still has to open the console to answer. The ask: it should be automatic both ways from a normal inbox — a member's reply lands in my email, I answer from Gmail/my phone, and it goes back to the member without a "customer service" step.

**Decision.**
- **Direction is decided by a secret-derived address, never by the From.** The reply-address codec (`lib/comms/reply-address.ts`) gains a `role`: the existing `member` token (signs `conv:<ref>`, address `reply+<ref>-<tag>@` — UNCHANGED, addresses in the wild keep validating) and a new `house` token (signs `conv:<ref>:house`, address `reply+<ref>.h-<tag>@`). A reply to the member address routes INBOUND; a reply to the house address routes OUTBOUND to the member. Because the two tags are distinct HMACs, a leaked member address can never send outbound, and a **spoofed From cannot flip direction** — the classic risk of "reply-by-email as the house" is closed by construction, so no SPF/DKIM trust is required.
- **Forward in, route out.** On a member reply (bridge on) the webhook forwards a copy to the assigned agent's (else owner's) real inbox, with `Reply-To` = the house address. When the agent replies from their mail app, that lands on the house address and `routeHouseReplyOutbound` records it as an outbound message and sends it onward to the member with `Reply-To` = the member address — closing the loop entirely over email.
- **Always honor a valid house token, even when the flag is off.** A house address can only exist because we emitted it while the bridge was on, so an agent's reply to an in-flight forward is never dropped after the flag is turned off; the flag gates only whether NEW member replies are forwarded.
- **Idempotent + loop-safe.** The outbound is deduped on the agent's inbound `Message-ID` (a provider redelivery never double-sends to the member); the existing RFC 3834 loop guard (`isAutomatedMessage`) runs before both roles, so a vacation responder on either side never threads.

**Alternatives.** (1) Classify house-vs-member by the From address + SPF/DKIM verdicts — rejected: spoofable / brittle across the many domains an agent might mail from; the dual-token address is unforgeable and needs no auth heuristics. (2) One address for both roles, distinguished by sender — rejected: same spoofing exposure, and it couples direction to a mutable field. (3) A provider auto-forward rule — rejected: loses the thread record and the tracked outbound.

**Consequences.** New env `CONVERSATION_EMAIL_BRIDGE` (default off) + the receiving prerequisites from ADR-812 (`RESEND_INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, MX on `reply.`). No schema change. Backward-compatible codec (member role unchanged); the role split + cross-role non-verification are unit-tested (`lib/comms/reply-address.test.ts`). Residual risk: a house address that leaks from an agent's mailbox could be used to send as the house on that one thread — bounded to one member, requires possession of a forwarded email, and is the same trust surface as the agent's mailbox itself. End-to-end behavior can only be verified once inbound receiving is configured.

## ADR-815 — Inbound is metadata-only: hydrate the body from Resend's Received Emails API (2026-07-25)

**Status.** Accepted; shipped. Fixes a latent gap in ADR-812 Phase 2 before inbound goes live.

**Context.** ADR-812's inbound router parsed the reply body/headers straight from the `email.received` webhook payload. Resend's `email.received` webhook is **metadata-only** — it carries the received-email `id`, `from`, `to`, `subject`, `created_at`, and attachment metadata, but **no body, no headers**. The full content must be fetched from the Received Emails API (`GET /emails/receiving/{id}`, SDK `resend.emails.receiving.get(id)`). Without that fetch, every reply would thread with an empty body, no loop-guard headers (`Auto-Submitted`/`Precedence`), and no dedupe key (`Message-ID`) — i.e. inbound would be broken the moment receiving went live.

**Decision.** A new `loadInboundMessage(payload, fetcher?)` (`lib/comms/inbound.ts`) wraps the pure `parseInboundMessage`: when the payload carries a received-email id but no inline body, it fetches the full email (`fetchReceivedEmail` in `lib/email.ts`, the single Resend integration point) and merges `text`/`html`/`headers`/`message_id` over the webhook metadata before parsing. The webhook route calls it instead of the bare parser. Fail-safe: if the fetch fails, or a provider DOES inline the body, it falls back to the raw payload (the reply still records so the thread reopens + the agent is notified, just without the body text). The fetcher is dependency-injected so the merge is unit-tested without network.

**Alternatives.** (1) Subscribe to a different webhook that includes the body — rejected: Resend does not offer one; metadata-only + fetch is the documented contract. (2) Fetch inside `parseInboundMessage` — rejected: keeps a pure, unit-tested parser IO-free; the IO belongs in the `load*` wrapper. (3) 5xx to force redelivery when the fetch fails — rejected for v1: risks redelivery loops; recording metadata (reply visible, body empty) is a safer degradation, and the daemon-name loop guard still catches bounces without headers.

**Consequences.** No new env or schema. `fetchReceivedEmail` uses the installed `resend` SDK (v6.17.2) `emails.receiving.get`. The hydration + no-double-fetch + failure-fallback paths are unit-tested (`lib/comms/inbound.test.ts`). Still gated on the operator wiring receiving (MX on `reply.`, `RESEND_INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`); this change is what makes a real reply arrive with its actual text.

## ADR-816 — Anonymous live-chat over a capability-token Broadcast channel (2026-07-25)

**Status.** Accepted; shipped behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT` (default off). Full spec: `docs/COMMS-SYSTEM.md` + `docs/MESSAGING-PLATFORM.md`. Extends ADR-812; reuses the Broadcast typing hook from the messaging platform.

**Context.** The ask: a real-time, platform-wide "chat with Frequency" widget, open to anonymous visitors, with a live typing indicator — and it should land in the same Conversations inbox as email tickets. The existing realtime systems (DMs, Rooms) are authenticated and RLS-gated via `postgres_changes`, which an anonymous visitor cannot use (no `auth.uid()`), and the messaging-platform doc already establishes the split: Broadcast for ephemeral/<50ms, `postgres_changes` for durable-with-RLS.

**Decision.**
- **A live chat is just a conversation on the comms spine** (`channel='in_app'`, platform-scoped, owned by `CRM_INBOX_OWNER_PROFILE_ID`), so it threads, assigns, and logs on the contact card exactly like email — one inbox for both.
- **Capability-token Broadcast, not postgres_changes.** The visitor gets an HMAC token over their conversation `ref` (`lib/comms/chat-token.ts`, distinct derivation from the reply-address tokens). That token (a) gates the token-only server actions that persist / load history, and (b) **names the Realtime Broadcast channel `chat:<token>`** — unguessable, so it is the access control for an anonymous, RLS-less channel. Both the visitor widget and the operator bridge join the same channel; messages + typing fan out peer-to-peer, while the server actions persist the durable transcript (the source of truth on reload). This sidesteps anonymous-RLS entirely.
- **Both ends live.** The visitor widget (`components/chat/support-chat-widget.tsx`, mounted platform-wide) and the operator `LiveChatBridge` (swapped in for the email composer when a thread's `channel='in_app'`) share one `useSupportChat` hook + the existing `useTypingIndicator`; each passes its own `persist` (visitor → inbound, staff → outbound).
- **Anonymous-safe.** Public actions are token-gated + rate-limited (Upstash), bodies are length-capped and rendered as text (never HTML), and the whole surface is dark unless `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT` is enabled.

**Alternatives.** (1) `postgres_changes` + Supabase anonymous auth — rejected for v1: heavier (anon sessions + per-visitor RLS) than a capability channel that needs no identity. (2) Poll a server action — rejected: no live typing, worse latency. (3) A separate chat table — rejected: the comms spine already gives threading, assignment, and the unified inbox.

**Consequences.** New env `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_CHAT` (default off). No schema change (`in_app` is an existing `channel` value). Realtime cannot be verified in CI — the token codec is unit-tested; the live loop needs preview testing (two browsers).
