## ADR-855 — A ticketed event's price lives on its tiers, so structured data must read the tier authority (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The schema.org `Event` emitted by `lib/jsonld.eventSchema` priced its `Offer` from `events.price_cents`. A ticketed event does not store its price there: it prices on its ACTIVE TIERS in `event_ticket_types`, and `events.price_cents` stays null for those events. The result was that every tier-priced event published `isAccessibleForFree: true` with a `$0.00` offer, on both the canonical `/events/<slug>` page and `/discover/events/<slug>`, while the page itself rendered the real price.

That is worse than a cosmetic bug. It is a Google structured-data mismatch (the markup contradicts the visible page, which is a manual-action risk for the whole property), it advertises paid events as free in rich results and to AI answer engines, and it is invisible from inside the code that emits it, because `price_cents` is a real column with a plausible value of null.

**Decision.** `eventSchema` takes an optional `ticket_from_cents` supplied by the caller from the tier authority (`ticketFromPriceCents`, already the pricing function behind the Tickets rail), and prefers it over the column.

The field is deliberately **three-state**, and the distinction is the whole point:

| Value | Meaning | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `undefined` | the caller supplied no tier data | fall back to `events.price_cents` (untiered events are unchanged) |
| `null` | the event IS tiered and every active tier is free | free, and it must NOT fall through to the column |
| number | the cheapest active tier's effective price | that price |

A plain `??` collapses the middle case back onto `price_cents` and silently re-introduces the bug, so the code tests `!== undefined` explicitly and both callers spread the key in conditionally rather than passing it always.

**Alternatives considered.** (1) *Have `eventSchema` read the tiers itself.* Rejected: `lib/jsonld` is a pure, dependency-light formatting module with no database access, and giving it one would make every JSON-LD call a query. (2) *Backfill `events.price_cents` from the tiers.* Rejected: it duplicates an authority instead of reading it, and the copy goes stale the moment a tier price changes. (3) *Only fix the canonical page.* Rejected: `/discover/events/<slug>` emits its own JSON-LD, and two surfaces publishing different prices for one event is the failure we are trying to remove.

**Consequences.** `ticketFromPriceCents` now takes only the four pricing fields it reads rather than a whole `TierRow`, so any caller holding active tiers can reuse it; it is the one pricing authority for both surfaces. The `/discover` enrichment read is fail-soft by construction: no tiers, or a read the anon role cannot satisfy, simply omits the field and restores the previous `price_cents` behaviour rather than asserting a wrong price. Three tests in `lib/jsonld.test.ts` cover the three states; the two that describe the new behaviour were confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix module.

The durable rule: **structured data reads the same authority the page renders from.** If a price, date, or availability is computed for the UI, the JSON-LD takes that computed value, never a column that happens to sit nearby.

## ADR-856 — The migration ledger is a bijection with the repo, and every database privilege names its verified caller (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** Closing out the meta scan's four "needs your call" database decisions surfaced two structural facts. First, the pre-2026-09-13 ledger divergence was not cosmetic as recorded: set comparison showed **296 repo migration files absent from the ledger** (renamed during a historical filename rewrite while the ledger kept the original timestamps) alongside 477 ledger rows with no repo file. An unledgered repo file is a loaded gun — any future `supabase migration up` would re-apply it against a schema that already contains it. Second, re-verifying the status doc's claims against the live catalog and the code found two of them stale: `circle_momentum` IS called on the authed client by a member-facing surface, and `resonance_neighbors` / `mkt_interest_demand` are called via the service role, not "never called".

**Decision.** Four moves, each verified before and after:

1. **Ledger reconciled to exact bijection (549 ⇄ 549).** Every one of the 296 missing versions was proven applied first: 261 by name lineage to an orphan row, 33 by checking a signature object from the file against the live catalog, and 2 (the practice-tiers pair) by the later `retire_practice_intensity_tiers` migration that deliberately drops their objects. Then, with repo ⊆ ledger established, the 477 orphans were deleted in the same transaction, guarded by an in-transaction assertion that aborts unless exactly 549 rows remain. The full pre-surgery ledger is archived at `docs/maintenance/ledger-archive-2026-07-27.json`; any row can be restored by inserting it back verbatim.
2. **Function privileges follow verified callers** (`20270104000000`). `circle_momentum`: anon revoked, authenticated kept (the live member surface). `resonance_neighbors` and `mkt_interest_demand`: service-role only — the SQL functions that call `resonance_neighbors` are SECURITY DEFINER, so their inner calls are ACL-checked as the function owner and are unaffected. The first attempt revoked from `anon` alone and changed nothing, because functions are granted to PUBLIC by default; the durable form is **revoke from PUBLIC, then grant the verified roles explicitly**.
3. **The duplicate `record_qr_scan` dropped.** The 8-arg form already defaults `p_variant` to null, so the 7-arg twin existed only to swallow variant attribution when a call omitted the parameter.
4. **All 19 advisor-flagged FKs indexed** (same migration). Every one points at `profiles`, `spaces`, or `contacts` — tables the product genuinely deletes from — and all arrived with #1961's new tables, so the indexes were created against empty-or-tiny tables for free.

**Alternatives considered.** *Leave the pre-0913 divergence documented* (the meta scan's original call): rejected once the direction of the drift was measured — 296 re-appliable files is a correctness risk, not cosmetics. *Delete orphans without inserting the missing versions first*: rejected as actively dangerous; bijection requires the insert half to come first. *Index only the cascade-parent FKs*: rejected because all 19 hit delete-bearing parents and the marginal cost at current row counts is nil.

**Consequences.** `supabase migration up` is now a no-op against prod, as it should be. The advisor's `unindexed_foreign_keys` INFO goes to zero. The `/maintenance` skill now checks ledger ⇄ repo parity as version sets in both directions and instructs the operator to rename the MCP's apply-timestamp ledger row to the repo version after every `apply_migration` — the tool records its own timestamp, which is the exact mechanism that manufactured this drift class twice in one day.

The durable rules: **a migration exists in exactly two places — as a repo file and as a ledger row with the same version — and anything else is drift**; and **a database privilege is not "locked down" until `has_function_privilege` says so for the role in question**, because a role-specific revoke under a standing PUBLIC grant is a no-op.

## ADR-857 — A circle attached to a Space makes its events that Space's events (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** Two asks: attach a Circle to a Space, and make events assignable to both the circle and the space. Most of the machinery already existed — `circles.space_id` (tenancy, root = personal), the two-sided transfer gate (ADR-843), the Space circles console, and events carrying independent `scope_id`/`scope_type` (circle axis) and `space_id` (space placement axis). What was missing was the connective tissue: no UI path moved an existing personal circle INTO a space (the gate allowed it; nothing called it), and every circle-event writer stamped `space_id = root` even when the circle belonged to a Space — so a Space's own circles' events never appeared on the Space calendar, which filters by `events.space_id`.

**Decision.** The space follows the circle; an event is never assigned to a circle and a space independently.

1. **Attach = the existing transfer.** `attachCircleToSpaceAction` is the inbound twin of the outbound move: the caller must edit the destination Space, and `transferCircle`'s ADR-843 gate stays the sole authority on the source side (host of a personal circle, or steward of its owning Space). The picker (`listAttachableCirclesAction` over `listCirclesHostedBy`) only shapes the offer. No new permission model, no new table.
2. **Placement derives from the circle.** One helper, `spaceIdForCircle`, is the single derivation, and all four circle-event writers stamp through it (member create, admin create, circle scaffold events, both Journey-run sites). A circle event therefore lands on the circle page (read by `scope_id`) AND the owning Space's calendar (read by `space_id`). A personal circle derives root — byte-identical to prior behaviour.
3. **Calendars follow the circle.** `transferCircle` and the handoff accept restamp the circle's events (`scope_type='circle' and scope_id=<circle>`) to the destination space (root on a move to a person), best-effort after the authoritative ownership write. Without this, the old Space keeps showing — and gating, under space isolation — events of a circle it no longer owns.
4. **History swept onto the invariant** (`20270105000000`, applied): idempotent backfill setting each circle event's `space_id` to its circle's. The restrictive `can_view_space_content` starting to apply to restamped rows is the correct tightening, not a regression: a private Space's circle is already invisible to non-members via the identical restrictive policy on `circles` — the events matching the circle's own boundary is the point.

**Alternatives considered.** *Independent circle+space pickers on the event form*: rejected — it invents a cross product the ownership model cannot answer (whose event is a circle-A-in-space-B event when B does not own A?), and `event_space_shares` already covers the legitimate "also on that calendar" case. *A `space_circles` join table (multi-space circles)*: rejected as scope creep; one owner per circle is ADR-843's model and nothing today needs more. *Deriving in a DB trigger instead of the writers*: rejected — the app-layer helper keeps the derivation visible, testable, and consistent with how `stampCircleSpaceId`/`stampEventSpaceId` already work.

**Consequences.** The event form's circle options now say when a circle lives in a Space ("circle in {space}"), so the dual placement is visible at the moment of choice. `lib/circles/circle-space-events.test.ts` locks both halves — functional (derivation + both restamp directions) and source-shape (every writer references the helper), all confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix tree. One adjacent defect found during verification is recorded in META-SCAN-STATUS rather than fixed here: `placement-actions.ts` writes `scope_circle_id` alone, which the `sync_event_scope_arc` trigger does not propagate back to `scope_id`, leaving such events invisible to the circle-membership RLS disjunct.

The durable rule: **an event's space placement is a derived fact, not an assigned one — it derives from whoever owns the event's home.** Writers stamp it through the one helper; moves restamp it; nothing else touches it.

## ADR-858 — The Space Message center: audiences are rosters, channels are lanes, and every chip tells the truth (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** A Space had three disconnected comms surfaces (ticketed Conversations inbox, email campaigns, CRM board) and no way to send one message to the people it actually organizes: its members, a paid tier, one of its circles, or an event's guest list. The scope-agnostic four-channel composer already existed and was wired only on events.

**Decision.** One console at `/spaces/<slug>/messages`, bound to Space-shaped audiences and lanes:

- **Audiences are the canonical rosters**, never parallel lists: all members (`listActiveSpaceMemberIds`), a tier's active `space_memberships`, a circle's CRM roster, an event's Message Attendees set. The action re-resolves the audience server-side from segment keys (ADR-274). One selected circle or event stamps the comms scope spine; anything wider is a space-wide send on the tenancy lane — `'space'` is deliberately not a `scope_kind`.
- **Email rides the Space's own campaign machinery**, so the whole anti-spam battery applies unchanged (kill switch, daily cap, marketing consent, topic mutes, suppression, RFC 8058). Topic `'marketing'`: a free-form member blast is held to the strictest consent bar.
- **DM**: the loop that was copy-pasted across the event and journey composers is now ONE helper (`lib/comms/bulk-dm.ts`) used by all three, byte-equivalent (cap 300 refuse-first, block gates, email-keyed threads). `scoped-dm` gains the `'space'` scope with a leadership/membership gate mirroring the circle one.
- **Dispatch becomes a first-class Space audience**: `dispatches.audience_scope` gains `'space'` (`20270106000000`, applied), the rail and digest readers union the member's spaces, and push fan-out reaches active members through the same preference-gated path events use.
- **Text is refuse-first** (ADR-256): a disabled chip that says so, and a server that refuses a smuggled request. The consent ledger exists; A2P provisioning does not.

**Consequences.** The menu row extends `SPACE_MODULES` beside its inbound sibling Conversations. Known deferred items: member-audience email keys on contact consent rather than `notification_preferences` (the same asymmetry the event lane has); recipient email resolution is per-profile auth reads, acceptable under the DM cap but worth batching before five-figure audiences.

The durable rule: **an audience is a read of the roster that already governs the surface, and a channel chip is disabled with a reason or enabled with a destination — never decorative.**

---

## ADR-859 — A membership tier includes a circle, and the lifecycle keeps it true (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The owner's model: a Space runs a circle per membership tier; the circle is that group's communications hub; private events attach to the circle; access comes from the membership. Everything existed except the tier→circle edge and any entitlement-driven circle membership.

**Decision.** `space_membership_tiers.circle_id` (one circle per tier) plus provenance on the grant: `memberships.granted_by_tier_id` (`20270107000000`, applied). The sync engine (`lib/spaces/tier-circle.ts`) grants on activate and revokes on lapse at all five lifecycle sites (free join, waitlist promote, member/admin cancel, both Stripe webhook branches, tier switch = revoke old + grant new).

Why durable rows when ADR-823 chose a live gate for tickets: a ticket gate is a checkout-time question; circle membership is what the product reads everywhere else — `member_count`, the roster, the comms audience, and the `get_my_circle_ids()` RLS that gates `circle_only` events. The provenance column is what makes durable rows safe: **revoke deletes only rows the tier created; a self-joined member is never evicted by a billing event.** A full circle never fails a paid membership (the grant reports `circle_full` and continues). Linking a tier sweeps current members in, so new links self-heal and no backfill migration exists.

Fixed en route because the feature made it load-bearing: `cancelMembership` never cancelled the Stripe subscription, so a member cancel kept billing and the next webhook re-asserted `active` — which would have silently re-granted circle access. It now cancels best-effort before the DB flip.

**Consequences.** Operator UI is the Circle access panel in Memberships settings (mirrors ADR-824's Event access). Deleting a tier releases its rows to the members (`ON DELETE SET NULL`) rather than evicting them. Two recorded limits: `past_due` keeps access (existing consumer behavior, documented on `hasActiveSpaceMembership`); and `circle_only` event RLS also requires platform tier `crew`+, so a paid Space member on a free platform account cannot see tier-circle events — widening that disjunct is a separate, deliberate decision.

The durable rule: **entitlement-granted state carries provenance, and revocation follows provenance — never breadth.**

## ADR-860 — Menus: the sync only ever inserts, so code must stay the source of truth it re-enters through (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted (first tranche shipped; the backlog is in META-SCAN-STATUS).

**Context.** The operator reported the Menu manager "isn't synced up" with submenu items needing reorganization. The audit found the mechanism: opening the manager materializes a surface into `menu_*` rows, and from then on the sync ONLY inserts new hrefs — it never updates a label, href, gate, or grouping, and menus seeded before the baseline column existed swallowed every page added since. Identity is href-only, so a route rename strands the old row and blocks the new one; injected items lose their sub-group (categories are matched top-level only); and the public header's code defaults had silently lost two of their six documented triggers.

**Decision.** Two-sided repair. **Code:** the header regains The Community and Spaces triggers (with the REAL `/for/<niche>` slugs); retired names leave the nav catalogs (Dispatches, Market); the payouts row gets its own destination instead of a duplicate href; profile renderers flatten child categories like the rail already did; the sync creates categories on the full parent path with the default's access copied, and positions append at `max+1`. **Data:** the live header's dead `/for/*` doors were re-pointed at the real slugs, the Spaces/About category-position collision resolved, the stranded pricing item re-homed, retired labels updated, and the profile surface — two default rows surviving, ten swallowed — was emptied so `getMenu` falls back to full code defaults.

**Consequences.** The deeper redesign is recorded, not smuggled: a non-destructive "re-check for new pages" action, `default_key`-based sync identity, per-item drift badges, the mobile marketing menu reading the resolved menu, and an `admin_header` code-vs-DB drift guard. Until those land, the operational rule stands in the manager's docs: **a code-side nav change reaches a materialized surface only by explicit re-sync or reset — check the surface after shipping nav changes.**

## ADR-861 — Roommate matching explains itself, and the housing surface reactivates its dark half (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The housing audit found the finder's best pieces dark or broken: person-to-person roommate matching fully built with zero UI; the seeker form silently wiping lifestyle preferences on every re-save (killing the 15% lifestyle term); member listings never geocoded (degrading the 15% geo term and excluding them from proximity reads); results showing a bare percentage nobody can act on; no edit route; a favorites table with zero code; and a consent asymmetry where listing matching ignored `opted_out_as_target` while person matching honored it.

**Decision.** Matching v3 (`20270108000000`, applied): both RPCs keep the v2 blend and now also return the raw budget/geo/timing/lifestyle fit terms, and the listing RPC gains the reciprocal consent join the person RPC always had. The UI renders the terms as up to three plain chips ("Budget fits", "Close by", "Timing lines up", "Similar lifestyle") — **resonance and astrology are never chipped**: one is opaque, the other is doubly-opt-in-sensitive; both stay inside the overall score only. The roommate page becomes two tabs, Rooms and People, the People tab finally mounting the person-to-person RPC through profile cards that show match, city, and chips — deliberately **not** other seekers' budget ranges, which would widen the RPC's coarse-city-and-score-band privacy contract; budget compatibility surfaces only as the chip. The lifestyle wipe is fixed by an exact inverse of the sanitizer (`seekerPreferencesToLifestyle`, round-trip-tested to a fixed point). Creates now geocode best-effort; owners get an edit route with an owner-scoped `updateListing`; `listing_saves` gets its heart and saved view; housing JSON-LD gains bedrooms, bathrooms, floor size, amenities, and per-month `UnitPriceSpecification` while `addressLocality` stays the only address field.

**Corrections made against live truth.** The audited "never-revoked `housing_rentals_near`" does not exist on prod (an earlier orphan cleanup dropped it) — the migration records that instead of issuing a failing REVOKE. And the first apply of this migration was a placeholder error (ledgered, not executed); the real body was executed immediately after and verified by reading the function signatures back. Both are examples of the same rule: **the live catalog outranks any document, including our own audits.**

**Consequences.** Tier B (richer listing fields behind an address-precision setting) and the `/housing` namespace move are next, recorded in the plan. The fair-housing posture is unchanged and must stay deliberate: gender/age fields remain gated to shared living and unscored, and any future hard filter must branch on arrangement type.

The durable rule: **a match score a member can act on names its reasons in plain words, and never names another member's private numbers.**

## ADR-862 — Housing moves to /housing, off the retired marketplace namespace (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** ADR-596 retired "Marketplace" as a member word, splitting commerce into Classifieds, Market, Frequency Store, and Shop. Housing kept the last member-facing `/marketplace/*` URL (`/marketplace/housing`), an inconsistency the housing audit flagged to fix BEFORE the surface grew in Tier B rather than after, when more inbound links and indexed URLs would exist.

**Decision.** The whole housing subtree moves to `/housing` (index, detail, edit, new, roommates), with `git mv` preserving history. `/marketplace/housing` and `/marketplace/housing/:path*` 308-redirect permanently, so indexed URLs and shared links survive. Every reference updated in one pass — nav areas, the crawler-gate pattern, search destinations, the sitemap (now emitting `/housing/<id>`), canonical/JSON-LD bases, breadcrumbs, the member-footer seed, the commerce components' base paths, and the live `menu_items`/`menu_rail_cards` rows. The mandate's `/housing` (a top-level route, matching NAMING's pattern) was chosen over META-SCAN-STATUS's earlier `/market/housing` suggestion.

**Consequences.** Two follow-ups recorded, not smuggled: `/marketplace/events` is still member-linked, so housing was not literally the last `/marketplace/*` URL — that surface deserves its own ADR-596 pass; and the breadcrumb umbrella still labels all four commerce surfaces "Marketplace", a pre-existing retired-word use left untouched here because changing it is a breadcrumb-taxonomy decision, not a routing one. The housing breadcrumb pin stays: all four surfaces are deliberately pinned to a uniform trail, and auto-derivation would hide them as single-crumb pages.

The durable rule: **a namespace rename moves before the surface grows, and moves completely — routes, redirects, sitemap, canonicals, nav data, and the live menu rows in one atomic change, never a slow drift.**

## ADR-863 — The privacy review of the message center and the housing match RPCs (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** An adversarial security pass over the session's new surfaces — the Space Message center (ADR-858), the tier→circle lifecycle (ADR-859), and the housing/roommate build-out (ADR-861) — turned up five confirmed data-flow defects, each one a place where a value the member never consented to expose could reach an operator or another member, or where a cap the schema promised was not actually enforced on one code path.

**Decision.** Five fixes, each closing a specific leak:

1. **The email lane emails Space contacts, not auth accounts.** `broadcast-actions.ts` resolved its recipients through `admin.auth.admin.getUserById`, writing members' *account* emails into the operator-visible send ledger — an identity a member never handed the Space. It now resolves through `resolveContactEmails(spaceId, profileIds)`, a single batched read of the `contacts` table scoped to `space_id` and deduped by `profile_id`. A source-shape guard (`message-center-privacy.test.ts`) fails the build if `getUserById`/`auth.admin` ever reappear in the send path.
2. **The circle cap is re-checked on reactivation.** `grantCircleRow`'s reactivation branch (a lapsed membership rejoining a tier's circle) flipped a soft-deleted row back to active without re-counting, so a circle could exceed `member_cap` by readmitting past members. It now reads `circles.member_cap`, counts active memberships, and returns `{granted:false, reason:'circle_full'}` before the UPDATE.
3. **The person-to-person match RPC stops emitting raw fit terms.** `housing_roommate_matches` returned `budget_fit`, `geo_fit`, and `timing_fit` as continuous scores — enough for a viewer to back out another member's budget band, rough location, and move timing. The migration `20270109000000_housing_roommate_fit_privacy.sql` returns `null::double precision` for those three terms (they still feed the internal composite score) and bands `lifestyle_fit` to {0, 0.5, 1.0}. The listing-candidate RPC `housing_match_candidates` is untouched — a listing is public by design.
4. **Recipient resolution moved past the cap.** The email lane no longer resolves the full audience up front (one auth call each) before any cap or lane runs; each lane resolves only what it needs, when it needs it.
5. **Editing a listing re-geocodes.** `housing/[id]/edit/actions.ts` re-geocodes `[neighborhood, city]` on save (as create already did), so changing the city no longer leaves the old coordinates behind to score `geo_fit` and proximity against the wrong place forever. Best-effort: a geocode miss leaves coordinates untouched rather than blocking the save.

**Consequences.** Both migrations (`20270108000000`, `20270109000000`) are applied to prod and recorded in the ledger under their repo timestamps (555 rows, bijection intact per `check:migrations`). The deployed `housing_roommate_matches` emits `null::double precision as budget_fit`, verified against prod. Fit terms 3 remains the only member-facing behavior change: a viewer sees *whether* a candidate fits on lifestyle (three bands) and the composite score, never the raw budget/geo/timing numbers.

The durable rule: **a value the member gave for one purpose is not yours to surface for another — an auth email is not a contact email, a continuous fit score is a de-anonymizer, and a cap the schema declares must be enforced on every path that admits a member, reactivation included.**

## ADR-864 — Programs live on Channels: a Channel is a focus area, and a Program is a Channel with a blueprint (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder wants to host franchise-style community models — "Meld — Community Coworking", "MoFlow" — where one canonical brand hosts many independent local groups that members start themselves, discoverable by "find one near you" and "start your own". Both Frequency and Collective business members must be able to run one. The obvious names were all taken (Collective = a Space membership plan, Hub = the Circle→Hub→Nexus tree, Channel = locked to "the topical forum feature only"), and the obvious shapes were all wrong: a `parent_circle_id` self-join would make circles carry a fourth parent and collide with the Hub tree, and a new standalone `programs` table would duplicate a container the schema already had.

**Decision.** Three moves, one of them a canon change:

1. **The Channel canon broadens** from "the topical forum feature ONLY" to **a focus area**: a Channel hosts circles (`circles.topical_channel_id`, already live), carries the forum feed (now one module *inside* a Channel, not its definition), and can run as a Program. Hub and Nexus stay reserved for the geographic tree; "tune in" stays the Channel verb.
2. **A Program is a Channel with two nullable columns**, not a new entity: `topical_channels.template_id` (the Chapter blueprint, a `circle_templates` row) makes it a Program; `topical_channels.owner_space_id` says who runs it (NULL = Frequency-run, set = a Collective business member's Space). `circle_templates.owner_space_id` distinguishes Space-owned blueprints from the staff-authored Starter Circle catalog, and every catalog read filters `owner_space_id IS NULL` so a Program blueprint never appears in the global Starter Circles rail. Migration `20270110000000`, applied to prod (ledger 556, bijection intact).
3. **A Chapter is a circle in the Program's channel** — nothing new is invented. "Start a Chapter" = the existing Remix flow (`remixTemplate` → draft → publish) with the draft stamped `topical_channel_id`; "find a Chapter near you" = the chapters' own coordinates ranked by the existing Haversine helper; creating a Space-run Program snapshots the Space's flagship circle into the blueprint and stamps that circle in as the first Chapter. The operator surface is one new universal `SpaceFunctionKey` (`'program'`) + one `SPACE_MODULES` catalog row per the locked menu contract (ADR-553), gated admin-and-up, with the Collective plan note riding the same tier seam every plan-flavored function uses.

**Consequences.** The word **Program** is now locked for the umbrella and **Chapter** for the local instance (NAMING §Community structure); "Chapter" is Program-framing only — the entity remains a Circle everywhere else. The founding seven Channels stay platform-curated and render exactly as before (a channel without a blueprint shows zero difference). Frequency-run Programs are administered through the existing staff channel tooling; Space-run Programs through the Space console's Program module. V1 has no Program edit/delete surface — the create is the commitment, and changes go through the crew.

The durable rule: **when a new product idea looks like a new hierarchy, check whether an existing container plus one discriminating column already expresses it — the schema you don't add is the collision you don't manage.**

## ADR-865 — The Programs review: owned blueprints are not Starters, and one Program per Space (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The adversarial review of ADR-864 (run before merge; the PR merged while fixes were in flight) confirmed four defects: (1) a Space's Program blueprint rendered publicly at `/circles/starter/[slug]` as staff content and was claimable through the open remix action, minting off-Program copies with no Chapter stamp; (2) nothing plan-gated Program creation, so any self-serve Space admin could mint network-wide public channels, a bar that used to be staff-only; (3) `startChapter` ignored `topical_channels.is_active`, so a retired Program still accepted Chapters via direct action replay; (4) `createSpaceProgram` is two inserts with no transaction and no duplicate guard, so a double submit could mint two public channels or strand a public orphaned blueprint, with no v1 surface to remediate either.

**Decision.** Four fixes:

1. **Owned blueprints never surface as Starters.** `CircleTemplate` now carries `ownerSpaceId`; the Starter preview 404s an owned blueprint and `remixTemplateAction` refuses one ("This blueprint belongs to a Program. Start a Chapter from its Channel instead."). The single-template reads stay open — `startChapter` is the one sanctioned path into an owned blueprint, and it stamps the Chapter into the Program.
2. **Program creation rides the plan ladder.** The `program` function's entitlement key is `'program'`, added to the Collective depth set (`COLLECTIVE_DEPTH_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS`), and the settings surface + action resolve through `spaceFunctionAccessLive` — so when billing goes live, running a Program is Collective-and-up by the same seam as every plan-gated function. While billing is OFF the seam stays permissive by the ADR-370 invariant; the cap below bounds the beta exposure.
3. **A retired Program takes no new Chapters.** `startChapter` reads `is_active` and refuses an inactive channel; the page's 404 is UX, the action check is the authority (ADR-274 posture).
4. **One Program per Space, enforced at the database.** Migration `20270112000000` adds a unique partial index on `topical_channels(owner_space_id)`; the action pre-checks for a sentence-shaped error, and a channel-insert failure now deletes the just-written blueprint so nothing public is ever stranded.

**Consequences.** Ledger at 557, bijection intact. Seventeen data-layer tests (three new: inactive-channel refusal, duplicate-Program refusal, orphan cleanup) plus two source-shape guards pinning the Starter page and remix action gates. The scale story changes from "any Space, any number" to "one Program per Space, Collective depth once billing is live" — a Space that outgrows one Program is a crew conversation, which is exactly where v1 wants that decision.

The durable rule: **every read path to a tenant-owned artifact is a render surface — guard the artifact where it renders and where it is claimed, not just where it is listed.**

## ADR-866 — Events leaves the retired marketplace namespace by merging into /events (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** ADR-862 moved housing to `/housing` and flagged `/marketplace/events` as the remaining member-linked `/marketplace/*` URL, deserving the same ADR-596 pass. The audit found it was not a housing-shaped problem: `/marketplace/events` was not a distinct surface with its own data but a literal twin of `/events` — one wrapper page rendering the same `EventsSurface` on the same `getEventsIndexData`, with the same header cluster, whose canonical already pointed at `/events`. Ticketed events already have their commerce projection inside Market's Tickets group (NAMING: a Ticket is a Market projection of a ticketed event), and ADR-596 explicitly rejected separate event/ticket verticals, so no rename target exists that NAMING would bless.

**Decision.** Merge, not move. The duplicate route is deleted (no `git mv` — the surviving surface already lives at `/events` with its own history; moving a copy onto it is impossible and unnecessary), and `/marketplace/events` + `/marketplace/events/:path*` 308-redirect permanently to `/events`, beside the housing pair in `next.config.ts`. The commerce hub keeps its Events tab — `MarketplaceFacets` and `MarketplaceGuide` now point it at `/events` — exactly as the Housing tab points at `/housing`. `EventsSurface`'s `basePath` contract narrows to `'/events'` so the retired route cannot silently come back as a prop value. Sitemap, search destinations, crawler gate, JSON-LD, robots, page-chrome, and the nav registry already knew only `/events`, verified by grep rather than assumed; the repo's menu seeds carry no old href, and a guarded UPDATE for any live `menu_items`/`menu_rail_cards` rows is written to `scripts/adr-866-marketplace-events-menu-rows.sql` (run separately against prod, no-op if none exist).

**Consequences.** Events WAS the last member-facing `/marketplace/*` URL: what remains under the namespace is only aliases — the `/marketplace` and `/marketplace/new` redirect pages and the three redirect pairs — plus the operator-only `/admin/marketplace` console, which ADR-596 never renamed. `/events` stays unpinned in breadcrumbs: it is the member events home the commerce hub links OUT to, not a fifth commerce surface, so the pinned "Marketplace > …" trail does not extend over it — and the breadcrumb umbrella label itself stays out of scope here, same as ADR-862. Duplicate-content risk goes to zero instead of being managed by canonicals: one URL, one page, one set of signals.

The durable rule: **before moving a surface off a retired namespace, check whether it is a surface at all — a route that renders another route's data and canonicals to it is a duplicate to retire, and a redirect beats a rename nobody can justify from the naming canon.**

## ADR-867 — Housing Tier B: richer listing facts behind a member-chosen address precision (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The housing audit's Tier B mandate, queued in ADR-861: the listing form captured the Phase-2 basics but none of the facts a renter actually decides on (parking, laundry, move-in costs beyond the deposit, stay bounds, occupancy, accessibility), and the location model was one-size-fits-all — every listing showed whatever neighborhood+city the member typed, with no way to be either more private (city only) or more forthcoming (a street address for serious, signed-in inquirers). Tier A had already standardized the surface (fit chips, edit route, favorites) and ADR-862 moved it to /housing, so the surface was ready to grow.

**Decision.** Migration `20270111000000_housing_tier_b.sql` (written this session, **applied by the main session** — file only here) extends `housing_listings` with nine columns: `parking` and `laundry` (CHECK-constrained enums), `bathrooms_shared`, `move_in_costs_cents`, `min_stay_months`, `max_occupants`, `accessibility` (a jsonb array CHECK-contained in seven known tags), and the privacy pair `address_precision` (`city`|`neighborhood`|`exact`, default `city`) + `address_line` (capped at 200 chars). Every column is a fact about the HOME — the fair-housing posture of ADR-861 admits no tenant-demographic field, ever.

The privacy model lives in one pure resolver, `resolveAddressDisplay` (lib/listings/housing.ts): `city` shows the city only, `neighborhood` adds the neighborhood, and `exact` reveals `address_line` to signed-in viewers only, server-checked on the detail page. Public output is safe by construction on three layers: `listingDetailFromHousing` computes its place line as a signed-out viewer (so meta descriptions and JSON-LD `addressLocality` can never carry the address), `upsertHousingDetail` refuses to store an `address_line` under a coarser precision (a stale address is a leak waiting for a display bug), and source-shape tests fail the build if `address_line`/`addressLine` ever appears in the SEO module or the sitemap. Both actions re-whitelist the enums, clamp the numbers positive, and cap accessibility to the exported tag list; create and edit share one form component, and a parity test asserts the two actions read an identical form-data key set. Unrecognised precision values coerce to `city` — the most private reading of bad input.

**Consequences.** Existing listings default to `city` precision, so their public place line coarsens from neighborhood+city to city until the owner opts back up — deliberate: the safer default wins over display continuity. Index cards stay untouched (the shared `ListingCard` reads the base listing shape only; chips there would mean widening the card contract, a separate decision). The coarse `approxCoordsForArea` geocode still runs on neighborhood+city regardless of precision — coordinates never left the coarse band, so precision governs display, not matching. Numbered as 867 because ADR-865/866 were claimed by parallel session work between the mandate and the landing.

The durable rule: **a privacy setting is one pure resolver every renderer calls, plus a write path that refuses to store what the setting says not to show — never a scatter of per-page if-statements around a value that should not be there.**

## ADR-868 — The member sidebar's commerce area collapses to a Marketplace umbrella, Channels turns on, and the directory reads Members (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted (founder mandate, seven changes, verbatim).

**Context.** The member sidebar's COMMUNITY section had grown to eight rows (Circles · Events · Business Spaces · Classifieds · Housing · Market · Community · My Contacts) with three problems the founder named directly: Channels (the focus areas ADR-864 just made load-bearing) was not in the menu at all; the commerce rows sprawled (Classifieds and Market are two doors into what a member experiences as one shopping area); and "Community" as a ROW label collided with the "Community" SECTION header two inches above it. The menu system is the DB-backed `menu_items` surface (`left`) whose sync only ever inserts (ADR-860), so any live-row change must land on both sides — the live rows AND the code defaults — or the two drift apart again.

**Decision.** Seven changes, one umbrella revival, both sides of the menu system:

1. **Channels turns on** between Circles and Events (`/channels`, icon key `channels` → Radio). The code default already carried it (BASE_NAV_AREAS); the live-row SQL activates an existing row or inserts one.
2. **Housing gets a house-search icon**: `MapPinHouse` (a house on a map pin — the closest lucide has to house+search, and it reads "find a place near you"; plain `House` reads as "home page"). The `housing` key finally gets an AREA_ICONS entry at all — it had been silently falling back to the globe.
3. **Classifieds + Market merge into ONE menu row, "Marketplace"** (icon `Store`). The row is the `market` vertical's nav contribution relabeled and re-pointed at `/marketplace`; the `maker` vertical no longer contributes a rail row (`nav: []`), and the `shop` area re-anchors `after: 'housing'` so a dangling anchor cannot append it after the Admin section.
4. **Marketplace lands on Classifieds by default.** `/marketplace` is a tiny SERVER redirect page (`app/(main)/marketplace/page.tsx`, force-dynamic, deliberately a temporary redirect) that whitelists the `commerce_last` cookie through `parseCommerceSurface` and defaults to `/classifieds`.
5. **The next visit remembers the last commerce surface.** One shared client component (`CommerceLastVisited`) writes `commerce_last` (`'classifieds' | 'market'`, path=/, SameSite=Lax, one year) on mount; it is mounted in exactly two new pass-through layouts — `app/(main)/classifieds/layout.tsx` and `app/(main)/market/layout.tsx` — so detail pages count as visits too. The shared vocabulary lives in `lib/marketplace/last-visited.ts` so writer and reader can never disagree on the whitelist. The index redirect coexists with the PERMANENT `/marketplace/housing` and `/marketplace/events` 308s in `next.config.ts` (path redirects run first; the index page stays live).
6. **The commerce area simplifies to Marketplace + Housing.** The live `/market` row is deleted; the code defaults no longer emit one (and `synced_default_keys` protection means the inserts-only sync can never resurrect it).
7. **Community → "Members"** with `BookUser` (an address-book person — clearly people, clearly a directory, distinct from Circles' `Users` pair). NAMING nuance recorded: "Members" names the directory of people at `/network`; lowercase generic "member" is untouched, and the member-footer link relabels with it since it is the same destination.

**The canon change rides its own line:** ADR-596 retired "Marketplace" as a member word; the founder deliberately revives it as the commerce UMBRELLA only — the menu row, the `/marketplace` landing redirect, and the already-pinned breadcrumb trail (which ADR-862/866 had left as a flagged retired-word use; this ADR makes it canon instead). The four surfaces keep their own names. NAMING.md carries the new umbrella entry and a "Marketplace" collision guard; the calm mobile spine's fifth tab follows its node and now reads "Marketplace" (a tab must never say one thing and land on another).

**Live rows.** `scripts/adr-868-member-menu-marketplace.sql` (idempotent, run once by an operator) applies all seven to the materialized `left` menu, renumbers the section to Circles · Channels · Events · Business Spaces · Marketplace · Housing · Members · My Contacts, and appends `/channels` + `/marketplace` to `synced_default_keys` ONLY when a baseline already exists (an empty baseline means "first sync trusts current state", and seeding it would flip that sync into injecting every absent default — ADR-860's mechanics, respected rather than fought).

**Consequences.** The member menu (menu_items / NAV_AREAS) is a different system from the locked admin module catalogs (ADR-553); nothing under `lib/admin/modules/*` moved. Known edges, recorded not smuggled: the operator visibility toggle for the `market` area now hides the whole Marketplace umbrella row (the Market surface keeps its own `makers` toggle for the page gate); the umbrella row highlights as active only on `/marketplace` itself, not on the surfaces it fans out to; and Frequency Store's default-rail row is untouched — it was already absent from the live menu, and retiring it is its own decision. Drift-guard tests updated in place: `lib/verticals/registry.test.ts` (the umbrella shape) and `lib/verticals/marketplace-resilience.test.ts` (maker contributes no rail row; shop anchors after housing). Numbered 868 because 867 was claimed by the housing Tier B session in parallel.

The durable rule: **a menu merge is one row, one stable door, and a memory of where the member last was — and any change to a DB-backed menu lands on the live rows and the code defaults in the same commit, or the inserts-only sync will tell you which one you forgot.**

## ADR-869 — The Program settings editor: display copy, blueprint refresh, and pause become self-serve (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** ADR-864 shipped Programs create-only on purpose, and ADR-865 hardened that posture: with the review fixes fresh, "changes go through the crew" was the honest v1 promise, and the settings surface said so out loud. But the posture aged fast in practice — the model was stable (one Program per Space at the database, owned blueprints fenced out of the Starter catalog, `startChapter` honoring the retire switch), while every rename, one-liner tweak, and pause request still meant a crew ticket against columns the owning Space already conceptually owned. The invariants were never the reason edits were closed; the missing editor was.

**Decision.** Phase 2 gives the owning Space three self-serve operations in `lib/channels/programs.ts`, all funneled through one ownership gate (`requireSpaceProgram`: the channel must be a Program AND `owner_space_id` must equal the calling Space, or the data layer throws) on top of the unchanged action-layer gate (ADR-274 re-verification of caller, Space, `canManage`, and `spaceFunctionAccessLive('program')`, exactly as the create action does):

1. **`updateSpaceProgram`** edits display copy (name, one liner, cover). It patches the Channel row AND keeps the blueprint's card copy in step (`circle_templates` name/one_liner/card/identity ride the same patch), so the Channel page and the Chapter-start flow never tell two different stories. The channel slug NEVER changes — a renamed Program keeps its `/channels/<slug>` address, so every shared link keeps working.
2. **`setProgramPaused`** flips `topical_channels.is_active` — deliberately the SAME retire switch `startChapter` already respects (ADR-865), not a new column. Paused: the Channel page is hidden (404) and no new Chapters can start; members and Chapters keep everything they have, and resume is one click.
3. **`refreshProgramBlueprint`** re-snapshots the blueprint from one of the Space's live circles, through the same shared helper (`snapshotCircleForBlueprint`) the create path now uses — so the ownership + non-draft checks and the snapshot shape can never drift between the two paths. Existing Chapters are untouched: a Chapter copied the old snapshot at remix time, so a blueprint change affects only future Chapters.

The settings surface grows the matching Edit / Blueprint / Pause sections, drops the "changes go through the crew" framing, and keeps ONE crew boundary as a quiet note: **deleting a Program stays crew-only.** Deletion is the operation that can strand Chapters, orphan a public blueprint, and free the one-per-Space slot in the same breath — the blast radius v1 was built to avoid, and nothing in phase 2 changes that math.

**Consequences.** Every ADR-865 invariant survives untouched: one Program per Space (no create/delete paths changed), owned blueprints still never surface as Starters (the refresh rewrites the existing owned row in place; `owner_space_id` never moves), the plan gate still rides `spaceFunctionAccessLive('program')` on every action, and pause reuses rather than duplicates the retire switch. `ProgramChannel` gains `isActive` so the surface can render the paused state. Data-layer tests go from seventeen to twenty-seven (foreign-Program and non-Program refusals, copy-sync patch shape, slug immutability, pause flip wired through the `startChapter` refusal, draft/foreign-circle refusals on refresh, and blueprint rewrite leaving display copy and Chapters alone). The duplicate-Program error's tail softens from "Changes go through the crew" to "Edit the one you have instead", matching the new reality.

The durable rule: **when a v1 says "changes go through the crew", write down which invariant each manual step was protecting — the ones protected by the database and the gates can go self-serve, and the ones protected only by human judgment (here: delete) are the durable crew boundary.**

## ADR-870 — The Channel Manage hub, and the staff Program lifecycle (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** Channels had staff capabilities but no console: the rail carried exactly two modules (`channel.settings` + the ADR-515 Insights readout) and everything else — who is tuned in, which Circles practice here, the Program — was invisible or read-only. Worse, the Program model had a structural gap: ADR-864 made a Program "a Channel with a blueprint", but the ONLY create path was `createSpaceProgram`, which requires an owning Space. A Frequency-run channel (`owner_space_id` NULL — e.g. the founder's Meld Community Cowork) had no blueprint-attach path at all, so the platform's own channels could never become Programs. The founder asked for two things directly: make Channel manage "the same style as the Events Manage section", and make Frequency-run channels promotable to Programs by staff.

**Decision.**

1. **The Channel Manage hub** — `app/(main)/channels/[id]/manage/{hub.ts,page.tsx,sections.tsx,load.ts,actions.ts}`, a file-for-file mirror of the event hub (Events manage overhaul): one master dashboard, a pill sub-menu, `?section=` in the URL, server-rendered, every section behind its own `<Suspense>` (PAGE-FRAMEWORK §5). Sections: **Home** (tuned in · Circles/Chapters · forum posts · 7-day room activity, plus quick links) · **Members** (everyone tuned in, via `topical_channel_memberships` joined to profiles) · **Circles** (status + fill; labeled **Chapters** while a Program) · **Program** (below) · **Settings** (the SAME `channel.settings` catalog module the rail mounts — never a parallel form). `hub.ts` is a PURE route-local section list, explicitly NOT a module catalog: MENU-CONTRACT/ADR-553 stays intact. Gated `channel.manage` (staff, ADR-274) with 404 for everyone else; every action re-checks the same capability, and a paused Program's console stays reachable (the PUBLIC page 404s; staff must be able to resume).

2. **The staff Program lifecycle** (`lib/channels/programs.ts`). `attachProgramBlueprint({ channelId, profileId, source })` makes any blueprint-less channel a Program: `source: { kind: 'circle' }` snapshots ANY live, real circle (no Space fence — the staff twin of the shared snapshot helper, still refusing demos and drafts); `source: { kind: 'starter' }` CLONES a catalog Starter into a new row — the original is never referenced or mutated, so it keeps living in the catalog and detach can retire the copy without touching it. Display copy rides the CHANNEL's name + description, same as the Space path. `detachProgramBlueprint` clears `template_id` and soft-retires the blueprint (`is_active` false, never deleted — Chapters copied it at remix time); the channel goes back to a plain focus area. The ADR-869 editor operations gain staff twins (`updateProgramForStaff` / `setProgramPausedForStaff` / `refreshProgramBlueprintForStaff`) funneled through a new `requireStaffProgram` gate — "is a Program" instead of "is THIS Space's Program" — while `requireSpaceProgram` and the whole Space path are byte-for-byte untouched.

3. **`circle_templates.program_only`** — migration `20270113000000_program_blueprint_flag.sql` (file only; **applied by the main session before push**). The catalog list reads filter `owner_space_id IS NULL`, which fenced Space-owned blueprints (ADR-864/865) — but a Frequency-run Program's blueprint has NO owner, so it would leak straight into the Starter Circles rail and the staff catalog. `is_active` cannot double as the fence (Remix needs it true to start Chapters, and `getAllTemplates` ignores it), so the row gets an explicit discriminator: `program_only boolean not null default false`, backfilled true for every row a `topical_channels.template_id` already references, stamped true by every blueprint write (create + attach + clone), and filtered (`eq program_only false`) by exactly the two catalog LIST reads. The single-row reads stay open on purpose — Remix loads blueprints through them.

4. **One rail row, the sanctioned way** — `channel.manage` joins `ADMIN_MODULES` (a `link` row into `/channels/<id>/manage`, resolving through `hrefForEntitySurface`; the route accepts DB id or slug, so a raw-uuid scope still lands). No rail render was touched; `pnpm check:menu` and the drift guards stay green, with the registry/href tests updated in place.

**Consequences.** Channels now have the full owner-console shape every other core entity has, and "all the admin rail functions" ride it: settings (existing module, mounted in the hub too), insights (the Home strip carries the same counts and more), and the new deep link. Every ADR-865 invariant survives: one Program per Space (the staff path never writes `owner_space_id`, so it cannot mint a second Space Program), owned blueprints never surface as Starters, `startChapter` honors the retire switch the staff pause flips. Data-layer tests go from twenty-seven to forty (attach refusals, circle-snapshot stamp, starter clone leaving the original byte-for-byte intact with a FUNCTIONAL catalog leak guard, detach, and the staff twins working on a NULL-owner Program the Space path provably refuses). The founder's Meld Community Cowork becomes a Program by staff clicking Attach on its Manage hub — no SQL required — once the migration is applied.

The durable rule: **when a discriminator is "the column is set", check what happens to the rows where it can't be — a NULL-owner variant of an owned pattern needs its own explicit flag, not a lucky filter.**

---

## ADR-871 — The three assignment flows: a Circle declares its Channel, staff curate a Channel's Circles, and staff assign a Channel's owner Space (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder asked, directly: "How can I assign a circle to a channel? How do I associate a space with the circle / channel." The audit found the taxonomy (Pillar > Channel > Circle, NAMING.md) fully modeled but only half wired: Space↔Circle attach existed (ADR-857), Space→Channel existed only by CREATING a Program (ADR-864), and the three connective edits were missing entirely — (1) an existing circle had no way to declare or change its Channel (`circles.topical_channel_id` was written only by Program flows), (2) the Channel Manage hub (ADR-870) listed the channel's circles read-only, and (3) `topical_channels.owner_space_id` had no assign/clear surface at all: once a channel existed, who ran it was frozen at birth.

**Decision.** Three flows, one data layer, no new tables or columns.

1. **A Circle declares its Channel** — the circle-settings admin module (`components/admin/modules/circle-settings-module.tsx`) gains a Channel select: active `topical_channels` grouped by Pillar (`pillar_id` → `pillars`, in display order), a "No Channel" option, and the circle's current channel kept visible even when paused so the select tells the truth. It saves through its own action (`setCircleChannelAction`, colocated in `app/(main)/circles/admin-actions.ts`), NOT the autosave form, because the save can be REFUSED — a paused Program takes no new Circles ("This Channel is paused and not taking new Circles right now.") — and the refusal must land inline with the pick rolled back. Same gate as every sibling field: `circle.editSettings`, re-checked in the action (capabilities are law).
2. **Staff curate a Channel's Circles** — the Manage hub's Circles tab (ADR-870) gains add and remove: add picks from real (`is_demo` false), forming|active circles not already in the channel and sets `topical_channel_id`; remove clears it behind a quiet confirm (`RemoveCircleButton`, the section's one client island). Both actions re-gate `channel.manage` (staff, ADR-274) exactly like the hub's Program actions. Remove verifies the circle is actually IN this channel first, so a stale form can never detach a circle from somewhere else. The circle keeps its host, members, and events either way — the Channel stamp is where it practices, not what it owns.
3. **Staff assign a Channel's owner Space** — `setChannelOwnerSpace({ channelId, profileId, spaceId })` in `lib/channels/programs.ts`: assign an active business/nonprofit Space, or clear back to Frequency-run (NULL — the root Space IS Frequency and is never a valid owner). **One owned channel per Space, full stop**: the ADR-865 unique partial index is on `topical_channels(owner_space_id) where not null`, so ANY second owned channel violates it, Program or not — the pre-check turns the constraint into a sentence ("That Space already owns a Channel. A Space can own one Channel, so clear that one first."). When the channel runs a Program, the blueprint's `owner_space_id` is re-stamped to match, because the ADR-865 catalog fence reads it; `program_only` is never touched (a Program blueprint is never a Starter, whoever owns it). The control lives on the **Program tab** of the Manage hub, not Settings: `owner_space_id` is the Program model's "who runs it" column (ADR-864), the tab's loader already carried it, and Settings mounts the shared catalog module, which must not grow a hub-only staff control (MENU-CONTRACT). It renders in both blueprint states — a plain focus area can be owned too.

The shared refusal is deliberate: `setCircleChannel` refuses ANY inactive channel — the same `is_active` retire switch `startChapter` honors (ADR-865) — so a paused Program takes no new Circles by any road, member or staff. Staff who want to seed a paused Program resume it first (one click, ADR-869).

**Alternatives considered.** *Channel select inside the RailAutosaveForm*: rejected — the autosave path treats a throw as a generic save error and Next.js redacts server-action error messages in production, so the paused-Program refusal copy would never reach the host. *Allowing a Space to own a second, non-Program channel*: rejected — the unique index covers `owner_space_id` wherever it is not null, so the DB already says no; pretending otherwise in the pre-check would just trade a sentence for a constraint error. *Putting the owner control in the channel-settings module*: rejected per MENU-CONTRACT — the catalog module is the one channel editor mounted in the rail AND the hub, and a staff-console-only control does not belong in it.

**Consequences.** The founder's question now has three one-click answers: a Host reassigns their circle's Channel from the rail they already edit it in, staff shape a channel's roster from its Manage hub, and handing a channel (Program or not) to a Space — or taking it back — is an assignment, not a re-creation. Every ADR-865 invariant survives: one owned channel per Space is now enforced with copy instead of only a constraint, owned blueprints stay fenced from the Starter catalog because the fence's column moves WITH the owner, and the retire switch gains a third respecter (`setCircleChannel`, alongside `startChapter` and the public page). Data-layer tests go from forty to fifty-one (paused/missing refusals, set + clear, wrong-channel remove refusal, root-Space and second-owner refusals, the no-op re-assign, blueprint re-stamp with `program_only` untouched, and the clear-to-NULL restamp).

The durable rule: **an assignment column every flow writes at birth needs an edit surface for the rest of its life — and the edit reuses the birth flow's guards (the retire switch, the unique index, the catalog fence), never a parallel set.**

---

## ADR-872 — Manual billing agreements: the off-Stripe money memory, and the renewal reminder ladder (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted. Migration `20270114000000_space_billing_agreements.sql` and seed `scripts/adr-872-seed-grandfathered-agreements.sql` written this session as FILES ONLY — **applied/run by the main session**.

**Context.** Three Spaces (Audrey DeWitt, Temple of Aset, Royal Temple) paid $490 CASH for a year of the Collective plan, grandfathered at $49/month · $490/year against the $79 list price. The main session set `spaces.plan = 'collective'` + the billing entitlements, and that was everything the system could hold: "the space's plan is the payment state-of-record" (lib/billing/space-subscriptions.ts), `space_subscription_items` mirrors STRIPE items only, and every renewal path assumes a Stripe subscription that re-bills itself. A cash deal had no durable record — no locked rate, no paid-through date, no history — and nothing anywhere would ever remind the Space (or the crew) that a payment was coming due. The deal lived in the founder's head.

**Decision.** A first-class MANUAL agreement record beside the Stripe mirror, plus a daily reminder cron — and a hard line about what it is NOT.

1. **`space_billing_agreements`** (migration above): one row per off-Stripe deal — `plan` (the paid SpacePlan labels), `interval` (month/year), `amount_cents` (the LOCKED rate actually agreed, not list), `method` (cash/check/transfer/other), `label` (the operator-facing rate framing, e.g. "Grandfathered at $49/mo, normally $79"), `started_at`/`paid_through` (plain dates, UTC-day semantics), three reminder stamps, `status` (active/canceled/settled — history is kept, never deleted), `note`. One ACTIVE agreement per Space via a partial unique index; RLS mirrors the sibling `space_subscription_items` exactly (staff read all, owner/active-admin read own, writes service-role only).
2. **The plan column stays the access authority; the agreement is the money memory.** Deliberately NOTHING here writes `spaces.plan` or entitlements: staff set the plan exactly as they do today, and the agreement records what was paid, at what locked rate, through when. One authority per axis — access resolves through the plan/entitlement spine (ADR-552/811), money-owed resolves through the agreement — so a mis-dated agreement can never yank a paying Space's tools, and canceling an agreement is a bookkeeping act, not a downgrade.
3. **The reminder ladder** (`app/api/cron/billing-renewals`, daily at 04:10 UTC): 30 days out, 7 days out, and past due — ONE notice each, idempotent via the per-row stamps, batched off one bounded read (`agreementsDue(now)`). The windows are DISJOINT (30d→7d, 7d→due, due→∞): a touch missed while its window was open is skipped, not sent late, because the more urgent touch covers it. The pure window/date math lives in `lib/billing/manual-agreement-dates.ts` (no `Date.now()` — `now` is passed in), with calendar-clamped interval extension (Jan 31 + month = Feb 28/29). Notices ride the primitives owner notices already use: an in-app `notifications` row for the owner + active admins, and an email to the owner through the durable outbox (`enqueueEmail`, ADR-026). Stamps are written only AFTER a send lands, so a failed fan-out retries the next day.
4. **`recordManualPayment`** extends `paid_through` by exactly one interval and clears all three stamps — the next cycle re-arms itself. **The staff seed path** is the "Manual billing" section on `/admin/spaces/[id]` (`ManualAgreementPanel` + janitor-gated actions in `billing-agreement-actions.ts`): the crew records future cash deals and renewal payments with no SQL. The OWNER sees a read-only receipt card on their existing billing surface (plan, locked rate, paid through, method, "Managed by the crew. Questions? Reach out.") — and the Stripe-portal button hides while a manual agreement is active, because there is no portal behind a cash deal.

**Alternatives considered.** *Faking a row in `space_subscription_items`*: rejected — that table is the Stripe mirror (`stripe_subscription_item_id`, `locked_price_id` are price-catalog handles), and a forged item would feed `spaceIsPaying` and the webhook's set-to-target reconcile with fiction. *Driving access FROM the agreement (plan follows paid_through)*: rejected — it would make a missed cash payment auto-downgrade a Space the founder shook hands with; the humane failure mode is a notice to a human, which is the whole point of the ladder. *A generic invoices table*: rejected as scope creep — three deals need a memory and a reminder, not an AR subsystem; `status`+history rows leave room to grow.

**Consequences.** The three grandfathered deals become durable rows (seed script, idempotent via `on conflict (space_id) where status = 'active' do nothing`), their owners get a locked-rate receipt on the billing page they already have, and twelve months from now the software — not the founder's memory — says a payment is due. Thirty-one new tests lock the ladder edges (window boundaries, stamps suppressing repeats, the 7-day window never re-opening the 30-day rung), the extend+re-arm contract, one-active-per-space (pre-check AND the 23505 race), and the migration's source shape. Billing copy is canon-checked (plain voice, locked-rate framing, no em dashes).

The durable rule: **when money moves outside the system, the system still gets a record and a clock — but the record never becomes a second access authority; one axis, one owner.**

## ADR-873 — A founding grant nobody can see is not a grant: the Founding Business badge, active-only, price private (2026-07-27)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder granted three Spaces founding status, and the rows landed in `public.founding_members` (`kind='business'`, `status='active'`, `locked_rate_cents=4900`, a `meta.terms` note explaining the grandfathered rate). Nothing changed on screen. `getFoundingStatus` (lib/founding/status.ts) had **zero consumers outside its own module** — no Space surface, public or operator, read it — so the whole grant existed only in the database. Members already had the other half of the pattern: `profiles.is_founding_member` renders through `FoundingBadge` (lib/community-roles) beside the name on `/people/[handle]`. The Space side had the record and no mark. Meanwhile `locked_rate_cents` sat on the same row as everything a public surface would want, which is exactly how a private commercial term leaks onto a storefront.

**Decision.** One reader shape, one chip, two public mounts.

1. **Batched reads, in `lib/founding/status.ts`** (not a new module — `founding_members` is not in the generated types, so it is reached through the ONE loose service-role handle this file owns, ADR-246). `foundingBadgesForSpaces(spaceIds)` returns a `Map<string, FoundingSpaceBadge>` from a SINGLE `.in('space_id', ids)` query, and `foundingBadgeForSpace(spaceId)` delegates to it so there is exactly one rule about what counts. Empty (or all-blank) input issues no query at all; every read is fail-safe to empty, because a read error must never fabricate founder status.
2. **ACTIVE ONLY.** A row earns the mark only at `status='active'` **and** `kind='business'`. `'reserved'` has not graduated — the spot is held and nothing was charged (the ADR-599 no-charge invariant), so the Space is not a Founding Business yet. `'lapsed'` fell out of the cohort, so the mark is no longer true. A `member`-kind row is not a Space founder even if it carries a space id. The status gate runs in app code rather than as a second `.eq('status','active')` on the query, deliberately: the directory's own tenancy filter is asserted by the SEC-02 leak-contract tests, and an identical filter emitted by this read would satisfy those assertions on the directory's behalf.
3. **`FoundingBusinessBadge` lives beside `FoundingBadge`** in `lib/community-roles.tsx` — same `.rank-badge` primitive, same gold rank token, same `Gem` glyph, same sizing prop — so the member chip and the Space chip cannot drift apart into two systems. The member chip reads "Founder"; the Space chip reads the locked cohort term, "Founding Business". Tooltip: *"Founding Business. One of the first businesses to join Frequency."*
4. **THE PRICE STAYS PRIVATE.** The chip takes a **boolean and nothing else**. `lockedRateCents` is carried on `FoundingSpaceBadge` for operator-facing readouts only and never becomes a prop, a tooltip, or a card field — `NetworkedSpace` exposes `isFoundingBusiness: boolean`, full stop. The badge is a **status, not a price tag**. A source-shape test asserts the chip's props, the tooltip's contents, both mount sites, and the card model are all free of the rate, so a rewrite that pipes it through fails CI instead of shipping a storefront price.
5. **Mounts.** (a) The Space profile chrome (`app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/(profile)/layout.tsx`), in the identity lockup where the type pill used to sit before D-refine #8 retired it — name → founding mark → tagline. It rides the header's existing `Promise.all`, so it adds no waterfall, and it is ungated: a Founding Business shows its badge to **every** visitor. (b) The directory card (`components/spaces/space-card.tsx`), through `EntityCard`'s existing `badge` slot, resolved for the whole grid by one batched call inside `listNetworkedSpaces` alongside the member/follower/event counts. No new layout, no query per card.

**Alternatives considered.** *A sibling `lib/founding/badges.ts`*: rejected — it would have to duplicate the untyped service-role handle, putting two doors on `founding_members`. *Reusing the existing `CharterBadge`* (components/ui/verified-badge.tsx, which already accepts a Space): rejected for this surface — it is the calm inline trust mark for storefront cards, and the brief is that the Space founder chip reads as the twin of the member's gold chip. *A per-card `foundingBadgeForSpace` call*: rejected outright, that is the N+1 the batched reader exists to prevent. *Showing the locked rate on the public badge*: rejected — it is a private commercial term between the operator and Frequency, and the neighbouring businesses on the same directory page have not agreed to see it.

**Consequences.** The three granted Spaces now wear their mark on their own profile and everywhere they appear in the directory, with no query added per card and no waterfall added to the header. Seventeen tests lock the reader (active-only, reserved and lapsed excluded, member-kind excluded, Map keying, empty input costs no query, de-dupe, one query for a whole grid, fail-safe on error) and the price-privacy source shape. The operator-facing rate readout is deliberately NOT built here: the Space billing settings surface is owned by the manual-agreement work (ADR-872), which already renders a locked-rate receipt on the page these owners have.

The durable rule: **a status row with no consumer is a rumour — but the surface that finally reads it publishes the status, never the terms.**

## ADR-874 — Selling and gating are two decisions on two dates: `billingLive()` charges, `featureGatesLive()` gates (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder's instruction was one sentence: *"I want billing switched on, people can explore the different levels until September 1st when the Beta period runs out and they have to pay."* The code could not express it. ONE flag, `billing_live`, carried both meanings. `featureAllowed` (lib/pricing/gates.ts) short-circuited to grant-everything on `!opts.billingLive`, and every gating seam — `spaceFunctionAccessLive`, the collaborator-hosting wall, the AI-depth ladder, `gamificationFullAllowed`, the Vera daily cap, the membership-ticket gate, the vault cash-in check, the operator-seat wall, the space-creation cap, the upsell teases — resolved that boolean by calling `billingLive()`. So flipping the master switch on to SELL would, in the same instant, REVOKE paid features from every free Space and every free member. The switch that opens the shop also emptied everyone's shelves, which is the precise opposite of the instruction. The only documented workaround (docs/PRICING-OPERATIONS.md) was to hand-disable each feature-gate row in `/admin/pricing` and remember to hand-re-enable all of them on Sept 1 — a manual checklist standing between the whole member base and their features.

**Decision.** Split the one boolean into two, and give the second one a date.

1. **`billingLive()` keeps its exact meaning: MAY WE CHARGE.** Stripe env keys AND the `billing_live` master switch. Every charging seam still reads it and nothing about it changed: checkout creation, `spacePlanSellable` / `memberTierSellable` / `bundleSellable` / `loadoutTierSellable` / `operatorSeatsSellable`, the founding-business checkout, `setSpacePlan` / `setSpaceAddons` webhook reconciliation, dunning, and the pricing surfaces whose CTA copy depends on whether checkout is real. It **fails CLOSED** (false on error), because its failure mode is charging somebody.
2. **`featureGatesLive()` is the new, separate question: DO THE PAID GATES BITE.** It is `billingLive()` AND the beta grace window has ENDED. Every feature-gating seam reads this instead. It **fails OPEN** (false on error, and false means GRANT), because its failure mode is stripping a paying-tomorrow member of what they have today. The two switches fail in opposite directions on purpose, and each comment says why.
3. **The grace window is an operator setting, not a constant.** `beta_grace` in `pricing_settings`, shape `{ until: string | null }`, the same mechanism as `trial` / `annual_discount` / `founding`. **No migration seeds it**: `readPricingSettings` already merges DB rows over code defaults, so an absent key resolves to `BETA_GRACE_DEFAULT` in `lib/pricing/beta.ts`, exactly as `founding` and `household_bundle` do. A row exists only once an operator edits the date.
4. **The default is a real window (`2026-09-01`), not `null`.** `{ until: null }` means "no grace, gates follow billing exactly" — the pre-ADR semantics — and it is available as an explicit operator choice (clear the field). But it is not the DEFAULT, because the default is what an operator gets when they flip billing on without having read this ADR, and that path must land on the intended go-live rather than an instant lockout. The date matches `BETA_PRICING_ENDS_AT`'s day, so the two halves of "the beta runs out" land together.
5. **The boundary: the grace date is the first ENFORCED day.** `until: '2026-09-01'` means the last soft day is Aug 31 and the gates begin on **Sep 1 at 00:00 UTC**. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` is normalized to `T00:00:00.000Z` explicitly rather than left to `Date.parse`, so a value can never be read in the server's local zone. Same convention as `isBetaPricingActive`.
6. **A failed read is not an empty setting.** `readPricingSettings` now returns `{ values, ok }`. `loadPricingSettings` is unchanged for its callers (values only, defaults-merged). `featureGatesLive()` consults `ok`: if the read failed it grants, rather than falling through to the code default and enforcing the moment that default date passes on the strength of a DB hiccup. This is the distinction between "the operator stored nothing" and "we could not read what the operator stored", and only the gate switch needs it.
7. **The pure resolvers stay pure.** `featureAllowed(feature, account, { gatesLive })` and `withinAllowance(key, tier, usage, { gatesLive })` still take a boolean; all IO stays in the settings seam. The option was RENAMED rather than aliased, so a call site that still passes `billingLive` is a type error, not a silent regression.
8. **Teases follow the gates, not the sale.** `resolvePersonalTeaseGate` / `resolveTierTeaseGate` / `resolveSpaceTeaseGate` and `shouldShowTease` moved to `featureGatesLive`. A tease says *"this is locked, here is the upgrade that unlocks it"*, and during the grace window nothing is locked. Showing it anyway would fail the skeptic test (CONTENT-VOICE §10). The real selling surfaces — the pricing page, the plan ladder, `FeatureTierUpsell` / `FeatureMeterUpsell` CTA copy, the upgrade page — ride `billingLive()` and are open for business the whole window.
9. **The operator can see both.** `/admin/pricing` opens with a one-line readout: billing live or not, gates enforced or not, and the grace date, derived from the same pure helper the runtime uses so the readout cannot claim a state the code is not in. The date is editable under Beta controls, next to the display-only countdown, with copy that says plainly which one changes access.

**Alternatives considered.** *A second boolean flag (`gates_live`) instead of a date*: rejected — the founder named a date, and a flag makes the cutover a thing somebody has to remember to do at midnight. *Reusing `beta_ends_at`*: rejected — that setting is documented and built as display-only (it drives a countdown banner and grants no access), and quietly giving it teeth would make every existing edit to it an access change. *Hand-disabling the feature-gate rows for the summer*: rejected, that is the status quo this replaces; it is a dozen manual toggles whose re-enable is a checklist item, with no record of when they are supposed to come back. *Aliasing `billingLive` as a deprecated option name on `featureAllowed`*: rejected — the whole failure was that the two concepts looked interchangeable, so the compiler should refuse the old one.

**Consequences.** Billing can be switched on today: checkout sells every plan, and no member or Space loses anything until Sept 1, when the ladder starts biting with no further operator action. Forty-one tests lock it (the pure grace window and its narrowing, the day-before / day-of boundary, `featureGatesLive` off with billing off, off during grace with billing on, on after the date, the fail-safe grant on a read error, null-and-absent grace semantics, `featureAllowed` under the renamed option) — including a **source-shape guard** listing nine gating seams that must read `featureGatesLive` and never `billingLive`, six charging seams that must read `billingLive` and never `featureGatesLive`, and a repo-wide sweep of every `featureAllowed` / `withinAllowance` call site. Re-conflating them fails CI instead of shipping.

The durable rule: **the switch that opens the shop is not the switch that empties the shelves, and if one flag does both, neither is a decision anybody can make.**

## ADR-1052 — The pricing page is DERIVED: seven sellable tiers, one grid built from the entitlement key sets, and the beta rate lives in the pricing config (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder's brief was four sentences: *"I want all plans to be sellable. Be sure to fully detail all the plans on the pricing page. Show a detailed feature grid, showing the access each tier gets. Also include, seats and AI addon. Make that all integrated."* Plus two corrections: *"I forgot the Independent tier.
