Make sure all of our pricing tiers are represented"*, and *"There are a few old packages on the website for different styles of business. Let's remove those and let the feature comparison do it's magic."*

Three real problems sat behind that. **(1) Only four of the seven offerings were on `/pricing`.** The table rendered Free Space, Business, Collective, and Non Profit; Independent was omitted by an explicit test, and the two personal tiers were a link to `/upgrade`. **(2) The comparison was hand-written prose.** Each tier column carried a `coreIncluded` sentence typed by a human, so nothing connected the page to `BUSINESS_DEPTH_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS` / `COLLECTIVE_DEPTH_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS` / `INDEPENDENT_DEPTH_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS`, to `FEATURE_GATES`, or to the usage ladders. Moving a capability between tiers changed what a Space could do and left the page saying the old thing, silently and forever. **(3) There were two disagreeing price layers.** `pricing_settings.plan.business` held `$29` with no anchor while the catalog (`business_base`) charged the `$19` beta rate, so the config the operator edits and the amount the checkout takes were different numbers. That is the same class of defect ADR-811's reconcile migration was written to fix, one layer up.

**Decision.**

1. **All seven offerings are on the page, each fully detailed.** The two member tiers (Member free, Crew) and the five Space tiers (Free, Business, Collective, Non Profit, Independent), each with its monthly price, its yearly price, its trial where one applies, its take-rate, and one plain sentence on who it is for. `pricingTiers()` gains the Independent column too, so the answer-engine surfaces (`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `pricingLadderSummary`) advertise the same ladder the page does.
2. **Every comparison cell is DERIVED, never typed.** The new `lib/pricing/pricing-grid.ts` is the pure model. A row declares its SOURCE, not its values: an `entitlement` row reads `planEntitlementKeys(plan)` (the three depth key sets); a `gate` row reads `meetsGate(FEATURE_GATES[feature])`; a `meter` row reads the tier's rung on the feature's usage ladder (`lib/pricing/feature-meters.ts`); the take-rate row reads `take_rate.network_bps`, the same vector `lib/billing/fees.ts` charges on. Move `whitelabel` into the Business depth set and the Business column says Included, with no edit to the page or the grid.
3. **The AI add-on and seats are rows, not footnotes.** The AI row is derived from `ADDON_ENTITLEMENT_KEYS`: those keys are in no tier base, so every paid tier resolves to the metered price and Free resolves to "not sold". Fold them into a tier base and that tier's cell flips to Included on its own. Seats derive from which tiers carry the `team` depth key, and while `operator_seat` is still `placeholder: true` the cell says "owner-priced" rather than publishing a per-seat number nobody approved.
4. **The beta rate lives in the pricing config, in the anchor idiom `tier.crew` already uses.** `monthly_cents` is what is CHARGED and `list_cents` is the crossed-out anchor above it (ADR-463). So `plan.business` becomes `$19` under a `$29` list and `plan.collective` becomes `$49` under a `$79` list, matching the catalog amounts exactly. `plan.collective` and `plan.independent` also become seeded, editable rows. Migration `20270115000000_pricing_beta_anchors.sql` reconciles the stored rows, idempotently and only where they still hold the known pre-anchor pair, so an operator-set rate is never clobbered. A test asserts the settings layer and the catalog layer agree, so the two can never drift again.
5. **No tier claims a discount the config does not carry.** Whether a struck anchor renders is decided by `priceRow` (an anchor reads only when `list_cents` is strictly above `monthly_cents`), so Business and Collective show their beta rate under a list and Non Profit and Independent show one price. The beta line states the grandfather promise ("yours for as long as you keep the plan"), not a countdown.
6. **The page reads config at request time, not build time.** `/pricing` resolves `getPricingValues()` + `loadCatalogConfig()` (both request-cached, behind `revalidate = 3600`), so a price edited at `/admin/pricing` changes the page, the metadata, the FAQ answers, and the JSON-LD Offers with no deploy. A source-shape test asserts the page file contains no dollar literal and no bare percentage at all.
7. **The per-business-style package cards are gone.** The "By who you are" loadout strip (five persona cards with monthly totals) is removed from `/pricing`; the comparison carries that weight now. `PERSONA_LOADOUTS` itself stays, because the `/for/<slug>` funnel pages are built on it.
8. **The grid is readable on a phone.** Desktop gets the real table, scrolling inside its own container. Mobile gets one native `<details>` per plan listing every group and row for that plan: no squashed multi-column table, and no client JS beyond the existing billing toggle.

**Alternatives considered.** *One eight-column table spanning both ladders*: rejected — a personal-tier row has nothing true to say in a Space column, and every cell would have needed a "not applicable" hedge. Two grids, one per ladder, say more with less. *Keeping the page on the CODE catalog defaults (`defaultCatalogConfig()`) for its zero-DB-read speed*: rejected — it meant an operator could change a price and the public page would keep quoting the old one until someone deployed, which is the drift this ADR is about; ISR makes the read once per revalidation, not per visitor. *Leaving `plan.business` at `$29` and letting the catalog own the beta rate alone*: rejected — the legacy `business_monthly` Stripe product is minted from `plan.business`, and `createSpacePlanCheckout` still resolves it, so the disagreement was a live mispricing waiting for the flag to flip. *Hand-writing the grid once and adding a test that it matches the key sets*: rejected — a test that compares two hand-written lists is a list you now maintain twice.

**Consequences.** The page cannot lie about what a plan grants: the only way to change a cell is to change the rule the product runs on. Thirty-one tests lock it, including two that **mock the depth key sets and assert the rendered grid moves with them** (white-label folded into Business flips that cell; the AI keys folded into Collective flip the add-on row to Included), a coverage test that every key in the three depth sets has a row, and the source-shape guard that the page hard-codes no money. What is deliberately NOT settled here: `canCreateSpace` (ADR-810) still requires Crew to create a first Space, while the page now states the founder's clarification that a free Space is open to anyone. That is a one-line product decision, flagged rather than made.

The durable rule: **a pricing page that repeats the entitlement rules will eventually contradict them; one that reads them cannot.**

---

## ADR-875 — The beta founder push: a grace notice replaces the lock tease, and paying early buys the badge (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder's instruction was one paragraph: *"I want the billing and pricing and notices to be very clear for the user. except for the three cash paying customers. Everybody else on the site is free. when they go to start anything above their tier, they should get a little pop up that says, you're using business tools or you're using collective tools. Memberships start September first. What I really want to do is inspire people to pay before the first to help us build the dream and get a founder's badge on their profile."*

ADR-874 had just built the first half of this and, correctly, silenced the second. It split `billingLive()` (may we charge) from `featureGatesLive()` (do the gates bite), so billing could go on today with nothing revoked until the `beta_grace` date. Part of that change put the in-context upsell teases to sleep: a tease says *"this is locked, here is the upgrade that unlocks it"*, and during grace nothing is locked, so it would fail the skeptic test. But the detection behind the tease was still doing real work. At the exact moment a member reached for a capability above their plan, the code knew two true things: which tier that capability belongs to, and that the beta is why they have it. Sleeping the tease threw that away and left the member with no idea they were on borrowed tools or that a date was coming. Meanwhile the founding grant had the opposite gap: `founding_members` + `profiles.is_founding_member` already render both badges (ADR-873), and `reserveFounding` / `grantFoundingStatus` already write them, but **nothing fired on a purchase**. Somebody could subscribe on August 15 and get no badge at all.

**Decision.** Keep the detection, change the sentence. Then hang the founding grant off the money.

1. **The same signal, a different sentence.** `resolvePersonalTeaseGate` / `resolveTierTeaseGate` / `resolveSpaceTeaseGate` now return `{ live, locked, notice }`. While the gates bite, `live` is true and the tease speaks exactly as before. While the gates are soft, `live` is false, `locked` is false, and `notice` carries a warm, non-blocking line. **They are mutually exclusive by construction**, and a test asserts that at every call shape. Nothing new was mounted to make this appear: the notice renders from *inside* `<UpsellTease>`, so it inherits every success-moment placement that component already had.

2. **Tier detection is DERIVED, never hand-mapped** (`lib/pricing/beta-notice.ts`, pure + client-safe). A feature's tier is read off its **real merged gate** (`mergeGate`, so an operator override moves the sentence with it); a bare tier floor is itself the tier; and a Space entitlement key resolves to the **lowest plan whose depth set grants it**, scanned from `planEntitlementKeys` — the same map the billing resolver writes. There is no feature → tier table to drift out of step with the gates that actually start biting on the date. A disabled gate and a free floor name nothing, because nobody is "using a paid tier" through either.

3. **The copy states the truth and nothing more.** *"You are using Collective tools" / "Memberships start September 1. Everything stays open until then." / "Subscribe before September 1 to hold the beta rate and add the Founding Business badge to your Space."* (A member reads "the Founder badge to your profile".) No wall, no muting, no modal, no urgency, no em dash. **A source-shape test asserts the copy contains no "locked" / "unlock" / "unavailable"**, because the one thing this notice must never do is claim an enforcement that is not happening. **The date is formatted from `beta_grace`, never written**, and the same test asserts no month name appears in any of the four source files, so moving the operator's one setting moves every sentence.

4. **It never nags.** The quiet meter is keyed **per TIER, not per feature** (`tier:crew`, `plan:collective`), so dismissing it at the Vault silences it at Vera too and a member meets at most a couple of these in total. It self-quiets after three appearances and stays quiet for fourteen days after a dismiss. The arithmetic is pure and unit-tested; the island owns only the localStorage read/write, exactly like the tease's frequency cap.

5. **One reader for the beta story** (`lib/pricing/beta-state.ts`): is the grace window open, when does it end, is checkout real, is this subject already founding, does this Space pay us off-Stripe. It composes existing readers only and owns no new state. **The three cash-paying Spaces are excluded by their records, not by their ids**: an active `space_billing_agreements` row (ADR-872) or a founding row suppresses the invite, so a fourth cash deal signed tomorrow is excluded the moment it is recorded, with no code change. A `reserved` founder counts as in (they answered the call already); only `lapsed` hears it again.

6. **The notice rides `billingLive()`, and that is on purpose.** It is a **selling** seam, not a gating seam: it decides what we say and can grant or revoke nothing. Per ADR-874 the honest selling surfaces ride the charging switch, so `beta-state.ts` joins the `CHARGING_SEAMS` list in the ADR-874 source-shape guard, which now also proves the founder invite never quietly becomes a second gate.

7. **Founding status is granted at RECONCILIATION, never at the success page** (`lib/billing/beta-founding.ts`), mirroring the placement discipline `lib/billing/founders.ts` already set for the Founders Round. The client success page is a redirect a browser may never follow: a member who closes the tab, pays on a phone that sleeps, or completes a subscription Stripe activates asynchronously would silently lose their badge. The webhook is the truth. Two call sites, one function: the member branch of `customer.subscription.created/updated` when the subscription goes active (`kind:'member'`, which also sets `profiles.is_founding_member`, the flag the profile chip reads), and `reconcileSpacePlanSubscription` once a paid plan settles (`kind:'business'`, the ADR-873 Founding Business chip).

8. **The cutoff reads the SUBSCRIPTION's creation instant, not the event's.** A renewal in October fires another `subscription.updated`; reading the event time there would answer "after the cutoff" for a founder who bought in August, and would re-run the boundary test on every renewal for the rest of their life. `sub.created` is fixed the moment they bought, so the first delivery and the thousandth decide identically. Combined with `grantFoundingStatus`'s existing no-op on an active row, the grant is idempotent by construction.

9. **The boundary, and a fail-safe that deliberately points the other way.** Strictly before the window ends, same UTC convention as `betaGraceActive`: `until: '2026-09-01'` means the last founding day is Aug 31 and a purchase at `2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z` is already past it. But where `betaGraceActive` fails toward **granting** (never lock a member out of a feature), `earnsBetaFounding` fails toward **not granting**: no window, an unreadable date, or an unreadable instant all withhold. A withheld badge is a one-line operator grant; a wrongly-issued lifetime rate is not.

10. **The locked rate gets a home.** `grantFoundingStatus` takes an optional `lockedRateCents`, and the reconcilers pass the amount actually charged, so the grandfather promise lives on the founder's own row instead of only in the price catalog. **An existing row's rate is never overwritten** — an agreed rate is settled the day it is set.

11. **A badge must never bounce a payment.** `grantBetaFounding` cannot throw: every failure returns a reason and is logged. The Stripe webhook releases its event claim and returns 500 on any thrown handler error, and a founding chip is not worth making Stripe redeliver a settled subscription.

**Alternatives considered.** *Leaving the teases asleep and adding a banner somewhere*: rejected — a global banner cannot say *which* tier's tools you are using, which is the entire content of the founder's instruction, and it would show to people it does not apply to. *A new `<BetaNotice>` mounted at fresh call sites*: rejected — the tease already knows the right moments (a contact just saved, a practice just logged, a code just shared, the CRM open); inventing parallel mounts would double the placement decisions and let the two drift. *A feature → tier lookup table for the copy*: rejected outright — that table would be a second source of truth about the ladder, and the day an operator raised a gate the notice would start naming the wrong tier. *Granting founding status on the checkout success page*: rejected, see §7. *Reading `event.created` for the cutoff*: rejected, see §8. *Hardcoding the three cash Spaces' ids*: rejected — they are identifiable from their own records, and a hardcoded list is a bug scheduled for the fourth deal. *A real modal ("pop up")*: rejected against the founder's own stated goal — the instruction is that everything is free until the date; a modal that interrupts the work contradicts the message it carries.

**Consequences.** A free member at a Crew moment, and a free Space in its CRM or running a Program, now learn plainly which tier they are on, that memberships start on the operator's date, and that subscribing early holds the beta rate and earns a badge, without one capability being taken from anyone. Anybody who buys before the date becomes a founder automatically, with their rate recorded, granted once no matter how many times Stripe delivers the event. Ninety-three tests lock it: the derived tier detection (Business feature → "Business tools", Collective feature → "Collective tools", an operator override moving the name, disabled and free gates naming nothing), all five suppressions, the exact copy of every variant, the no-lock-language and no-hardcoded-date source shapes, the quiet meter, the grant boundary day-before / day-of to the millisecond, both kinds, replay idempotency, the locked-rate write, and the never-throws contract.

The durable rule: **when a gate stops biting, the detection behind it does not stop being true — keep the signal and change the sentence, because the honest version of "this is locked" is "this is what you are using, and here is when it starts costing something."**

## ADR-876 — The first Space is open to everyone (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** ADR-810 capped Space creation at "free member → 0 Spaces; Crew → 1; owns a paid Space → unlimited", so standing up a first Space was a Crew feature. The rule has been INERT because it gates on `billingLive()`, which only became meaningful with ADR-874's split. Rebuilding /pricing surfaced the contradiction: the page sells a **Space Free** tier, and the founder confirmed the intent directly ("Free Space for anyone"). Shipping the page over the old rule would have promised a free Space that the platform blocks the moment the gates bite.

**Decision.** The personal-tier check leaves `canCreateSpace`. Any member, on any tier, may create their FIRST Space. Everything else about ADR-810 stands: one Space per member, and owning a paid Business or Non Profit Space lifts the cap entirely, so the second Space remains the Business upgrade. `spaceCreationBlockReason` loses its Crew branch, because the only remaining block is the second Space, and it names Business.

**Consequences.** The funnel's first rung changes from "join Crew to have a Space" to "have a Space, pay when you outgrow one" — which is the funnel /pricing now describes and the one the beta founder push (ADR-875) leans on. Crew keeps its own value on the member ladder (programs, rewards, Vera depth); it simply no longer stands between a member and their first Space. The cap's IO caller is unchanged, so this stays inert until the gates go live on the ADR-874 date.

The durable rule: **a price page is a promise, so the moment copy and gate disagree, one of them is a bug. Fix the one that contradicts what you decided to sell.**

## ADR-878 — Supporter leaves the sellable member ladder, and Crew shows one price (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder stated the member ladder in five words: Member (free) and Crew ($9/mo). "Drop the $12 tier." Supporter had already been retired once. ADR-458 turned it from a tier into a pay-what-you-want badge (`profiles.is_supporter`) and left `lib/core/entitlement.ts` mapping `supporter -> crew` at read time so nobody could lose access. Then the 2026-07 pricing overhaul (migration `20261217000000`) put it back on sale at $12: a `tier.supporter` price row, `tier_supporter_enabled` flipped true in prod, a Supporter column on the pricing template, a second CTA on `/upgrade`, `supporter_*` keys minted in the Stripe catalog, and Supporter advertised as a personal tier in `llms.txt`. Crew carried a crossed-out `$12` anchor over its $9 that existed only to echo that Supporter rate. The state we found: **zero** profiles on `membership_tier = 'supporter'`, **zero** carrying `is_supporter`. Nobody was buying it, and the ladder had three rungs where the founder had named two.

**Decision.** Remove Supporter from the SELL and DISPLAY paths, keep every READ tolerance, and give Crew one plain price.

1. **`tier.supporter` is DELETED from the config, not neutered.** `PricingDefaults['tier']` is now `{ crew: TierPrice }`. This is the load-bearing choice: a value kept "inert" is still a $12 number reachable at `values.tier.supporter`, and the next surface to iterate the tier map would render it in good faith. Typing it out of the shape made the compiler find every consumer instead of leaving a trap. A stored `tier.supporter` row in prod is read into the raw settings map and consumed by nothing, and the SQL below deletes it anyway.

2. **`memberTierSellable('supporter')` refuses in code, regardless of the flag.** The parameter still ACCEPTS `'supporter'` on purpose: making it a type error would mean a stale caller fails the build rather than failing safe, and a caller we missed would be worse than a caller that returns false. Belt and braces: the code refuses, `FLAG_DEFAULTS.tier_supporter_enabled` is already false, and the SQL turns the prod flag off. `tier_supporter_enabled` stays in `PRICING_FLAG_KEYS` so the operator console keeps reading its stored value honestly; nothing consults it to sell.

3. **Every Supporter purchase path is deleted, not disabled.** `MEMBER_TIER_KEYS` is `['crew']`, so the Stripe sync mints no `supporter_*` price. `startMembershipCheckout` takes no tier argument at all, and `createMembershipCheckout`'s `PaidTier` is literally `'crew'`, so a Supporter purchase is unrepresentable rather than merely unreachable. `CheckoutButton` lost its `tier` prop and its second visual variant. `priceFor` and `membershipAmount` no longer read `STRIPE_PRICE_SUPPORTER` / `STRIPE_SUPPORTER_AMOUNT`: setting those env vars now buys nothing.

4. **The READ tolerances all stay, and are tested explicitly.** `deriveTier('supporter') === 'crew'` (ADR-458), `isPaid('supporter')`, `deriveGamificationAccess('supporter') === 'full'`, and a `supporter` row clearing the paid tier gates. `tierForPrice` now always answers `'crew'`, which is the same access-preserving direction. `confirmCheckout` still honors a session stamped `tier: 'supporter'` as crew + the badge, because a session minted before this change must not strand a payment. The `supporter_monthly` / `supporter_annual` price keys (and their `_founder` variants) moved into `RETIRED_CATALOG_KEYS`, so the sync archives rather than deletes them and a grandfathered `locked_price_id` still resolves at renewal.

5. **The Supporter BADGE is untouched.** The pay-what-you-want contribution channel (`lib/billing/supporter.ts`, the `supporter_contributions` ledger, the Foundation donation, the badge toggle on `/upgrade`) is how a member backs the Foundation on top of Crew. That was ADR-458's whole point and it is not a tier. Retiring a price is not retiring a way to give.

6. **Crew shows ONE price.** `tier.crew.list_cents` leaves the code default, so `/pricing`, `/upgrade`, the page-editor template, `llms.txt`, the help center, and `CREW_NOTE` all render a plain "$9/mo". The anchor idiom itself is untouched: `priceRow` still derives a strike from `list_cents > monthly_cents`, the Space plans still use it, and an operator who deliberately sets a Crew anchor at `/admin/pricing` still gets one. What changed is that the code stopped shipping an anchor whose only justification was a tier that no longer exists.

**Alternatives considered.** *Keep `tier.supporter` in the config as an inert value*: rejected, see §1 — the point of the change is that no surface can render $12, and a live value in the shape is exactly how one would. *Drop `'supporter'` from `EntitlementTier`*: rejected — that union is the READ axis, and narrowing it would break the `supporter -> crew` tolerance that guarantees a historical row never loses access. Selling and reading are different questions and this ADR only answers the first. *Make `memberTierSellable`'s parameter `'crew'` only*: rejected, see §2. *Delete the `supporter_*` price keys outright*: rejected — a retired key is kept resolvable in this repo by long-standing convention (ADR-460/472/552) so a grandfathered subscription still renews. *Leave Crew's $12 anchor and just remove the tier*: rejected — an anchor is a claim that the real price is higher, and once the $12 tier is gone that claim has nothing behind it. It would fail the CONTENT-VOICE skeptic test.

**Consequences.** The member ladder reads the way the founder stated it, on every surface a person or an answer engine can reach: two rungs, one price each, no strike-through, no third option. Nobody is affected, because nobody was on it. Twenty-eight tests lock it, including `memberTierSellable('supporter')` returning false in the most permissive world the flags can describe (billing live, every switch on, a stored `tier.supporter` row present), the pricing grid resolving exactly two member columns, no `$12` reachable from any member display path, and the four access-preservation assertions for a historical `supporter` row. The operator SQL (`scripts/adr-878-retire-supporter-tier.sql`, run by hand, guarded and idempotent) turns the prod flag off, deletes the `tier.supporter` row, and strips Crew's anchor only if it still holds the exact `1200` this ADR retired.

The durable rule: **a price you have stopped selling has to leave the config, not just the page, because a number left in the shape is a number the next surface will honestly render.**

---

## ADR-879 — The Channel operator surface is complete, the category vocabulary has one source, and archive replaces delete (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The founder opened the Channel settings rail on their Meld channel and said: *"There should be a LOT more settings for Channels. I want all of them for my Janitor account."* They were right in a specific, checkable way. `public.topical_channels` carries eleven columns; the rail exposed four (name, category, description, is_active) and the Channel Manage hub (ADR-870/871) owned three more indirectly (owner Space, template, and the circles that point at the channel). That left **four columns editable by nobody, from anywhere**: `cover_image`, `pillar_id`, `slug`, and `display_order`. Meld rendering a gradient placeholder was not a design choice, it was a column with no writer. The Pillar chip on the channel page read a field no surface could set. The URL and the directory sort order were frozen at insert time.

The category was worse than missing, it was **wrong in a quiet way**. It was a free-text input, but two hand-written maps (`CATEGORY_ICON` in the channel page and again in `components/widgets/channels/channels-list.tsx`) decided what a category *looked* like from a closed set of seven keys. An operator typing "Creative " with a trailing space, or "wellness", got a generic Radio icon and no warning that anything had happened. Free text in front of a fixed map is a silent-breakage machine.

**Decision.** Finish the Channel's own fields in the rail module, keep everything the hub already owns in the hub, and close the category vocabulary around one file.

1. **The module owns the Channel; the hub owns its relationships.** `components/admin/modules/channel-settings-module.tsx` now edits cover image, name, description, category, Pillar, display order, the URL, and visibility. It does NOT edit Members, Circles, the Program, or the owner Space, because `/channels/[id]/manage` (ADR-870/871) already does, correctly, with its own gated actions. Those three get **link rows** into `?section=members|circles|program`, so the panel still reads as a complete map of what a Janitor can do without a second Program editor existing. Building a duplicate owner-Space or blueprint control here was rejected outright: two writers on one relationship is how a stale form detaches the wrong thing.

2. **The cover image reuses the one image path, it does not grow a new uploader.** `InlineCover` + the universal Loom picker, bound to `setChannelCoverUrl` / `removeChannelCover`, exactly as the Circle settings module does. The setter validates with `isLoomPublicImageUrl` before it writes, so a caller cannot smuggle an arbitrary address into a rendered `src`. The owner directive stands: every image upload opens the Loom.

3. **ONE category vocabulary** (`lib/channels/categories.ts`, pure + data-only). It carries the seven keys with their label, lucide icon, and token accent. The channel page, the directory card, and the settings select all read it; the two hand-written maps are gone and a **source-shape test asserts none of the three re-declares one or spells a category key at all**. The select can now only offer what the icon map can render, which is the whole point. **An off-list stored value is preserved, never rewritten**: every reader is total (an unknown value keeps its own text as its label and gets the generic Radio icon), and the select surfaces the stored value as a marked option, so saving an unrelated field can never silently relabel a live Channel. The old free-text default was `'general'`, which is off-list by design and stays that way until an operator chooses.

4. **The action patches only what it was given.** `updateChannelSettings` builds its update from `fd.has(...)`, field by field. The rail autosaves a snapshot of whatever form is on screen, and this action has more than one possible caller, so a form that omits a field must never blank it. An empty submission writes nothing and revalidates nothing. **This is why the Active checkbox became a Visibility select**: an unchecked checkbox submits nothing at all, which under a patch-only-what-was-submitted rule reads as "not submitted" and would have made archiving a one-way door. The same reasoning the Circle module already used for Unlisted.

5. **The slug is a rename, not a field save.** `updateChannelSlug` keeps its own action because a rename MOVES the page: it slugifies, refuses an empty result, checks uniqueness, and **refuses a collision with a plain sentence** ("Another Channel already uses that URL. Try a different one.") rather than throwing, so the refusal lands next to the field. Both the old and the new path are revalidated, plus the id path, because a channel resolves by id *or* slug and the abandoned URL must stop serving a cached page. The field carries the consequence in plain words: changing it changes the URL, and links already shared to the old one stop working.

6. **Archive is the only destructive verb. There is no hard delete, and that is deliberate.** `is_active = false` already hides the page (the route `notFound()`s on it) and drops it from the directory, and ADR-865 uses the same switch as the Program retire control, so the behaviour is proven. A hard delete is refused because **`circles.topical_channel_id` points here and carries no cascade guarantee we want to exercise**: a Channel with Circles practicing in it must not be able to vanish out from under them, and neither must a Program's Chapters lose the channel that defines them. The consequence line says what actually happens, in the founder's own terms: "Archived: the Channel page is hidden and it leaves the directory. Circles keep everything they have." Restoring is one select away. If a Channel ever genuinely needs erasing, that is an operator SQL script with the circle relocation decided first, not a button in a rail.

7. **The gate did not change, because it was already right.** Topical channels are platform-curated, so `isChannelManager()` (staff, admin+) is re-checked as the first statement of every exported action, ADR-274 style, with the admin client's RLS bypass making that check the only authority. The new actions join the same pattern rather than inventing a per-channel host that does not exist.

**Alternatives considered.** *Putting the category keys in the icon map and importing that*: rejected — the map lives in a Server Component that pulls the whole channel page's dependency graph, and the select is a client rail module. A pure data file both can import is the only version that stays cheap. *Typing the icon map as `Record<ChannelCategory, LucideIcon>` and leaving the maps in place*: closer, and it would catch a missing key at build time, but it leaves the labels and accents duplicated in two files and does nothing about the second copy in the directory widget. One array with everything on it is smaller. *Normalizing off-list categories to a default on save*: rejected — that is a silent rewrite of live data triggered by an operator editing an unrelated field. Mark it and leave it. *A checkbox for Active, as before*: rejected, see §4. *A Delete button with a typed confirm, like `DangerDelete` on Circles*: rejected, see §6 — a Circle's delete unlinks its own dependents, but a Channel's dependents are other people's Circles. *Rebuilding Members/Circles/Program inline so the rail is self-contained*: rejected — the hub owns them, and a second editor is a second set of authz to keep in step.

**Consequences.** A Janitor can now set everything a Channel is from the rail: Meld can have a cover, sit under a Pillar, hold a checked category, be moved in the directory, be renamed at its URL, and be archived and restored, with Members, Circles, and the Program one click away in the console that owns them. Thirty-five tests lock it: the staff gate refusing a member and an anonymous caller across all five actions with nothing written or revalidated, the patch-only-what-was-submitted rule (including that an unrelated submission writes nothing at all), pillar/display order/category/visibility writes, the Loom-URL guard on the cover, slugify + collision-as-a-sentence + the old-path revalidation, the seven-key vocabulary with its total readers, and the source shape proving the page, the directory card, and the select all read the one file and spell no key themselves. What is deliberately NOT built here: no hard delete, no per-channel host role, no second Program or owner-Space editor, and no migration (every column already existed and was simply unreachable).

The durable rule: **a column with no writer is a feature nobody can use, and free text in front of a fixed map is a bug the operator gets blamed for. Close the vocabulary, patch only what was submitted, and make the destructive verb reversible.**

## ADR-880 — An entitlement is earned by money MOVING, and a page must resolve a price the way the checkout charges it (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** An adversarial review of the live billing paths (`billing_live` is already true in production, with Stripe keys configured) traced six defects that all reduce to two habits. Two of them were charging or granting in production today.

The first habit: **treating the existence of a row as evidence of a fact.** `reconcileSpacePlanSubscription` granted Founding status whenever the reconcile settled on a non-free plan, and the member webhook granted it for `active || trialing`. Both Space checkouts set `trial_period_days: 14`, so day one of a free trial minted a founder. `paymentStatusForSubscription('trialing')` returns `'active'`, and `past_due` / `incomplete` also resolved to a paid plan, so a card that never cleared minted one too. Both checkouts set `allow_promotion_codes: true`, so a 100%-off code produced an `active` $0 subscription that minted one as well. On the member side that grant also sets `profiles.is_founding_member`, which `resolveMemberPriceId` honours as a permanent founder price. And **nothing in the repository ever wrote `status='lapsed'`** — zero write sites — so every wrongly-issued grant was permanent, publicly visible (ADR-873 mounts the badge on Space surfaces), and carried a lifetime rate. ADR-875's promise that the rate holds "as long as the subscription is maintained" was true in the copy and absent from the code.

The second habit: **letting a surface resolve a fact differently from the code that enforces it.** `/pricing` decided whether a plan was discounted with one rule, "`list_cents` is above `monthly_cents`", which has no clock and is permanently true after migration `20270115000000` wrote `{monthly:1900, list:2900}` and `{monthly:4900, list:7900}`. The checkout has a clock: `resolveLoadoutPriceId` switches to the LIST price key once `!isBetaPricingActive()`. From `2026-09-01T07:00:00Z` the page, its JSON-LD `Offer`s, its OG description and its "you keep it" FAQ would advertise $19/$49 while Stripe charged $29/$79. Worse, the same plan had **two live prices at once**: the legacy `createSpacePlanCheckout` (still exported from the Space billing actions) billed the `business_monthly` product minted from `pricing_settings.plan.business.monthly_cents = 1900`, which never reverts, so after the cutover one button charged $19 and the other $29. The comparison grid had the same shape of bug on a different axis: it read `FEATURE_GATES[feature]` while `featureAllowed` resolves `mergeGate(feature, await loadFeatureGateOverrides())`, so an operator raising `space_crm` to Collective left the page promising "Included" on Business.

Two smaller defects share one root: **supabase-js resolves with `{ data, error }` on a DB failure, it does not throw.** In the billing-renewals cron the in-app notification insert sat in a `try/catch` with `delivered = true` on the next line, so the catch was dead and a failed insert still stamped the touch; because the three reminder windows are disjoint and only `recordManualPayment` clears a stamp, that rung was suppressed for the whole cycle and the notice silently never happened. `stampAgreementTouch` had the mirror-image bug: it discarded its own write error and returned `void`, so a stamp that never landed counted as sent and the same reminder re-sent every day. Finally, `locked_rate_cents` was read from `items.data[0].price.unit_amount` — but a Phase B loadout is base + Vera AI + operator seats in no guaranteed order, so index 0 could be the $20 add-on, and an annual plan wrote `19000` into a column documented per-MONTH.

**Decision.** Fix the two habits, not the six symptoms.

1. **A founding grant is gated on a paid YEAR, in a pure module.** `lib/billing/founding-payment.ts` `foundingPaymentSignal(sub)` answers one question with no clock, no Stripe call and no database: `status === 'active'` (not `trialing`, not `past_due`, not `incomplete`, not terminal) AND a **base plan item** with a non-zero amount AND nothing that zeroed the bill (a 100%-off or fully-covering `amount_off` coupon, or an expanded `latest_invoice.amount_paid <= 0`) AND, per the owner's rule, **the base item bills annually**. The badge comes with the year: a monthly subscriber holds the beta rate and earns no badge. The cutoff stays exactly where it was, `sub.created` against the grace window in `beta-founding.ts`, because that logic is correct and replay-safe: a renewal in October re-decides identically. The signal fails toward NOT granting, the opposite direction from the feature gates and deliberately so — withholding a badge is a one-line operator grant, a wrongly-issued lifetime rate is not recoverable.

2. **The base item is found by its catalog key, never by `[0]`, and the locked rate is normalized to a month.** `baseSubscriptionItem` ranks the item whose `frequency_pricing_key` is a base plan (highest tier first, retired keys still resolvable for grandfathered rows), falling back to the single item of a one-item subscription (a member Crew sub, a legacy single-price Space sub). A yearly amount converts through the new `monthlyFromYearly`, the exact inverse of `yearlyFromMonthly` (two months free), so a $190/yr founder records $19/mo — **the rate they are locked at**, which is what they keep if they ever switch to monthly. Dividing by 12 would record $15.83, a rate we never promised and never charge.

3. **Founding status can lapse.** `lapseFoundingStatus({profileId|spaceId})` flips an `active` row to `'lapsed'` and, for a member founder, clears `profiles.is_founding_member`. It is narrow on purpose: a `reserved` spot is a held place and is left alone, a re-lapse is a no-op, and **a Founders Round buyer keeps the flag they bought outright** (`meta.founder.founder_round`), because a one-time $250 purchase is not a subscription's to take away. The Space path lapses only when `spaces.stripe_subscription_id` is the subscription being canceled, so a hand-recorded cash founder — who has no Stripe subscription at all — can never be lapsed by an unrelated event. `past_due` does not lapse: dunning grace (ADR-370) keeps a paying founder a founder while Stripe retries.

4. **The pricing page resolves prices through the same seam as the checkout.** `effectiveTierPrice(price, betaActive)` is the display twin of `effectiveCatalogAmounts`: during the window nothing moves, and after the cutover the list becomes the price, the anchor is dropped (we do not strike a number we now charge), and the annual re-derives through `yearlyFromMonthly`. `spacePlanRows` now REQUIRES `betaActive`, and `PricingGridInput` carries it; the page passes `isBetaPricingActive()`, the same call the checkout makes. The beta FAQ entry and the "beta rate" note exist only while a beta anchor does.

5. **One plan, one price.** `createSpacePlanCheckout` is now a thin adapter over `createSpaceLoadoutCheckout`: same catalog item, same beta auto-revert, same grandfathered locked price, same webhook metadata. The legacy `<plan>_<period>` Stripe prices stay synced and resolvable so a grandfathered subscription still renews on its own price id; nothing new is ever sold at them.

6. **The grid reads the merged gate.** `PricingGridInput.gateOverrides` carries `loadFeatureGateOverrides()`, resolved at the page (server) so the grid module stays pure and client-safe, and `gateCell` calls `mergeGate` — matching `featureAllowed` at enforcement time and `beta-notice.ts targetForGate`.

7. **Read the error supabase-js returns.** The cron checks `{ error }` on the notification insert before setting `delivered`, and `stampAgreementTouch` returns a boolean the cron only counts a touch on. A sent-but-unstamped touch is logged loudly, because it means a re-send tomorrow.

**Alternatives considered.** *Granting from `invoice.paid` instead of the subscription reconcile*: the honest money signal, and the reason `invoiceAmountPaidCents` is consulted when the event carries an expanded invoice, but moving the grant there means a second path from invoice to Space/profile and two places that can mint a founder. The reconcile is already the point the plan itself is written from; adding the money test to it keeps one grant site. *Keeping `status !== 'free'` and simply excluding `trialing`*: rejected — it leaves `past_due`, `incomplete`, and the $0 coupon. *Normalizing a yearly rate by 12*: rejected, see §2. *Reading the catalog directly in the grid instead of `pricing_settings`*: tempting, but it silently retires the operator's price console; instead a table-driven test asserts the two sources agree for every tier and interval on both sides of the cutover, so drift fails CI rather than reaching a customer. *Making `betaActive` and `gateOverrides` required fields on `PricingGridInput`*: `betaActive` defaults to the live clock inside the grid (the `pricingTiers(betaActive = isBetaPricingActive())` idiom this repo already uses) so a caller who forgets still cannot quote a stale price; making it required would only have broken sibling test fixtures without making the page more honest. *Deleting the legacy `<plan>_<period>` sync*: rejected — a grandfathered subscription resolves through those keys.

**Consequences.** Eighty-seven tests lock it: the money/interval signal branch by branch (trialing, past_due, unpaid, incomplete, canceled, paused, $0 price, 100%-off and amount_off coupons, a zero-collecting invoice, a monthly paid plan, base-item resolution behind an add-on and a seat line, and the monthly normalization of a yearly rate); the reconcile granting only on a paid year and lapsing only on a cancel of the subscription the Space is actually on, with a hand-recorded cash founder explicitly untouched; the lapse's narrowness including the Founders Round exemption; a table-driven page-equals-checkout assertion over every sellable tier × {monthly, yearly} × {beta, post-beta}; the legacy and loadout checkouts charging the identical price key on both sides of the cutover; operator gate overrides moving a grid cell in both directions with an invalid override never widening a gate; and a failed insert not stamping, plus a failed stamp not counting as sent. The beta invite copy now names the yearly plan, because the copy has to say what the code grants on. No migration and no schema change: `founding_members.status` already had `'lapsed'` in its vocabulary and simply had no writer.

The durable rule: **an entitlement is earned by money MOVING, never by a row existing; a price a page shows must be resolved by the same code the checkout charges; and supabase-js hands you the error instead of throwing it, so read it.**

## ADR-881 — Every sellable base must map to a paid plan (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** ADR-811 added the Collective and Independent tiers, and both were made sellable: `collective_base` / `independent_base` are catalog items, the loadout checkout mints them, and `ITEM_KEYS` even documents the intended mapping (`collective_base -> 'collective'`). But `planForItemKeys` (`lib/billing/space-subscription-items.ts`), the pure resolver that turns a Stripe subscription's live items into the Space's base tier, was never given a case for either. It fell through to its `return 'free'`.

**The consequence was silent and expensive.** A Space that paid for Collective reconciled to `plan: 'free'`, and `setSpaceAddons` then SET-TO-TARGET the billing namespace from the free depth set: it wrote free-tier entitlements over a Space paying $49 a month, revoking the CRM, email, reporting, automation, team seats, and Programs the customer had just bought. Independent ($249) did the same. The failure needed no error path and logged nothing, because from the reconciler's point of view the subscription simply implied no paid base. It was found by an adversarial review of the billing lanes, not by a test or a report.

**Decision.** The ladder gains both tiers in capability order: independent > nonprofit > collective > business > free. A test asserts the ordering pairwise, and a guard test iterates every sellable base item and asserts none of them resolves to `free`, so a base added to the catalog in future fails here before it can reach a customer.

**Consequences.** Any Space that subscribed to Collective or Independent before this fix has free entitlements written into its billing namespace; re-running the reconcile (or a plan write) restores them, and the entitlement namespace is set-to-target so no manual repair is needed. Nothing about the charge was wrong: Stripe billed correctly throughout. Only the access the payment was supposed to buy went missing.

The durable rule: **a resolver whose fallback is "no access" must enumerate every case that means access, and prove it with a test that walks the catalog rather than a list someone remembered to update.**

## ADR-882 — A Channel gets a real editor, not just a drawer (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** Every other core entity has three operator surfaces and Channels had two. An Event has the inline settings module (quick, autosaving, in the admin drawer), the `/manage` console (who is coming, what they said, how to reach them), and `/events/<slug>/edit` — the full page where the whole record is set up in one deliberate commit, with the destructive controls at the bottom. Channels had the first two. ADR-879 widened the drawer from four fields to nine, which closed the coverage gap but not the shape gap: the drawer is a panel that autosaves on blur, so it can never own the URL. Renaming a Channel MOVES its page and breaks every link already shared to the old address; that is not an on-blur write, and the drawer worked around it with a separate mini-form and its own Update button sitting inside a surface where nothing else has one.

**Decision.** Add `/channels/<slug>/edit`, the Channel's editor, on the event editor's shape: FocusTemplate, every field on one page, ONE Save, and the danger zone last.

1. **A full-form save, the opposite contract to the drawer's patch.** `updateChannelSettings` writes only the keys the FormData actually carried, because a drawer that renders a subset must never blank what it did not show. The editor always renders every field, so `saveChannelEdits` writes the WHOLE record: a cleared description means "no description" and is written as `null`, not skipped. Both actions live in the same file and share the staff gate, so the two contracts sit next to each other where the difference is visible.
2. **The URL is part of that same save.** One Save button, so a rename cannot need a second click. The action slugifies the input, falls back to the NAME when the field was emptied (a save can never strand the page on an empty address), refuses a collision in a sentence rather than letting the unique index throw, revalidates both the old and the new path, and returns the resulting slug so the form can move the page to it.
3. **Delete, with Archive still the softer option — and it goes through an RPC, not a table delete.** The first version of this shipped a bare `.delete()` on `topical_channels` and was wrong. Only two things hold a foreign key to that table: memberships (CASCADE) and `circles.topical_channel_id` (SET NULL, so every Circle that practiced here survives and simply stops belonging to a Channel — the copy says exactly that before the click). But a Channel owns two MORE things through **polymorphic scope columns that carry no FK and therefore cannot cascade**: its open room (`rooms WHERE visibility = 'channel' AND scope_id = <id>`) and its forum (`posts WHERE scope_id = <id>`). Deleting the row alone strands both — a live room still serving at `/messages/r/<id>`, still postable by anyone holding the link, still listed in the Messages of everyone who joined it, pointing at a Channel that no longer exists. Three sequential PostgREST deletes do not fix it either, because each gets its own transaction and a failure part-way leaves exactly that orphan. So `delete_topical_channel(uuid)` (migration `20270116000000`) does all three in ONE transaction. Deleting the room cascades its members and messages; deleting a post cascades its replies, mentions, and reactions.
   **The authz trap inside it, because it is worth naming.** The obvious guard, `if private.get_my_web_role() not in ('admin','janitor') then raise`, is silently wrong here. That helper resolves `auth.uid()` and COALESCEs a miss to `'none'`, and the caller that matters is the server action's admin client, which holds the **service role and has no `auth.uid()` at all**. The blanket check would have refused the one path the function exists to serve, on every call, while reading as perfectly strict in review. The guard is therefore conditional on there being an authenticated user: an authenticated caller must be staff, the service role is admitted because the action already re-checked staff (ADR-274, the same seam every other admin-client write in the file uses), and the grant itself is the outer lock: only `service_role` holds EXECUTE, so `/rest/v1/rpc/delete_topical_channel` is unreachable from the public REST surface at all rather than merely guarded on it. The role check stays as defense in depth in case a later migration re-grants.
4. **The rail row comes from the catalog.** `channel.edit` is a new `ADMIN_MODULES` row plus one case in `hrefForEntitySurface` — a data edit, not a render edit (MENU-CONTRACT / ADR-553). A `link` row for the same reason `journey.builder` is one: a full-page editor is never inlined into a sidebar.
5. **Nothing is rebuilt.** Members, Circles, and the Program (with its owner Space) stay in the Manage hub (ADR-870/871) and get link rows out. The editor covers every column `topical_channels` owns except the two the Program owns, so the page is complete without being a second console.

**Alternatives considered.** *Widening the drawer further*: it was already widened, and the drawer's shape is the problem, not its coverage. *Making the editor the only surface and retiring the drawer*: rejected — in-place editing is the point of the embedded-admin pattern, and a one-field tweak should not cost a navigation. *Autosaving the editor too*: rejected — the URL is on it. *Pointing the Channel page's hero "Edit" at the new route*: rejected, because the event hero's Edit opens the drawer and the two headers follow one grammar; the editor is reached from the Manage hub's header button and its Settings tab, which is where the event editor is reached from too.

**Consequences.** Both delete defects were found by verifying the shipped work against the live schema rather than by a test, which is the honest account: the FK inventory said "two children, both handled", and the polymorphic ones are invisible to that query. The fix was proved end to end against the live database on a synthetic Channel that the function itself then removed (channel gone, room gone, zero orphan rooms remaining). Fourteen tests lock the save's semantics against the drawer's: every field written on a full save, a cleared description landing as `null`, "No Pillar" and Archived clearing their columns, a non-numeric order falling back to `0` instead of writing `NaN`, the slugify-and-rename happening inside the same commit with both paths revalidated, the empty-URL fallback, and both refusals (blank name, taken URL) coming back as sentences with nothing written. Delete is covered on both branches, including that a failed delete does not revalidate as though it worked. The Manage hub's header button now reads "Edit Channel" and goes to the editor rather than to its own Settings tab.

The durable rule: **an entity is only as editable as its most deliberate surface — if a field can break a shared link, it belongs behind a Save button, not an on-blur write.**

## ADR-883 — A Circle placement writes the bare scope pair, and a cross-Circle strip shows only public (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** Exactly one Event in production has ever been tied to a Circle, and it was made through the create form. The *placement* flow accounts for none of them, and the reason is a schema seam that fails silently in the safest-looking direction.

`events` carries both a bare polymorphic scope (`scope_id` + `scope_type`) and the H1-1 typed arc (`scope_circle_id`, `scope_region_id`). Placement wrote the typed column. **Every reader consults the bare pair**: `getEventCapabilities` keys on `scope_type = 'circle' AND scope_id`, so does the `can_read_event` RLS policy, so do the calendar-follow views and the Dispatch audience. A trigger, `sync_event_scope_arc`, is supposed to bridge the two, and its own comment states the problem: `-- Contract-phase reverse path (no-op while scope_id is NOT NULL)`. `scope_id` is `NOT NULL` on `events` (verified against production), so that branch can never fire. Placement wrote a column nothing reads while the UI reported "Lives here", and the Circle page, the members' RLS read, the host's edit rights and the Space calendar all stayed exactly as they were. Nothing errored, because locally nothing was wrong.

Three defects shared the seam. **"Remove from Circle" was the inverse lie** (it nulled the typed column and left `scope_type = 'circle'`, so the event stayed). **Create authority was narrower than approve authority**: `circle.editSettings` could approve an event into a Circle but not create one there, so a `?circle=` deep link from those very surfaces degraded silently into a personal public event. And the **edit page looked up `circles` by `scope_id` regardless of `scope_type`**, mislabeling every public and Space event as "This event".

A fourth defect was found only because the first was fixed. The Channel page's `UpcomingEventsWidget` reads across every Circle practicing a Channel, **through the admin client, so RLS is not there to catch it**, and it carried no `status` and no `visibility` filter. It never leaked, because circle placement was broken and the strip was permanently empty. **Repairing placement is what would have armed it**: 18 published `circle_only` events exist today, and the first one placed into a Circle would have surfaced on a public Channel page to a viewer who is a member of none of them.

**Decision.**

1. **One write shape, in a pure function.** `livePlacementPatch` / `clearPlacementPatch` (`lib/events/placement.ts`) own the tie. A circle placement writes the **bare pair AND the typed column AND the circle's Space** (ADR-857). The invariant is stated once and tested, rather than restated at each call site, which is how the two halves drifted apart in the first place.
2. **Removal moves the event, it does not publish it.** `scope_id` is NOT NULL, so "remove from Circle" has to have somewhere to go: the event returns to its region as a standalone public event, and `circle_only` steps down to **`unlisted`, never `public`**. Publishing an event a host deliberately kept inside the Circle would trade one bug for a worse one. If there is no region to move to, the action fails honestly instead of half-moving.
3. **Create uses the same capability as approve.** `circle.editSettings`, plus an existence check, because staff resolve that capability against any id and `scope_id` has no foreign key to lean on.
4. **A cross-Circle strip shows public, published events only.** The viewer's membership is unknown there by construction. A single Circle's own block may widen to `circle_only`, because on that surface membership in *that* Circle is known.

**Alternatives considered.** *Fixing the trigger's reverse path instead of the writers*: rejected. Dropping `NOT NULL` from `scope_id` to let the typed column lead would make the bare pair optional across dozens of readers and RLS policies that assume it is present, which is a migration of the whole read side to fix one writer. *Backfilling `scope_circle_id` into the bare pair*: unnecessary, and checked rather than assumed — zero events carry `scope_circle_id` without a matching `scope_type`, because the path was never successfully used. *Leaving the widget to a follow-up ticket*: rejected, since this change is precisely what converts it from latent to live.

**Consequences.** 12 tests on the patch shapes, the visibility step-down, the no-region guard, and source-shape guards that the actions route through the seam; 18 on the Circle block's read rules (ordering across mixed timestamp spellings, dedupe, cap, foreign-circle and sentinel rejection, the visibility matrix); 4 on the widget's filters. The widget guard matches against **code with comments stripped** — its first run failed on its own explanatory prose, which names `circle_only` to describe the leak. The `standalone` scope value (one legacy importer row whose `scope_id` is a profile) is left alone but is now a known, undocumented fourth value in the vocabulary. **Not verified against a live database:** trigger convergence after writing the bare pair is reasoned from the migration SQL, so one manual placement on staging should confirm it before this is trusted.

The durable rule: **when a value is stored twice, exactly one copy may be authoritative and the writers must be forced through one function that writes both; and fixing a broken write path can arm a read path that was only ever safe because nothing flowed through it.**

## ADR-884 — An Event links to a Journey by association, and a recurrence copies its anchor (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context, part one: linking.** An Event could name a Circle (placement) and a Space (association). It could not name a Journey. The obvious move, a fourth `scope_type`, is the wrong one: `scope_type` is the event's single HOME, and every reader plus `can_read_event`, the calendar-follow views and the Dispatch audience branch on it. A new value would have to be taught to all of them before the first row could be written safely, and ADR-883 is the record of what happens when one half of that learns and the other does not.

A correction found on the way in: **there is no `journeys` table.** The entity a member authors and runs is `journey_plans`; migration `20260604170000` renamed `arc_chains`/`arc_steps`/`arc_progress` to `journey_*` but never created `journeys`. The FK points at `journey_plans(id)`.

**Context, part two: recurrence.** Auditing the same domain turned up a live defect with a bigger blast radius than the linking gap. `generateOccurrencesForAnchor` built each materialized occurrence from a hand-listed payload of ten columns. Every column NOT on that list fell to its database DEFAULT, and the defaults are not neutral: `visibility` defaults to `circle_only`, `price_cents` to NULL (which `page.tsx` renders as a free RSVP), `capacity` to NULL, and trigger `events_default_space_id` rewrites a NULL `space_id` to the ROOT Space. In production both live recurring series are $22.00 public events, and **all 16 upcoming occurrences were free, `circle_only`, and uncapped**; the Meld series' seven were additionally re-tenanted from Royal Temple, a paying Collective customer, to the root Space with `host_space_id` NULL, so ticket money would not have routed to the business.

Two findings compounded it. The RLS `circle_only` branch admits `scope_type = 'circle'` **or `'region'`**, and no writer has ever written `'region'` (a region-scoped event is `scope_type = 'public'`), so that disjunct is dead and a `circle_only` public-scoped event is readable by its host alone: the visibility drift was not a downgrade, it was disappearance. And `generateAllOccurrences` selected anchors with no `is_cancelled`, `removed_at` or `status` filter, so cancelling a series stopped nothing, the nightly cron simply minted a fresh non-cancelled occurrence as the horizon rolled forward.

**Decision.**

1. **Journey is an ASSOCIATION, like Space.** `events.journey_id uuid references journey_plans(id) on delete set null`, plus a partial index on `(journey_id, starts_at) where journey_id is not null`. No RLS change, and that is the point: `journey_id` appears in no policy, so a link can never make an Event readable or unreadable. Deleting a Journey never deletes someone's Event.
2. **One function attaches and detaches.** `journeyLinkPatch(id | null)` emits exactly `{ journey_id }` and is forbidden by test to carry `scope_id`, `scope_type`, `space_id` or `visibility`. Attach and detach are the same function rather than a pair, because a pair is exactly how ADR-883's "Remove from Circle" became the inverse lie of "place in Circle". Mirrored tests assert the other direction too: placing an Event never touches `journey_id`, and un-placing it never silently unlinks its Journey.
3. **The offer and the gate are one rule.** The picker lists Journeys the caller can EDIT (`canEditJourney`: author, operator, or owner/admin/editor of the owning Space) and both actions re-check that same function. Enrolment is not authority, so "Journeys I am on" is not offered. A `?journey=` deep link that misses the list is re-resolved through the real authority and, failing that, surfaces a visible notice rather than a silent drop. An absent field means "leave the link alone", never "detach", so the draft-publish, Vera spark and scanner paths cannot wipe a link they do not know about.
4. **A recurrence inherits from its anchor.** One `INHERITED_COLUMNS` constant drives BOTH the anchor SELECT and the child payload, so a column can no longer be read without being written; the drift mechanism itself is closed rather than the ten symptoms patched. `geog` copies only in its round-trippable EWKB-hex form. `anchorIsDormant()` now filters cancelled and removed anchors in both the per-anchor path and the cron query.

**Alternatives considered.** *A fourth `scope_type = 'journey'`*: rejected, see above. *A polymorphic `event_links` join table*: rejected, because storing one relationship in two shapes is the ADR-883 defect. *Enumerating the drifted columns in the occurrence payload*: rejected as the same bug one release later, since the next added column would drift again. *Guarding `journey_id` against a direct PostgREST PATCH*: deferred deliberately, because `space_id` and `host_space_id` are equally column-blind today and `space_id` is the more consequential of the three; one guard across all three is a separate decision, and guarding only the newest column would imply protection its neighbours lack.

5. **The same list repairs and propagates.** Two follow-ups the owner approved, both driven by that one constant rather than a second hand-written list. `scripts/adr-884-backfill-recurrence-drift.sql` is GENERATED from `INHERITED_COLUMNS` and repairs the already-materialized rows, which the code fix cannot reach (`generateOccurrencesForAnchor` uses `ignoreDuplicates: true` and will never overwrite an existing row). `propagateAnchorEditsToOccurrences` pushes a later anchor edit onto upcoming occurrences, which is what stops a repaired series from silently re-drifting the next time anyone edits it. Both are scoped to UPCOMING occurrences: a past occurrence is the record of an event that already happened, and rewriting its price or venue after the fact would be inventing history rather than correcting it. A drift test parses the SQL script and the TypeScript constant and fails if they disagree, so a column added to the generator can never be silently omitted from the repair.

**Consequences.** 31 tests on recurrence, 23 on the placement/link seam, 19 on belonging resolution. **The backfill has been applied to production**: all 16 upcoming occurrences now match their anchors on every inherited column, verified by the script's own after-check reading 0 on every drift count. Meld's seven are back to $22.00, public, capacity 22 and hosted by Royal Temple rather than root; Breathe's nine are back to $22.00 and public. The one PAST drifted occurrence was deliberately left as it was. The dead `'region'` RLS disjunct and the `updateEvent` visibility coercion gap are both identified and both still open. Two timezone latencies are logged as suspected: reminder copy labels with `HOME_TZ` rather than the event's `time_zone`, and `lib/journeys/runs.ts` parses a tz-less string in the server's local zone, correct only because production Node runs UTC.

The durable rule: **a row copied from another row must inherit through one list used by both the read and the write, because a default is a decision someone else made for a different purpose.**

## ADR-885 — The Channel detail page carries its own scope rail, and 'scoped' comes back for exactly one route (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The member-facing Channel page was one wide, sparse content column (hero, name, a two-fact row, a forum composer over an empty feed, then a "Circles practicing…" grid) sitting beside the GLOBAL member rail, which showed Your Quest, Your activity, Happening soon, New members, Frequency Signature and Your stats. None of that is about the Channel. So the page simultaneously under-used its own column and had nowhere to put the facts that belong to a Channel: how busy it is, what is coming up, and which Circles practice it. `docs/PAGE-FRAMEWORK.md` §6 had specified the right answer since the framework was written — `/channels/[id]` → Detail, "rail: program, circles-in-topic, events" — and it had simply never been built.

`Rail = 'scoped'` already models exactly this case, and `SCOPED_PREFIXES` was empty with a note to re-add a prefix "only if a section grows a genuine in-body rail".

**Decision.**

1. **The Channel detail page renders its own in-body scope rail, and the global rail is suppressed on that route.** Owner request, 2026-07-28: "Redesign the Channel pages. Give it a right column for activity, upcoming event, associated circles, etc." This **narrows the 2026-06-20 directive** ("the right rail shows on every page") for this one route, and only this one: everywhere else, including the `/channels` index and the Channel's own `/manage` and `/edit` surfaces, the global rail still shows. Two right columns of unrelated content is the exact failure `'scoped'` exists to prevent.
2. **The rule is an anchored PATTERN, not a prefix.** `SCOPED_PREFIXES` matches with `startsWith(s) && length > s.length`, which is a whole-subtree match. A `/channels/` prefix would therefore have swallowed `/channels/<id>/manage` and `/channels/<id>/edit`, neither of which has a rail of its own, silently stripping their right column. A sibling `SCOPED_PATTERNS` list (`/^\/channels\/[^/]+$/`) says what was meant. The page's tabs are query params (`?tab=feed`), not path segments, so one pattern covers all four tabs.
3. **The rail is a slot on `DetailTemplate`, not a hand-rolled column.** Template C always declared a scope-aware `rightRail`; it is now a real optional `sidebar` slot whose geometry matches `HeaderSidebarTemplate` (content first on mobile, `lg:w-80` beside it above that). Omitting it leaves every other Detail page byte-identical. A page that fills it MUST also be `'scoped'`, which is stated at both ends.
4. **Three modules, and empty is the state they are designed for.** Activity (the pulse, read through the SAME `loadChannelHomeStats` the Manage console uses, so member and operator views cannot disagree), Upcoming (the shared `UpcomingEventsWidget` across the Circles practicing the Channel), and the Circles/Chapters directory (the cards the page already loaded, so no second read). A new Channel has one member, one Circle, no posts and nothing on any calendar; each module states what will appear there rather than vanishing or spinning.

**Alternatives considered.** *Leaving the global rail and folding channel facts into the body* — rejected: it is what the page already did, and it is why the column read as sparse while the rail read as irrelevant. *Adding `/channels/` to `SCOPED_PREFIXES`* — rejected, see decision 2; it is the obvious edit and it is wrong. *Editing `UpcomingEventsWidget` to take an empty state* — rejected: it was hardened to public+published only in ADR-883 and is shared with other surfaces, so the rail composes it and reveals its own fallback with `:not(:only-child)` (the `owner-block-frame.tsx` idiom) when the widget renders nothing.

**Consequences.** The two modules that read the database each sit behind their own `<Suspense>` with a dimension-matched skeleton, so nothing new is awaited on the page's top-level path. `GroupCard` moved to `components/channels/group-card.tsx` because the rail and the body directory now render the same card. The rail drops its directory module on the directory tab, where the body already IS the full directory. The existing `page-chrome` guard asserted "has no scoped entity-detail pages"; it now asserts the opposite for this one route, with `/channels`, `/channels/<id>/manage` and `/channels/<id>/edit` pinned as `'global'` beside it so the prefix trap cannot be reintroduced. One cosmetic seam is knowingly left: the Upcoming module keeps the shared widget's own uppercase heading, which differs from `ModuleCard`/`SectionHeader` typography, because that file belongs to the events area.

The durable rule: **a route-shape rule must be as narrow as the surface it describes — a prefix match promises a subtree, and a detail page is not a subtree.**

## ADR-886 — The Channel admin gets the Event settings structure (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The owner asked to mirror the Event settings structure into the Channel admin. Laid side by side, the Event rail carries a stats row, images, the fields, a permalink with its own action, **header controls** (cover focal point + hero height), and a **danger box** pinned to the bottom. The Channel rail had the fields and the permalink and nothing else. Two of the gaps were real rather than cosmetic:

**A Channel cover is usually a wordmark, and a center crop cuts it.** `PageHero` has always accepted `coverFocus` and a size, and `lib/layout/cover-height.ts` is a SHARED Short/Standard/Tall ladder that events and Business Space covers both resolve through, so the render side was ready the whole time. The Channel simply had nowhere to store the two values. That is visible in production: the Meld Community Cowork cover is a two-line logo whose lower line is cropped away, with no operator control to move it.

**A Channel could only be deleted from the full editor.** Events have carried Cancel + Delete in the rail from the start.

**Decision.**

1. **`topical_channels.theme jsonb`, the same bag Events use, with the same two keys.** Not a column per setting, and not a second convention: a reader who knows `lib/events/cover-focus.ts` + `lib/events/hero-height.ts` already knows `lib/channels/hero.ts`. Defaults are dropped on write, so a Channel nobody has tuned keeps `{}` and renders exactly as it does today. Backward compatible by construction.
2. **One documented divergence: an explicitly chosen `standard` height is STORED, not dropped.** On an Event nothing competes for the height, so `standard` and unset mean the same thing and dropping it is free. A Channel hero also answers to the header ELEMENT config (`resolveHeaderElement`, ADR-793). If an operator picks Standard on a Channel whose element says Tall and the key were dropped, the decision would silently return to the element and the click would appear to do nothing. Hence `hasChannelHeroHeight`, which distinguishes a CHOICE from a default, and a page that reads `savedHeroHeight ?? header.height` so the element keeps deciding for every Channel no one has touched.
3. **The danger box is a CATALOG row, not a hand-mount.** Events mount `EventDangerZone` directly in `settings-panel.tsx` as an "inline extra". `hub.danger`, `nexus.danger` and `journey.danger` all render from `ADMIN_MODULES` through the module map instead, and that is the pattern this follows: a data edit, not a rail edit (MENU-CONTRACT / ADR-553). Archive is offered first and reads as the softer option, because it is.
4. **`order: 20`, not 10.** `modulesForScopeKind` sorts by `order` alone and is stable, so an order-10 danger row lands among the other 10s in the MIDDLE of the rail. The drift guard caught exactly that and the row was moved rather than the expectation rewritten.

**Alternatives considered.** *A column per setting*: rejected, two columns for presentation on a table that has no other presentation state, when the sibling entity already models it as a bag. *Copying the Event hand-mount for the danger box*: rejected, the catalog path is the contract and three other scopes already use it; mirroring the STRUCTURE does not mean mirroring an exception. *Dropping the default height for parity with Events*: rejected, see §2 — parity would have produced a control that silently does nothing.

**Consequences.** 15 tests on the theme helpers, focused on totality (`theme` is untyped jsonb and can hold anything: a string, a number, an array, a missing key, an unparseable height, all resolve to a sane default) and on the divergence, including an explicit assertion that a chosen `standard` survives a round trip. Two guards moved with the change rather than around it: the registry drift guard now expects Danger last, and the Channel page source guard asserts `size={savedHeroHeight ?? header.height}` with a note that the element still owns the fallback. A CodeQL log-injection finding on the recurrence propagation logger was fixed in the same pass by stripping CR/LF from the caller-supplied id and capping its length, rather than trusting an encoder to imply it.

The durable rule: **when you copy a sibling's structure, copy its contract and not its exceptions, and name every place the copy has to differ.**

## ADR-887 — One subject vocabulary for Channels and Spaces, and the register rule narrows to content (2026-07-28)

**Status.** Accepted.

**Context.** The owner asked for a redesigned Channel category structure whose names "cross over into the category a Space is in," expanded on both ends. Two findings reframed the work. First, **Spaces already had a live category vocabulary** (`lib/spaces/categories.ts`, six keys at `preferences.profileData.category`, filtering the directory), so the crossover was a merge of two conflicting vocabularies, not a greenfield add. Second, the two lists were answering **different questions with the same word**: Channel categories say what something is ABOUT (spirituality, movement); Space categories say what SHAPE of thing it is (practitioner, coach, studio, venue). The owner's own example, "Guides / Coaches," does not fit a subject list, and that is the diagnostic: it is a kind, not a subject. Conflating them forces a yoga studio to pick one of two true answers.

The taxonomy also collided with the voice canon. The original proposal cut "Spirituality" because CONTENT-VOICE §2a says the Seeker "does not identify as spiritual at the front door." The owner overruled the cut and **amended the canon** (2026-07-28, recorded in §2a): the register rule governs BODY COPY, not names. Doors may say the plain wellness word out loud — Spirituality, Meditation, Holistic Health, Functional Medicine; the card, the empty state, and the notification stay in the plain register. A name is a label, not a sermon.

**Decision.**

1. **Three axes, documented so this stops being re-litigated.** SUBJECT = what it is about — `lib/taxonomy/subjects.ts`, fifteen keys, shared by Channels and Spaces (and by Circles through their Channel). KIND = what shape of thing it is — Space-only (Guides / Coaches, Studios, Venues), today's Space vocabulary renamed. PILLAR = what it develops — game only, orthogonal; a Space can never hold one, which alone rules out nesting subject under Pillar.
2. **The fifteen subjects**: Spirituality · Meditation / Breathwork · Movement / Fitness · Outdoors / Adventure · Holistic Health · Functional Medicine · Mental Health / Recovery · Friendship / Relationships · Creative / Arts · Crafts & Hobbies · Food / Cooking · Gardening · Parenting / Kids · Service / Activism · Business Support. Every label is a thing a person does or a door they would name, combo labels use " / " so one door covers a focused group, and the four the owner named explicitly (Spirituality, Functional Medicine, Gardening, Crafts & Hobbies plus Meditation and Parenting / Kids) are all present.
3. **Keys were kept wherever possible, and the migration shrank accordingly.** Five of seven original Channel keys survive verbatim, so their rows never moved. Exactly two rows remapped (`scripts/adr-887-subject-remap.sql`, applied to production, guarded by slug + current value, idempotent, verified after: zero off-list rows): `human-relating` → `friendship`, and the Mental / Emotional Health Channel's `holistic-health` → `mental-health` — while the Holistic Health Channel keeps `holistic-health`, which remains in the vocabulary.
4. **`lib/channels/categories.ts` became a view.** Its entire public API is unchanged — type, array, total readers, the null-prototype icon map — so no import moved; it derives from the shared list instead of declaring its own. The ADR-879 rules ride along untouched: off-list values are never rewritten, readers are total, the settings select marks an off-list value rather than replacing it.
