## ADR-922 — Web vitals are a page property, so their stream is anonymous by design (2026-08-03)

**Status.** Accepted. Implements the audit's "zero performance measurement" finding as field RUM with no new vendor.

**Context.** Neither existing sink could carry Core Web Vitals for the visitors who matter most for them: `/api/track` drops anonymous requests and feeds the semantic ledger (and through it the gamification engine), and `/api/observe` is member-tied AND consent-gated by the `analytics` scope. Marketing, discover, and help traffic — the SEO surface whose INP/LCP actually move rankings — was invisible. Meanwhile Sentry's tracing already collects vitals incidentally at a 0.1 sample as error context, and `interaction_events` was built with a nullable `profile_id` "to keep an anonymous-session path open later".

**Decision.** A third, deliberately anonymous stream: `components/analytics/web-vitals.tsx` in the ROOT layout (client leaf, no cookies, root stays static) → `lib/analytics/vitals.ts` (pure normalizer + per-page-load head-sampled buffer, one beacon per load) → `POST /api/vitals` → `interaction_events` with `profile_id` NULL, `surface` NULL, `kind='web_vital'`, templated `path`. Never member-tied — that is the property that keeps it outside the `analytics` consent scope, and adding a profile id is the one change that would require revisiting this ADR. No rate limiter on the route: `lib/rate-limit` fails closed in prod when KV is unconfigured, which would silently drop all vitals; the batch cap and normalizer bound each request instead.

**Alternatives considered.** *Relax `/api/observe` for anon* (rejected — breaks the ADR-166 member-tied/consent-gated invariant and pollutes the rollups the traits store reads). *Register `perf.web_vital` in the semantic taxonomy* (rejected — per-page-load noise in `engagement_events` feeds the activation funnel and rewards engine). *Vercel Speed Insights / other vendor* (rejected — first-party is the declared source of truth; the stale `vitals.vercel-insights.com` CSP allowlist entry should go rather than grow a third collector).

**Consequences.** p75 LCP/INP/CLS per templated route, split anon/member-agnostic, 90-day bounded, queryable today. ⚠️ Sampling is 1.0 during beta; drop `SAMPLE_RATE` to 0.25 once daily loads pass ~10k. ⚠️ If `surface` is ever set on these rows, `interaction_surface_stats` needs a `kind <> 'web_vital'` filter first. ⚠️ Attribution fields (element, interaction target) are not available from `next/web-vitals` in this Next version; adding them means adopting the `web-vitals` package directly — a separate decision.

The durable rule: **data that never touches an account needs no account consent — and the way to keep that true is to make the account link structurally impossible, not merely omitted.**

## ADR-923 — Tenancy walls: the deny-all space_*/CRM surface gets DB-enforced per-Space policy quads, and admin-client usage becomes a ratchet (2026-08-03)

**Status.** Accepted. The tenancy-walls phase of the 2026-08-03 master production plan (the ADR-921 runway), applied to production the same day.

**Context.** After the CRM convergence pass (20260905000000) policied `crm_deals`/`crm_activities`/`crm_stages`/`contacts`/`client_notes`, twenty-six Space-scoped tables still ran fail-closed: RLS enabled, zero policies, service-role only (the reasoned posture in `scripts/rls-deny-all.txt`). Safe, but structurally blind — isolation lived entirely in app-layer guards on the RLS-bypassing admin client, the database proved nothing about tenant separation, and both deferred platform phases (App Platform, white-label sites) are gated on DB-enforced walls being verified in prod. `app_instances` additionally carried its Phase-2 policy set only as a commented block.

**Decision.** Migration `20270206000000` extends the canonical policy quad in two shapes: RESOURCE tables (17: CRM work items, relationships, campaigns, segments, email templates, drips, automations, invites, availability, service types, donation asks, membership/ticket tiers, programs) get the full quad live on `contacts` — SELECT for Space write-authority or platform staff, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for Space write-authority, with UPDATE guarding both old and new row so a row cannot cross Spaces. LEDGER and MEMBER-STATE tables (9: outreach/email-event ledgers, event shares, memberships, enrollments, bookings, RSVPs, follows) get read arms only — self (owning profile id), Space operator, staff — writes stay server-mediated until each surface's session-client convergence. Migration `20270206000100` applies the `app_instances` Phase-2 policies with two deliberate divergences from the Phase-1 commented block: permissive rather than restrictive (an as-restrictive set over zero permissive policies grants nothing), and `can_write_space_content` rather than `can_view_space_content` as the first read arm — the commented version would have exposed draft and archived instances on every public Space to everyone, anon included, because `can_view_space_content` answers Space-level visibility, not instance-level authority. Cross-tenant proof: `supabase/tests/space_tenancy_walls.test.sql` (pgTAP) asserts the walls from four seats (operator, plain member, anon, far-side operator) over two seeded Spaces; the stale `public.can_write_space_content` reference in the existing definition guard is repointed to `private.*` (ADR-847). The admin-client ratchet lands as `check:admin-client` (CI-wired): the 736 current importers of `lib/supabase/admin` are frozen in `scripts/admin-client-baseline.txt`; a new importer fails CI unless added to the baseline in the same PR, and the list is regenerable only downward as surfaces converge onto the session client.

**Alternatives considered.** *Public read arms on storefront tables (tiers, programs, availability)* (rejected this pass — walls restrict, they do not expose; public rendering stays on the server path until each surface converges, so the batch stays strictly non-expanding). *Client write arms on member-state tables (follows, RSVPs)* (rejected — additive capability without the surface's validation path; lands with convergence per table). *A count-based admin-client ratchet* (rejected — a stable total hides swapping one bypass for another; per-file is reviewable). *Join-based policies for the no-space_id stragglers (`space_availability_overrides`, `space_venue_holds`, `space_collaborations`)* (deferred — follow-up, not blocker; they remain deny-all and listed).

**Consequences.** Applied to production 2026-08-03 and verified: all 26 tables report the intended policy counts, security advisors show no new findings (the deny-all INFO class shrank by 26), and service-role paths are untouched, so no app behavior changes. The ADR-921 platform gate "tenancy walls verified in prod" is satisfied structurally; the pgTAP matrix is the behavioral half and runs in `db-tests` (manual dispatch). ⚠️ The prod-applied copies use compact do-block generators; the repo files carry the identical policies as literal statements so `check:rls` can see them — predicate drift between the two is impossible to introduce silently because the repo file is the replay source. ⚠️ Staff read arms use `get_my_web_role() in ('admin','janitor')` matching the CRM precedent; `client_notes`-style personal-data tables keep no staff arm.

The durable rule: **a wall the database cannot prove is a guard, not a wall — and every new RLS bypass is a visible, reviewable act, never a default.**

## ADR-924 — The 2026-08-03 DAWN sync round: neutral lift, chrome band adopted, rank spectrum locked, one tab vocabulary (2026-08-03)

**Status.** Accepted. The first inbound design round from the DAWN system (Claude Design), applied per `design_handoff/SYNC.md` on `design-sync/2026-08-03` (PR #2011), with four owner rulings taken the same day.

**Context.** DAWN adopted the full production style sync (HANDOFF-TO-DAWN-2026-08-03) and pushed back one value set: the neutral field read too tan and the app frame too white. Its CHANGES.md also carried the Quest-icon finish, the completion-ladder color mapping, an AA contrast fix, a marketing spacing correction, four bugs to check for, and five kit primitives specced against BRIEF-06.

**Decision.** (1) The neutral lift lands value-for-value in `app/globals.css` (canvas, marketing canvas, elevated/post surfaces, both borders) plus the new `--color-chrome`/`--color-chrome-border` pair in all four render states; **owner adopted the chrome band on the app top bar** (`bg-chrome` + `border-chrome-border`, blur kept). (2) The season-ladder spectrum is locked to **stone / clay / gold / jade** in the single binding point `lib/season-ranks.ts`; ladder names were already canon. (3) **Owner ruling on naming: ADR-868 stands** — Marketplace is the full system, Market is the surface where member Spaces sell goods and services (where the take rate matters); DAWN relabels its rail recreation back to "Marketplace" next round. (4) **Owner ruling on tabs: UnderlineTabs is the one tab vocabulary, consoles included** — the four ADR-828 pill manage consoles adopt it in the fabric-phase sweep via `activeHref`; the pill convention is superseded. (5) The five DAWN kit primitives land as `components/ui/` (Counter/CounterRow, StreakMeter, Meter, GateNotice, ProgressTrack — the last was entirely missing against ~30 ad-hoc bars); adoption sweeps stay with the fabric phase. (6) The marketing `Section` default padding moves to the `.mk-section` var rule (a section followed by another gives up a third of its bottom padding); the rail toggles become borderless foot glyphs; the marketing header's over-hero state gains the top scrim; the reveal-observer skip-past bug (real in `components/marketing/motion.tsx`) is fixed.

**Alternatives considered.** *Applying DAWN's `can_view_space_content`-style commented specs verbatim* (rejected where wrong — this round's `app_instances` lesson repeated: DAWN's rail recreation had also invented an opaque panel production never had; production stays the source of truth for structure). *Renaming the rail row to "Market" per brief 02* (rejected by owner ruling — Marketplace is the system name). *Adopting the full four-role marketing spacing system from prose* (deferred — the role classes' tuned values live in DAWN's `tokens/spacing.css`, which arrives with the full project export; only the stated double-count correction landed).

**Consequences.** The lighter canvas + chrome frame changes every app page's first impression; the Playwright visual-snapshot harness (#2005) should re-baseline after merge. `text-subtle` remains failing AA at small sizes anywhere outside the swept rail chrome — the P8 dark/a11y pass owns the site-wide sweep. ⚠️ The DAWN 2 rounds (docks, screens, marketing rebuilds, pricing page, Lab vision, wizard) are gated on the full project export reaching the repo. ⚠️ Brief 02's naming deltas are NOT canon where they conflict with NAMING.md — the naming canon wins on names, and DAWN inherits corrections, not the reverse.

The durable rule: **design rounds are applied through the repo's conventions and canons, never pasted — and where a design doc and production disagree about what exists, production is the witness.**

## ADR-925 — The eight UX maturity lifts become phased, gated workstreams (2026-08-04)

**Status.** Accepted. Owner directive on the 2026-08-04 rebuild grading: "build these 8 recommends into the next phases. Go deep into each and make sure it's fully mature."

**Context.** The rebuild graded 74/100 against a best-in-class bar: token architecture and design ops in the 90s, screen craft mid-migration (65), accessibility spot-fixed (60), mobile inherited rather than designed (55), and no user evidence anywhere in the design loop (40). Eight improvement recommendations came out of the grading; unphased recommendations decay into sentiment.

**Decision.** The eight lifts are specced as full workstreams in [`docs/UX-MATURITY-PLAN.md`](UX-MATURITY-PLAN.md), each with a definition of done, machine enforcement in the house gate pattern, a moving metric, and named owner actions: (1) the user-evidence loop (journey registry + quarterly moderated tests + findings feeding the DAWN round), (2) adoption-debt ratchets (`check:adoption` baselines that only shrink, generalizing the admin-client ratchet), (3) accessibility as blocking gates (token-pair contrast validation across all four render states, axe-core in e2e, focus/reduced-motion audits), (4) a mobile grammar decided once via BRIEF-07 to DAWN with a standing every-pass mobile statement rule, (5) one render path per marketing route (block parity → template regeneration → coded-body retirement held by `check:render-path`), (6) visual regression at real surface area (~120 captures across four render states, auto-compare on styling PRs), (7) per-template vitals budgets read in every DAWN round with a breach protocol, (8) an interaction-state contract with a kit sweep and a `check:elements` extension. Sequencing interleaves the lifts into the existing waves rather than adding a track.

**Alternatives considered.** *A dedicated "quality phase" after the remodel* (rejected — quality phases scheduled after feature work are the work most often cut; mounting the lifts onto running waves makes them un-cuttable). *Advisory-only gates* (rejected except research freshness, the one cadence a build cannot honestly block on — every other lift gets a blocking check because the repo's own history shows advisory counts drift).

**Consequences.** The near-term wave order in UX-MATURITY-PLAN §Sequencing supersedes the informal "next screens" queue. ⚠️ Four items are owner-gated and listed there: research recruiting, the seeded snapshot account, flipping new checks to required, the Auth leaked-password toggle. ⚠️ The vitals beacon gains a `viewport_class` field — account-free, so ADR-922's consent posture is unchanged.

The durable rule: **a quality bar without a gate is a wish, and a gate without a number is a ritual — every lift ships with both.**

## ADR-926 — The DAWN 2 marketing block set: the rebuilt screens become editor blocks, and plan bands bind live pricing (2026-08-04)

**Status.** Accepted. Owner directive: "All marketing pages should be Puck editor with our custom blocks. Edit any custom blocks to look like the styles from Claude Design."

**Context.** The DAWN 2 screen passes rebuilt `/about` (6395fe4), `/the-lab` (329cc4f), and `/pricing` (32c7a09) as coded pages, but the marketing routes render preferentially from their page-editor templates (published → template → legacy), so the rebuilds were invisible: the templates still composed the pre-DAWN block sequences. Meanwhile the block library itself predated the DAWN alignment (raw `white/N` on-ink literals, literal `rounded-2xl`, no fact dock, no PhotoBeat/PhotoTrio/ink-principles grammar), and the pricing page had ADR-918's live-price binding only on the old `Tiers` cards, not the DAWN two-band plan layout.

**Decision.** (1) A new general-purpose block module `components/page-editor/blocks/dawn.tsx` wraps the marketing kit rather than duplicating it: `PhotoBeat`, `PhotoTrio` (arc shoulder + dot-grid options), `StoryBeats` (rule-amber ruled prose), `ValueBand` (ink principles with the sheen cards), `BuildTimeline` (numbered/dated milestone cards, chosen-card highlight), `PhotoCardRow` (numbered photo panels with the honesty overline), `PlanBand`, and `PillarNav`. (2) The fact dock lands on the EXISTING `Hero` key as an additive `facts` array (stored docs unaffected), not a new hero block. (3) `PlanBand` extends the ADR-918 rule to the DAWN two-band layout: every card can bind a `livePriceKey`; figures resolve from `metadata.live.pricing` (now carrying `monthlyCents`) and the typed text is only the fail-safe; Product/Offer JSON-LD can be emitted from the resolved live figures, **opt-in and off by default** because `/pricing` hoists page-level price schema on both branches. (4) The `about` and `the-lab` templates are regenerated to the same structure and copy as the rebuilt coded pages; the `pricing` template is deliberately NOT regenerated (a full Publish freezes figures — partial-conversion pattern, per ADR-916/918). (5) The whole block library is restyled to DAWN: `white/N` → `on-ink/N` tokens, `rounded-lg/2xl` card literals → `rounded-control`/`rounded-card` roles (identical at baseline, theme-aware under ADR-578), `Divider` gains a `rule-amber` style.

**Alternatives considered.** *A new `DawnFactHero` block* (rejected — the Hero key is already stored in published docs; a new key forces re-authoring). *Regenerating the pricing template to the two-band DAWN structure* (rejected this round — a static template that types dollar figures re-forks the price source the value-ladder work unified; the PlanBand binding is the conversion path instead). *Page-specific blocks (AboutStory, LabRooms)* (rejected — blocks are generic with copy defaults drawn from the coded pages, so the remaining marketing pages template without new block work).

**Consequences.** The DAWN rebuilds are now live through the template rung with no DB publish. Existing published docs keep rendering (all prop changes additive; restyle only changes emitted classes). `lib/page-editor/templates/templates.test.ts` guards every registered template against unknown block types; `dawn.blocks.test.ts` locks the new schemas and the PlanBand binding. ⚠️ The plan-card lockup in `PlanBand` mirrors the page-local card on the coded `/pricing`; when a third surface needs it, promote it into `marketing-ui.tsx` and re-point both. ⚠️ A `DawnHowToSteps` block emitting HowTo JSON-LD is the wave-2 shape for the seeker articles: same contract as `PlanBand`'s opt-in schema (steps array → HowTo nodes, off by default where the page already emits).

The durable rule: **a design rebuild is not shipped until the highest-precedence render path expresses it — and a CMS block never stores a number the product derives.**
